title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an enthusiastic salaried general practitioner to join our friendly, caring and innovative general practice team.

Honeypot Medical Centre is a forward-looking, innovative GMS general practice, serving a population of approx. 19,000 patients.

We believe in retaining the traditional values of general practice, including a strong patient-centred ethos, while embracing innovation and technology to provide a general practice fit for the future.

We embrace skill-mix with an extensive team, including GPs, advanced nurse practitioners, practice nurses, pharmacists, first contact physiotherapists, paramedic, physician associate, social prescribing link workers and health care assistants. We are a training practice approved to train GP registrars, F2 doctors and medical students and are committed to training the future generation of doctors and GPs. We are an integral member of our Primary Care Network and our Senior Partner is the Clinical Director. We have newly built modern, attractive premises and our own staff car park. We have an additional branch site just 200 yards away.

title: Paramedic
descriptionHtml:
We are offering an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic and keen Paramedic to join our experienced and friendly team in an urgent care role.

We are a 3 partner, 8000 patient practice in semi-rural Sussex, uniquely located in Uckfield Community Hospital.

We encourage personal development and sharing clinical experience.

The role will involve working alongside our GP's, existing paramedic and advanced nurse practitioner and involves coordination of care by telephone triage, delivering urgent and emergency care to patients in surgery and during home visits. The ideal candidates would be able to work as an autonomous practitioner and have minor illness and minor injury qualifications. Existing experience in primary care and a prescribing qualification are desirable but not essential.

We are an expanding surgery, offering several additional support roles, including pharmacy technician, Care CoOrdinators, First Contact Physio and Social Prescriber.

We value everyone's opinion and suggestions and also the importance of a stable work/life balance.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are currently recruiting for Salaried GPs to join our growing medical team. We are ideally looking for GPs looking for more substantive appointments of between 4 and 6 sessions per week and have vacancies at our St Marys and Telephone house sites from January 2027 and at our Mulberry House site from February 2027.

The job plan for the role will include mixed clinical duties including list-holding and supporting continuity of care (through working in a small locally focussed micro-team), triage, mixed routine & on-day clinics, occasional duty clinics and clinical admin.

All salaried GPs are provided with a clinical partner mentor and a tailored induction programme. We are a training practice and have extensive experience of supporting newly qualified GPs into salaried roles, as well as providing opportunities for more established GPs to develop additional roles and interests. Terms and conditions are aligned with BMA recommended arrangements.

Southampton Sea City Partnership was formed in April 2025 through the merger of St Mary and Victor Street partnerships. We are proud to serve some of the most vibrant and diverse communities in the South of England. Working for us you will have opportunities to develop your experience and clinical skills whilst at the same time making a real difference in peoples lives.

We are a progressive organisation and have exciting plans for developing sustainable, high quality modern general practice. Last year we implemented a new clinical model with improved access and triage arrangements (supported by ANIMA), together with a strong emphasis on continuity and neighbourhood delivery, ensuring patients with more complex needs have continuity of care with a clinician they know and trust. We are a well led organisation which has good links within our local health system and beyond. We offer work in a positive and collegiate team and are committed to staff wellbeing and development. We have recently formed a new PCN and multi-neigbourhood collaboration arrangements with two other practices serving a total of circa 120k patients and are excited about the opportunities this will bring for sharing learning and working at scale when it suits (e.g. delivery of GPSI services).

employer: Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
title: Adult Forensic Consultant
descriptionHtml:
The Adult Forensic Service at Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust has an existing opportunity for a Consultant Forensic Psychiatrists to be a crucial part in helping drive improvements to our patients' experiences and in helping contribute to the development of our new model of care.

While our new model of care is under development, and definitive medical job planning is under review, it is anticipated that the post holders will be the Responsible Clinician for 12 - 16 male inpatients or 10 - 12 female inpatients, following their caseload from admission to discharge.

We would welcome further discussions with those interested and look forward to hearing from you.

This is an exciting time to join us as Consultant (Forensic) Psychiatrist. This opportunity could be for a full-time post within either our women's blended secure service (WBS) or our male medium secure service. Either role would allow a successful candidate to contribute to the development of our new model of care and to shape the future of secure services for women and men from Greater Manchester.

You will be supported by a full and expanding complement of multidisciplinary colleagues, with the current position being that you will work with a medical secretary, junior doctor(s), clinical psychologist, social worker, occupational therapist, and our nursing colleagues. To support our service user's physical health, there is additionally a visiting GP, dentist, and well-established physical health team.

Alongside inpatient management, additional clinical activities include on-call work, access assessments to the service, and a range of additional activities dependent on negotiation with consultant colleagues and our new model of care.

Greater Manchester Mental Health (GMMH) Foundation Trust employs over7000members of staff, who deliver services from more than160locations.

We provide inpatient and community-based mental health care for people living in Bolton, the city of Manchester, Salford,Trafford and the borough of Wigan, and a wide range of specialist mental health and substance misuse services across Greater Manchester, the north west of England and beyond.

Greater Manchester is one of the world's most innovative, original and exciting places to live and work. From the beauty of the surrounding countryside to the heart of the vibrant inner city with great shopping, entertainment and dining options.

Wherever you go you will experience a great northern welcome with people famed for their warmth, humour and generosity.

Our people enjoy their work, have opportunities to learn and develop their skills and are encouraged to generate new ideas that improve care for our service users.

title: Consultant Gastroenterologist
descriptionHtml:
UNLOCK YOUR BEST WORK LIFE

+ make a difference for every patient

We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced Consultant Gastroenterologist to join our high-performing team at Practice Plus Group Hospital, Shepton Mallet. Youll play a key role in delivering high-quality endoscopy services, supporting both NHS and private patients, and helping us continue to build an exceptional reputation for safe, patient-centred care.

This is your chance to work in a centre of excellence where youll deliver diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopy services, including upper and lower GI endoscopy, in a state-of-the-art, patient-focused environment.

This is a full-time position (40 hours per week), but we are also open to part-time arrangements (2030 hours per week over 23 days) to support flexible working.

Youll be joining a collaborative, forward-thinking environment where innovation and teamwork are at the heart of everything we do.

As our Consultant Gastroenterologist, you will:

  • Deliver diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopy procedures, including upper and lower GI work.
  • Conduct outpatient gastroenterology clinics, providing expert advice and continuity of care.
  • Work closely with a multidisciplinary team to enhance patient pathways and clinical quality.
  • Maintain compliance with JAG standards and participate in ongoing clinical governance, audit, and quality improvement initiatives.
  • Contribute to the training and development of colleagues and the wider endoscopy team.
  • Participate in local and national endoscopy forums to help shape service delivery and excellence across the organisation.

Were seeking a motivated and collaborative clinician who shares our commitment to quality, safety, and outstanding patient experience. Youll bring:

  • Full GMC registration with a licence to practise
  • JAG accreditation for independent upper and/or lower GI endoscopy practice
  • Demonstrable competence aligned to GRS and JAG KPIs (e.g., colonoscopy completion rate >90%)
  • Substantial experience in treating gastrointestinal conditions in a specialist setting
  • A proactive, team-oriented approach, with a strong commitment to patient care and continuous improvement
  • Excellent communication and leadership skills with the ability to mentor and influence others
  • Commitment to CPD, clinical governance, and contributing to strategic improvement of services

Salary is competitive, but substantive employment only to be considered

Please ensure that your CV used in applying includes details of what interested you in the role as well as describing relevant experience within the past 3 years i.e., number of cases performed and outcomes from national database (when relevant).

In time consultants joining Practice Plus Group will be guided through the process to achieve accreditation with BUPA, applicants already with this accreditation are considered favourably and encouraged to highlight this in their application.

title: Consultant Gynaecologist - Part Time
descriptionHtml:
UNLOCK YOUR BEST WORK LIFE + make a difference for every patient   We are excited to offer a fantastic opportunity to join our multi-disciplinary medical team at our CQC "Good" rated Hospital in Shepton Mallet. Your expertise in non-Obstetric Gynaecology will be highly valued as a key member of our team.

As a Consultant at Practice Plus Group, you will have access to excellent facilities within a well-structured, yet relaxed environment. We provide high-quality day case and inpatient treatments across a wide range of specialties, ensuring exceptional clinical care for all patients.

Reporting to the Medical Director, you will be part of a multi-professional team and carry out various non-Obstetric Gynaecological procedures.

You will treat both NHS and private patients referred to the hospital, adhering to protocols and working practices. This includes providing in-patient and out-patient care for patients with common gynaecological concerns such as menstrual disorders and urogynaecological issues.

As a UK registered medical professional listed on the Specialist GMC register, we expect your commitment to high standards of care to match ours.

Everything we do is focused on providing a high standard of safe and effective patient care. Our facilities are modern, employing the latest technology with friendly and professional staff. We have strong control processes to ensure we maintain high standards of hygiene and above all, were passionate about giving our patients the best possible care and helping them feel better, faster.  

Procedures include:

  • minor/intermediate procedures of the vagina, cervix, uterus, and fallopian tubes such as hysteroscopy, endometrial sampling, endometrial ablations, laparoscopy, tubal sterilizations, insertion/removal of MIRENAs etc
  • Major procedures to include Vaginal Hysterectomy, Colporrhaphy, abdominal hysterectomy, fascial sling etc
  • Skills in the management of endometriosis would be an advantage.
  • Skills to be able to do total laparoscopic hysterectomy, laparoscopic assisted vaginal hysterectomy, laparoscopic excision of endometriosis and hysteroscopic resection of fibroids would be an advantage.
What we are looking for:  
  • UK registerable Medical Degree
  • Strong background in laparoscopic surgery is essential
  • MRCOG or appropriate specialist qualification
  • Relevant CCT or equivalent
  • Past record of academic achievement
  • Full and Specialist GMC Registration in relevant speciality
We want our team members to feel motivated and rewarded.
  • Competitive salary - substantive employment only to be considered
  • Flexible shift patterns  -helping you fit your working life around your home life.
  • Private pension
  • 25 days annual leave (+ Bank holidays) increasing with long service
  • Continuous training and development -including 10 CPD days per year 
Please ensure that your CV used in applying includes details of what interested you in the role as well as describing relevant experience within the past 3 years i.e number of cases performed and outcomes from national database (when relevant).

In time consultants joining Practice Plus Group will be guided through the process to achieve accreditation with BUPA, applicants already with this accreditation are considered favourably and encouraged to highlight this in their application.

title: Second Opinion Appointed Doctors
descriptionHtml:
The Department of Health and Social Care (the Department) are currently seeking to add to the existing pool of Second Opinion Appointed Doctors (SOADs), with applications for the unique role being welcomed until 30 April 2026. If you are a qualified psychiatrist with at least 5 years practical experience at a senior level, then this could be an opportunity for you.The pool of SOADs registered with the Department are completely independent of local services and work as and when requested. This is generally between 4 to 6 times per year, usually for one day each time. However, you may need to see up to 3 patients per visit. The SOADs are called upon to provide second opinions for a patients treatment, where that patient is covered by the powers of the Act. The SOADs will report through the Head of Quality and Compliance at the Department of Health and Social Care.

Thepurpose of the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) is to ensure the provision of health and social care meets the needs of the Isle of Man. The Department supports health and social care delivery in the Island, making sure people have access to safe, effective and high-quality care. The DHSC does not directly provide any health and social care services. The delivery of NHS health and social care services to patients and service users are provided by Manx Care and its contracted service providers. Services are provided under a Mandate from the Department which is published annually.

employer: Avon & Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust
title: Consultant in General Adult Psychiatry- NW Intensive Service, Devizes
descriptionHtml:
The Trust is seeking a consultant psychiatrist to join the North Wiltshire Intensive Service. The post is vacant due to the post-holder leaving. The consultant will provide clinical advice and leadership in a number of settings and interactions throughout their working week rather than at designated times only in their weekly timetable. There are weekly case reviews where an MDT approach reviews more complex presentations. This facilitates team discussion and creation of a team formulation. The Service are currently advertising for a Speciality Doctor to support the consultant.

Provide clinical leadership and consultation for Intensive Team members, supporting them in providing home based care and facilitating safe and timely transitions for patients between Inpatient and community services.

  • Assess and treat patients referred to the Intensive Team advising on management plans through regular Team reviews and handovers and advice to Team members

. Work with colleagues in the Intensive and Inpatient services to lead the acute care pathway

  • Teach and supervise Medical Students.
  • Support and participate in Clinical Governance and Quality Improvement.
  • Comply with all Trust policies including Equal Opportunities and to promote equality of access to healthcare at all times.
  • The post holder will be encouraged to develop an area of special clinical interest in line with service needs. This may be practice-based research.
  • The Trust expects engagement in Continuing Professional Development (CPD) and, in view of this, appropriate study leave and expenses will be supported. CPD will include continued training to maintain the role of Educational supervisor for trainees.
  • The post holder will undertake administrative duties associated with the running of his/her clinical work.

We are AWP (Avon and Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust) a diverse organisation with over 5,000 dedicated staff providing inpatient and community-based mental health care. We provide services from a range of locations to approximately 1.8 million people living in Bath and North East Somerset (B&NES), Bristol, North Somerset, South Gloucestershire, Swindon, across the county of Wiltshire and in parts of Dorset.

Our outstanding people promote mental health and wellbeing. The expertise and resources within AWP are dedicated to a person-centred approach for those who use our services and for all employees. We recognise that happy and fulfilled employees give better care.

employer: Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist, CAMHS East Team (attracts £25K RRP)
descriptionHtml:
Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust is a General Medical Council (GMC) Sponsor Employer.

This job attracts a Recruitment and Retention payment of £25,000 in addition to £8000 relocation allowance. The RRP is pro rata for part time employees.

We are looking for an experienced and motivated Consultant Psychiatrist to join our Community Children and Young People Services (CYPS) team in East Surrey. You will play a key role in supporting the mental health and wellbeing of children and young people aged 5-18, working with a skilled multi-disciplinary team based across Leatherhead and Gatton Place, Redhill.

This is a great opportunity to provide clinical leadership and direct psychiatric care within a service that delivers early support and specialist interventions for young people experiencing mental health difficulties. Our team works closely with families, schools, social care, paediatrics, and voluntary sector partners to ensure joined-up, holistic care.

You will carry out assessments, provide diagnosis and treatment, and offer consultation and supervision to colleagues across the service. The role also involves contributing to service development, clinical governance, teaching, and quality improvement activities. You'll be supported by an experienced leadership team, administrative staff, and a Trust that values learning, wellbeing, and professional development.

You'll have the opportunity of working within a well-established and friendly team of highly skilled professionals who are passionate and committed to the care needs of our children and young people.

The postholder will offer outpatient clinics, hold a caseload and be required to do occasional home visits. You will liaise with primary care, be involved in referrals and new assessments.

The post holder will be working as part of a multidisciplinary team.

Our Offer:

  • NHS Consultant grade £113,565 - £150,569 per annum + £149 fringe + on- call requirement
  • GMC Sponsorship
  • Recruitment premia £25,000 *subject to policy requirements
  • Relocation allowance: up to £8000 *subject to policy requirement
  • Sponsorship for International candidates
  • Up to £2000/year CPD allowance *subject to policy requirements
  • NHS pension employers contribution 23.7% from day one
  • Company Car Lease Scheme
  • Discounted Nuffield Gym Membership and many more.

Please check our benefits here:Medical : Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust for other benefits.

Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust is the leading provider of health and social care services for people of all ages with mental ill-health and learning disabilities in Surrey and North East Hampshire. We also provide social care services for people with a learning disability in Croydon and ASD and ADHD assessment services in Hampshire.

We actively seek to engage people who use our services and our communities in improving the mental wellbeing of the local population. We work closely with other NHS and voluntary sector organisations who provide services and support people who use services and carers.

Surrey is a beautiful county lying just 30 minutes away from Central London and from the South Coast.

Our historic market towns and bustling districts are enveloped in wonderful countryside, and our excellent road and rail networks bring the rest of the country within easy reach.

For international travel, both Gatwick and Heathrow airports are nearby.

Please note that we reserve the right to close posts as soon as sufficient applications are received.

Working from home contracts do not attract high cost area payments.

We look forward to receiving your application!

employer: Hawkinge and Elham and Valley Practice
title: Salaried General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Join Us as a Salaried GP at Hawkinge and Elham Valley Practice

3 to 4 Sessions per Week

Are you looking for a role where you can make a real impact, work in a supportive team and enjoy the balance of rural and semi-rural general practice? At Hawkinge and Elham Valley Practice were excited to welcome a dedicated and forward-thinking Salaried GP to our team.

You'll be joining a progressive, training-focused practice that values innovation, teamwork and high-quality patient care. Whether you're an experienced GP or newly qualified, we offer a nurturing environment where you can thrive professionally and personally. With a strong multidisciplinary team, modern facilities and a genuine sense of community, this is a great opportunity to build your clinical portfolio and be part of shaping the future of general practice.

If you're passionate about delivering excellent care and want to feel truly supported in your role, wed love to hear from you.

  • Provide high-quality, patient-centred clinical care to our diverse population, including acute, chronic disease, and preventive care.

  • Undertake face-to-face, telephone, and online consultations as part of our total triage model.

  • Work collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team to ensure effective, holistic care.

  • Contribute to the continuity of care through personal list working where possible.

  • Participate in practice meetings, clinical audits, quality improvement initiatives, and significant event reviews.

  • Support and supervise trainees and students, depending on experience and interest.

  • Manage administrative tasks related to patient care, including referrals, pathology results, and correspondence.

  • Take part in duty doctor sessions on a shared rota basis.

  • Engage with practice development, innovation, and service improvement.

About Us Hawkinge and Elham Valley Practice

Hawkinge and Elham Valley Practice is a friendly and forward-thinking GP practice serving a patient population of over 10,000 across two sites in Hawkinge and Elham. We offer a full range of NHS General Medical Services and are proud to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care to our local communities.

Our multidisciplinary team includes GP Partners, Salaried GPs, a Nurse Practitioner, Practice Nurses, Healthcare Assistants, General Practice Assistant and Clinical Pharmacist. The clinical team is fully supported by an experienced and proactive management and administrative team.

We are a training practice involved in the development of Foundation Year 2 doctors, GP registrars, nurses, and medical students. With modern facilities, a supportive working environment and a strong team ethos, we offer an excellent place to work, learn, and develop your career in general practice.

employer: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board
title: Consultant in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a full-time Consultant in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery with a special interest in skin cancer management within Cardiff and Vale University Dental Hospital. The University Hospital of Wales is the first Major Trauma Centre to launch within Wales. The Major Trauma Centre is part of an inclusive and collaborative South West and Mid Wales Trauma Network spanning six Health Board areas.

The Board is seeking forward thinking surgeons who will develop a service, fit to care for the needs not only of the population of Cardiff and the Vale but with the skills and attributes to take the lead in skin cancer managment.

The OMFS posts will be based in the Head and Neck Directorate within the Surgery Clinical Board .

Cardiff and Vale University Health Board is recognised as a teaching centre of excellence in a wide range of clinical services.

Applicants should preferably either be on the Specialist Register or be a Specialist Registrar within six months of eligibility for inclusion.

You will be able to take advantage of the excellent Consultant contract for Wales.

A satisfactory disclosure check will be required of the successful candidates for these posts.

You will provide with consultant colleagues a service in the speciality to the hospitals so designated, with responsibility for the prevention,diagnosis and treatment of illness and promotion of health.

The work will be based at both University Hospital of Wales and the University Dental Hospital. You will be responsible for the professionalsupervision and management of junior medical / dental staff. If appropriate the post holder will be named in the contracts of junior staff as the person responsible for overseeing their training and as an initial source of advice to such doctors regarding their careers.The successful candidate will participate in a 1 in 6 Trauma on call rota .

You will be required to cover for consultant colleagues' periods of leave.

Cardiff and Vale University Health Boardis one of the largest Integrated Health Boards in the UK, employing over 15,000 staff, providing over 100 specialist services. Working across 6 hospital sites, we have a diverse range of career opportunities to offer. Serving around 500,000 people living in Cardiff and the Vale of Glamorgan, we are focussed on the health and care needs of our local population whilst working with our partners to develop regional services.

Our mission is"Caring for People, Keeping People Well",and ourvision is that every person's chance of leading a healthy life should be equal. As an organisation we are unashamedly ambitious for our population's health, rising to the challenges of today and tomorrow through our 10-year strategy, Shaping our Future Wellbeing. We are contributing to a healthier Wales with great emphasis placed on innovation and improvement, learning from around the world and leading the way in clinical research. Partnership working is strong at Cardiff and Vale, and we work closely with our staff and our community.

Cardiff, the thriving Welsh capital, is a fantastic city to live and work in with an abundance of sports, arts and cultural attractions. Situated to the west of Cardiff, the Vale of Glamorgan offers a combination of beautiful Welsh countryside and a dramatic natural coastline. Whether city life or rural living, Cardiffand the Vale offers the best of both worlds.

title: Consultant Gynaecologist - Nationwide
descriptionHtml:
Outpatient Network are looking for Consultant Gynaecologists with a special interest in General Gynaecology, Gynaecological Oncology and Urogynaecology for Nationwide services.

Main Duties of the Job

  • Deliver high-quality outpatient Gynaecology clinics within NHS insourcing services, assessing and managing patients across General Gynaecology, Gynaecological Oncology and/or Urogynaecology, depending on your specialist expertise.
  • Diagnose, investigate and formulate management plans for a wide range of benign and malignant gynaecological conditions in line with national and local guidelines.
  • Perform appropriate outpatient procedures and diagnostic assessments within your scope of practice.
  • Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, including specialist nurses, allied health professionals, radiology, pathology and other clinical specialties, to ensure seamless patient care.
  • Support elective recovery programmes by delivering safe, efficient and patient-centred outpatient services while maintaining high clinical standards.
  • Complete accurate clinical documentation, coding and outcome letters, ensuring all records meet NHS governance and information governance requirements.
  • Contribute to clinical governance, audit, quality improvement and patient safety initiatives, maintaining compliance with GMC standards and Trust policies.

Overview of the Organisation

Outpatient Network is a leading CQC-registered provider of NHS insourcing services, partnering with NHS Trusts across the UK to deliver high-quality elective care solutions. We support Trusts in reducing waiting lists, improving patient access to care and achieving national performance targets by providing experienced clinical teams across a wide range of specialties.

Our services are underpinned by robust clinical governance, operational excellence and a commitment to delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care. Working with Outpatient Network offers clinicians the opportunity to support NHS elective recovery programmes through flexible sessional work, backed by a dedicated operational and clinical support team.

employer: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Neurology
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an enthusiastic and forward-thinking Consultant Neurologist to join our well-established Neurology Directorate at Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. This is an excellent opportunity to work within a regional tertiary neurosciences service, supporting patients across Lancashire and South Cumbria while developing your clinical, teaching, leadership and research interests.

Our Neurology service provides specialist acute and outpatient care for a population of approximately 1.8 million people. You will join a supportive multidisciplinary team of consultant neurologists, neurophysiologists, neuroradiologists, neurorehabilitation consultants, specialist nurses, doctors in training and allied health professionals.

This post offers an attractive balance of outpatient neurology, inpatient input, multidisciplinary working, on-call participation, teaching and service development. We welcome applicants who are committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care and who want to contribute to the ongoing development of neurology services across the region.

The successful candidate will provide consultant-level neurology input across outpatient, inpatient and multidisciplinary settings. Clinical activity will include outpatient clinics at Lancashire Teaching Hospitals and, depending on service need, peripheral hospital sites. The final job plan will be agreed through the consultant job planning process.

Some of the duties will include:

  • Providing high-quality direct clinical care for neurology patients.
  • Contributing to multidisciplinary team working and support coordinated care across hospital and regional pathways.
  • Participating in the neurology on-call rota, currently operating on a week-on basis.
  • Support inpatient care and investigation through access to beds within the Regional Neuroscience Unit at Royal Preston Hospital.
  • Providing outpatient clinics at Royal Preston Hospital and other sites according to service need.
  • Contributing to audit, clinical governance, service improvement and patient safety activity.
  • Supporting undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, including supervision of doctors in training.
  • Maintaining professional development and participate in annual appraisal, revalidation and job planning.

Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is a major acute and specialist Trust in the North West, providing services from Royal Preston Hospital and Chorley and South Ribble Hospital. The Trust is the regional centre for a range of specialist services, including neurosciences, oncology, renal, vascular, plastics and major trauma.

The Neurosciences Centre at Royal Preston Hospital brings together neurology, neurosurgery, neurophysiology, neuroradiology, neuropathology and neurorehabilitation. The Neurology Directorate serves a broad and diverse population across Lancashire and South Cumbria and provides acute neurology, outpatient care and specialist support across multiple hospital sites.

We are proud of our commitment to education, research, innovation and excellent patient care. Neurosciences research is a priority clinical research theme for the Trust, and the department is actively involved in research and national and international programmes. There are opportunities for the successful candidate to contribute to research, education, leadership and service development.

Our values are centred on being caring and compassionate, recognising individuality, involving people in decisions, working together as one team and taking personal responsibility for delivering high standards of care.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Thank you for your interest in joining the team at Hamble Valley Health.

The Practice is committed to delivering high quality patient care which requires us to have a supportive and cohesive team.

We currently have 6 sessions available in our salaried GP team. The location will be across Hedge End Medical Centre, Blackthorn Health Centre, and Bursledon Surgery.

We offer Terms and Conditions equivalent to the BMA model contract. We are happy to consider newly qualified GPs as well as experienced GPs.

If you are looking for a new GP role, we very much look forward to receiving your application.

The Partners

Hamble Valley Health

This post has a base as their main site at Blackthorn Health Centre. On a rolling basis, you will also work in our Urgent Care Centre which is at Bursledon Surgery. This is on a fair share rota. In the same way, you will be our "operational director" around once every 3-4 weeks. This means you are the clinical lead for the urgent care centre in the practice. This requires a longer working day (8am to 6.30pm). Routine care is generally 13 appointments in the morning and 12 in the afternoon. Mornings are generally 8am-1pm, and afternoons 2pm-6pm. We are a single practice Primary Care Network. We have visiting paramedics, so apart from terminal care, visits are rare. You will be responsible for the prescriptions, pathology results and incoming correspondence for your list size. On average, you will manage around 40 prescriptions a week, 20 results a week, and 5 letters a week per session. We have robust processes in place to support prescribing and document workflow.

Blackthorn Health Centre and Hedge End Medical Centre have merged and are now known as Hamble Valley Health.

Our list size is over 37000, and our patients are mainly concentrated in Hamble, Bursledon, Hedge End and Botley. Our aim is to provide high quality, accessible medical care to our patients, whilst maintaining a supportive and pleasant working environment for clinicians and staff.

We are part of Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB, and offer General Medical Services to our patients.

We are a training practice, and take registrar doctors and also teach medical students from Southampton School of Medicine.

The practice has seven Partners. The current Partnership team is Dr Harris, Dr Cropley, Dr Graham, Dr Sonpal, Dr Shahsavanspour, Dr Yates and Dr McKenzie.

We employ fourteen salaried GPs, five Advanced Nurse Practitioners, a Nursing team of fifteen, and a reception/admin team of seventy.

The practice uses Emis as a clinical system. We are paper light, so scan all incoming correspondence onto patients medical records.

descriptionHtml:
Consultant Neurologist

We are seeking a dynamic and forward-thinking Consultant Neurologist to join our friendly and innovative Neurology team at Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust. Based at our new Midland Metropolitan University Hospital (MMUH), this is a fantastic opportunity to help shape and grow a high-quality, integrated neurology service within a single-site acute care model. You will work alongside an experienced and supportive team with a strong teaching, research, and sub-specialist focus. We welcome applicants with a general neurology background and a complementary subspecialty interest--particularly in epilepsy,.

Join us as we embark on the next chapter of our service, improving outcomes for a diverse and complex patient population of over 500,000.

The successful candidate will provide high-quality outpatient and inpatient neurological care at MMUH, contributing to the delivery and development of general and specialist neurology services. You will work closely with fellow consultants, nurse specialists, neurophysiology and stroke teams, as well as regional colleagues at the Queen Elizabeth Neurosciences Centre.

The role includes supporting specialist clinics, contributing to the neurology/stroke on-call rota, teaching undergraduates and trainees, and participating in audit, clinical governance, and research activities. There is no general internal medicine commitment.

Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust (SWB) serves Birmingham and the Black Country - one of the country's most culturally diverse areas. It's a friendly and welcoming place - a place where you can belong, and a place where you can grow.

We care for our patients, we care about our population, and we care about our people.

Our values - Ambition, Respect and Compassion - are at the heart of who we are. They guide us every step of the way; how we work with each other, and how we look after our patients and their families; how we respect and value the rich diversity of our team and our community.

Our Trust has always aspired to be more than a hospital, more than a healthcare provider. Our purpose is to "Improve the Life Chances and Health Outcomes of our Population." It is what inspires, drives, and unites us every day. It's what makes us unique.

We want working at SWB to feel like more than just a job. We want our Trust to be a place where you can feel you belong. A place where you feel happy, safe, and rewarded. A place where you can develop your career in whatever way you choose. When we say we're 'with you all the way' we want you to know that we mean it. Visit the SWB website to find out more about our ambitions and people plans.

title: Consultant - Respiratory Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Due to the expansion of our Respiratory Department, we are looking for a further Consultant to join our friendly team.

This is an exciting opportunity for you to use your skills and experience to further develop local services and deliver excellent care, whilst benefiting from the incredible lifestyle that Cornwall has to offer, in an organisation that values work/ life balance, with a job plan that enables you to make the most of living here.

All 10 PA job plans have 2.5 SPA as standard for new Consultants; 1.5 SPA for existing Consultants) to support professional development and quality improvement, with separate admin sessions. Additional SPA for educational, research or leadership activities are agreed in annual job plan reviews. Job plans are annualised, so that in non ward weeks, there is a day off and following the respiratory weekend on call (8am- 2pm), there are two days off. We have a generous study leave budget and study leave allowance.

We are a flexible team and although both posts are offered as substantive 10 PA jobs, we would encourage interested applicants to discuss less than full time working or fixed term appointments with us.

These roles would suit either an established Consultant looking to relocate and restore balance, or a new Consultant wanting to establish themselves in a supportive department.

This is a permanent consultant post. You must be on the specialist register or a pending a CCT date. Please check this via gmc-uk.org/doctors/ before applying as no specialist registration applications will be rejected.

The post-holders will be joining a team of seven consultant chest physicians & an associate specialist. The department has a growing complement of experienced specialist nurses, physiotherapists and a physiologist. Ward teams have a mix of trainees and recurring fellow posts & Cornwall benefits from a large pool of locums taking time out and making the most of living here. The department is based at the Royal Cornwall Hospital, in Truro, but there are opportunities to undertake community clinics throughout the county & we have a developing integrated respiratory care team.

Our main respiratory ward includes a 6 bed Higher Care Unit/ Acute Respiratory Unit, for enhanced respiratory support. We have been able to flex ward bases to accommodate covid & non -covid ARU areas when demand increases.

We offer a wide range of services including bronchoscopy, EBUS & pleural day-case clinics, with subspecialty services in lung cancer, TB, cystic fibrosis, sleep medicine, ILD, and respiratory failure including home ventilation. We have close links with Derriford hospital in Plymouth for severe asthma, Thoracic surgery and medical thoracoscopy.

We have a comprehensive mentoring programme for all new employees together with study leave and support for revalidation and CPD

Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust is the biggest provider of healthcare services in Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. Our three main sites are Royal Cornwall Hospital Truro, St Michael's Hospital Hayle and West Cornwall Hospital Penzance, our staff and services are available across the region.

The Trust employs 5,000+ staff, has a budget of £380 million and 750 beds. We work with health and social care organisations -including NHS Kernow and NHS England- to ensure local healthcare needs are met. We provide acute medical, surgical and specialist services to around 500,000- which can increase significantly during busy holiday periods.

The Trust has teaching hospitals status as part of the University of Exeter Medical School. Keeping at the forefront of medical advances, we continually develop clinical services and are committed to maximising the range of specialist care offered locally.

We can offer you a rewarding career in a supportive working environment. We have extensive educational links to help you realise your full potential and develop skills to provide outstanding healthcare to the local community.

Enjoy an outstanding quality of life in a place that offers surfing beaches and fishing harbours to beautiful countryside and historic towns. With clean air, plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities and excellent schools, colleges and universities (including adult education) it is the ideal place for families and for you to develop your own career.

title: Consultant in Upper GI Surgery
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic and forward-thinking Consultant Upper GI Surgeon to join our surgical team in Cornwall.

We are seeking a surgeon with a strong interest and experience in Upper GI surgery, ideally with a specialist interest in bariatric surgery and experience in robotic-assisted surgery. The successful candidate will join a supportive multidisciplinary team and contribute to the continued development of high-quality, patient-centred surgical services across Cornwall.

About you

We are looking for a Consultant who is:

  • Fully trained in Upper GI surgery and eligible for appointment at Consultant level.
  • Experienced in complex Upper GI surgery.
  • Ideally experienced in, or with a strong interest in, bariatric surgery.
  • Experienced in robotic surgery, or with demonstrable commitment to developing their robotic skills.
  • A strong team player with excellent communication and leadership skills.
  • Committed to clinical excellence, teaching, research and continuous service improvement.

The role

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to:

  • Deliver a high-quality elective and emergency Upper GI surgical service.
  • Develop and expand their specialist interest in bariatric surgery.
  • Undertake and develop robotic-assisted surgical procedures as part of our evolving minimally invasive surgery programme.
  • Work closely with gastroenterology, oncology, radiology, anaesthetics, dietetics and other members of the multidisciplinary team.
  • Contribute to service development, clinical governance, teaching and training.
  • Support the continued development of specialist Upper GI and bariatric pathways across Cornwall.

We are particularly interested in candidates who can bring robotic surgical expertise and enthusiasm for developing innovative, minimally invasive approaches to patient care.

Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust is the biggest provider of healthcare services in Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. Our three main sites are Royal Cornwall Hospital Truro, St Michael's Hospital Hayle and West Cornwall Hospital Penzance, our staff and services are available across the region.

RCHT employs 5,000+ staff, has a budget of £380 million and 658 beds.

This is a fantastic opportunity to combine an exciting consultant surgical career with an exceptional quality of life.

Cornwall offers a unique lifestyle, with stunning beaches, beautiful countryside and a relaxed coastal environment, while still providing excellent opportunities for professional development. Whether you enjoy surfing, sailing, walking, cycling, or simply making the most of the outdoors, Cornwall offers something very special.

You will be joining a friendly and supportive surgical community with the opportunity to make a genuine contribution to the development of specialist surgical services in the region.

If you are an ambitious Upper GI surgeon with an interest in bariatric and robotic surgery and would like to develop your career while enjoying everything Cornwall has to offer, we would be delighted to hear from you.

For further information or an informal discussion about the post, please contact the surgical team.

title: Senior Clinical Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an experienced and strategic clinical leader to join us as a Senior Clinical Pharmacist. This is a temporary senior leadership role with the potential to become permanent. You will be responsible for shaping our medicines optimisation strategy, strengthening clinical governance, and ensuring the highest standards of patient safety, quality, and regulatory compliance across our practice.

Working closely with the Partners and senior leadership team, you will lead our pharmacy and medicines management team, drive continuous improvement, and support the delivery of outstanding patient care.

The Senior Pharmacist will provide executive leadership for medicines optimisation, prescribing governance and clinical governance across the organisation. The role includes leading medicines-related audits and quality improvement programmes, overseeing patient safety and risk management systems, ensuring compliance with CQC and NHS regulatory requirements, and supporting the delivery of QOF and enhanced services.

The postholder will also lead and develop the pharmacy team, provide strategic assurance to the leadership team, and represent WellBN at PCN, ICB and wider NHS meetings.

WellBN is a progressive multi-site GP practice providing primary care across Brighton & Hove. We are committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred healthcare through clinical excellence, innovation and collaborative working.

Our teams work across multiple sites to provide accessible services for our diverse local communities. We value continuous improvement, strong governance and a supportive working environment where staff are encouraged to develop and contribute to the future of primary care.

title: Corneal Consultant
descriptionHtml:
Consultant in Cornea and External Eye Disease

The Bristol Eye Hospital (BEH) at Bristol NHS Foundation Trust (BFT) is looking to grow its talented team of consultants to drive an ambitious future vision of care across Bristol. See Yourself at Bristol Eye Hospital (subtitles) on Vimeo

Our hospitals are spread across Bristol and Weston, join us and you can enjoy the very best of both worlds; city living within a stone's throw of the countryside or beside the seaside, both with easy access to all that theSouth Westhas to offer.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust values all people as individuals. As an equal opportunities employer actively working towards a diverse workforce we aim to recruit andretaina workforce whichrepresentsthe rich diversity of the local population at all levels and are committed to designing our services around the needs of individual patients and those around them. Anonymous information will be used from your applicationin order toensurewe'remeeting our pledge.

title: Consultant Physician in Stroke Medicine
descriptionHtml:
We are committed to delivering excellent, evidence-based care and continuously improving services in line with national best practice. The successful candidate will join a motivated multidisciplinary team and have the opportunity to contribute significantly to the strategic direction of stroke services across the Island. The role offers a diverse and rewarding case mix, encompassing hyperacute, acute and rehabilitation stroke care, supported by regional neuroscience and thrombectomy centres on the mainland. Consultants have the opportunity to lead service improvement initiatives, participate in regional stroke networks, and contribute to education, research and quality improvement.

Make a visible and lasting difference to the health outcomes of the Island population. Performance and Patient Outcomes Stroke care is a priority for the Isle of Wight NHS Trust, and we are proud of the significant progress made in recent years through a relentless focus on quality improvement, multidisciplinary working and patient outcomes. Our stroke service has demonstrated sustained improvements in performance across the Sentinel Stroke National Audit Programme (SSNAP), reflecting the commitment and expertise of our clinical teams. We recognise SSNAP as more than a performance metric; it is a powerful driver of excellence.

As a member of the Wessex Integrated Stroke Delivery Network (ISDN), we benchmark our performance against some of the highest-performing stroke services in the country and actively participate in regional quality improvement programmes. This collaborative approach has enabled us to adopt best practice rapidly and ensure that patients on the Isle of Wight benefit from the same high standards of care available across the wider Wessex region. The successful candidate will join a service with a clear ambition to achieve and sustain high levels of SSNAP performance across all domains of stroke care. You will play a key leadership role in analysing performance data, identifying opportunities for improvement and implementing innovative solutions that further enhance patient outcomes and experience.

Why This Role is Different Unlike larger organisations where individual influence can be diluted, the very nature of the Isle of Wight NHS Trust means stroke consultants can have a direct impact on the entire patient pathway. From emergency assessment and hyperacute treatment through rehabilitation and community follow-up, consultants are able to drive improvements that translate rapidly into enhanced SSNAP performance and, most importantly, better outcomes for patients. Our ambition is simple: to become one of the highest-performing stroke services in the Wessex region, delivering outstanding SSNAP outcomes and exceptional patient-centred care. Working in partnership with Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust, regional neuroscience services and the Wessex Integrated Stroke Delivery Network, we are creating an increasingly integrated stroke model that combines local delivery with access to specialist expertise, innovation and clinical excellence. The successful candidate will play a key role in helping us realise this ambition

title: GP
descriptionHtml:
Part time flexible position for a salaried GP (2-6 sessions). This would suit someone looking for a portfolio career in general practice or to accomodate personal commitments.We are looking to appoint a GP who is enthusiastic, innovative and keen to play an active role in the development of the whole team and to take part in our exciting projects.

  • Clinical Duties - Telephone appointments and face to face appointments that result from SystemConnect triage, very occasional visits (paramedics do the vast majority of these), dealing with queries from patients o other health care professionals in the form of tasks, telephone calls, instant messages or direct conversation.
  • Salaried GP contained proportion of administration ffrom the registered patient list. (We do not have personal lists)
  • Total Triage sessions that are split between GPs across the week
  • Supporting paramedics and other clinicians in decision making and management.
  • Attending regular clinical meetings, Protected Learning Time sessions, monthly clinical supervision sessions.
  • Clinical lead role in an area of interest or expertise.

Orchard Surgery is a long established, friendly 9000 patient practice in the market town of Horsham, West Sussex. We are recruiting a salaried GP following a colleague's relocation.

We are a systmOne practice. Since adopting Total Triage in June 25, we have cut routine waits from 5 weeks to 2.5 weeks and see all urgent patients on the day. Our standard GP face to face appointment is 20 minutes, recognising the need to address increasing levels of medical and social complexity in our population.

We are educators of the whole multidisciplinary team, encouraging our staff to develop their skills and extend their roles.

We are leading the development of a Women's Health Hub for Horsham District neighbourhood, running PCN menopause group consultations, a community menopause cafe and information evenings. We are keen to innovate and took part in the NHSE Acceleration programme in 2022/23.

We are one of two practices in Park and Orchard PCN each with a co-clinical director. PCN staff include paramedics, a social prescriber, mental health practitioners, care coordinators, a first contact practitioner (physio), clinical pharmacists and pharm techs. In house remote clinical pharmacists provide medication reviews and we have a robust annual recall system for long-term conditions.

We are engaging in the development of the new Horsham Integrated neighbourhood Team, working with our community and statutory colleagues to improve patient care.

We are actively engaged with our PPG.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are a friendly, busy, dual-site practice serving 25,000 patients in Herne Bay on the beautiful north Kent coast. We have an exciting opportunity for a motivated and committed Salaried GP to join our supportive and well-organised team for between 4-6 sessions a week.

We are seeking an enthusiastic individual with a patient-focused approach and a commitment to delivering high-quality care. The ideal candidate will be flexible, proactive, and able to travel between our two sites.

The successful candidate will work as an autonomous practitioner, responsible for providing high-quality medical services to our practice population. This includes delivering an excellent standard of clinical care while complying with the GMS contract and adhering to GMC standards for good medical practice. The role may also involve a care home ward round.

The post-holder will contribute to the effective management of the practice, lead by example, and maintain a positive, collaborative working relationship with the multidisciplinary team.

At Park Surgery, we are committed to supporting you to be the best you can be, confident in your care and proud of the outcomes you achieve for your patients. We strive to create an environment where all staff feel motivated, valued, and engaged in the running of the practice.

Our vision is to be the practice where patients wish to register and staff want to work. Although we are currently rated as CQC Good, we are dedicated to continuous improvement and are always looking for ways to enhance the quality of care we provide.

Park Surgery has a strong reputation for GP, student, and nurse training. We are passionate about growing our own talent and fostering an environment of personal development and mutual learning.

Our partnership is led by five partners and supported by a highly experienced and comprehensive management team. We are an integral part of the Herne Bay Primary Care Network (PCN), working closely with our neighbouring practice to provide integrated, patient-centred care.

title: Consultant Gastroenterologist and BCSP Colonoscopist
descriptionHtml:
Are you considering your next career opportunity?

On the 30th June, we are hosting an open day at the CUMBERLAND INFIRMARY in Carlisle for Consultant posts in a number of specialties. Please use the following link for more information -https://www.ncic.nhs.uk/consultant-jobs

The Department of Gastroenterology in North Cumbria Hospitals is looking for an enthusiastic new colleague to join us on our journey to provide high quality endoscopy and gastroenterology for the future in an organisation committed to clinical leadership and medical education.

Bowel Cancer Screening has been provided at NCIC since 2008 as part of the Cumbria and Morecambe Bay Screening Service. We look to continue our quality service by recruiting an additional colonoscopist. You will join us at an exciting time following the opening of our new £15M, 5 room, State of the Art, JAG accredited Endoscopy Suite. A full range of diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, including ERCP, are available.

We are looking for committed Doctors to become an integral part of the GI team. The post holder will provide dedicated colonoscopic screening lists and together with their gastroenterology colleagues will contribute to inpatient and outpatient care.

The gastroenterology consultant team share the responsibility of "Consultant of the Week" on a rotational basis to cover the GI inpatient work and contribute to the GI bleed rota. The team is supported by deanery trainees, Trust doctors and specialist nurses.

The post holder may be expected to fulfil some of their clinical commitments on other sites in the Trust.

We are passionate about teaching, and you will be able to play your part in teaching the next generation of doctors, nurses and other allied health professionals. You will have the opportunity to provide endoscopy training locally and to contribute to NETA - The Northern Endoscopy Training Academy. You will be involved in the recruitment of junior staff and to supervise their education, appraisal, and study leave. We will support you in keeping up to date on educational developments. If you are a new consultant, you will be asked to enrol on an educational supervisor accredited course by our medical education department. We have a growing experience and have been at the forefront of teaching and implementation of Physician Associate and Advanced Clinical Practitioners.

At NCIC, we have an ambition to deliver outstanding healthcare services to the population of North Cumbria. The Trust is committed to creating a centre of excellence in providing rural and remote healthcare and provides a wide range of community and acute services throughout our county.

Our 5 key principles demonstrate our belief in the delivery of 'safe, high quality care every time':

  • Being a clinically led organisation
  • Quality and safety at the heart of our Trust
  • A positive patient experience every time
  • A great place to work
  • Managing our money well

As an organisation we are serious about supporting a diverse workforce that reflects our local community and are very much focused on being an inclusive and compassionate place to work.

Across the North East and North Cumbria we are working together to deliver our ambition to be the greenest region in England by 2030. All staff are expected to support sustainability.

title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
The post-holder will manage a caseload and deal with a wide range of health needs in a primary care setting, ensuring the highest standards of care for all registered and temporary patients. We would consider hybrid working and flexable working too.

Clinical responsibilities:

In accordance with the practice timetable, as agreed, the post-holder will make themselves available to undertake a variety of duties, including surgery consultations, telephone consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork and correspondence in a timely fashion

Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems, whether self-referred or referred from other health care workers within the organisation

Assessing the health care needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems

Screening patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness

Developing care plans for health in consultation with patients and in line with current practice disease management protocols

Providing counselling and health education

Admitting or discharging patients to and from the caseload and referring to other care providers as appropriate

Recording clear and contemporaneous consultation notes to agreed standards

Collecting data for audit purposes

title: Senior Care Assistant

employer: Avon & Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust
title: Consultant in General Adult Psychiatry - PCLS - Wiltshire
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a consultant psychiatrist to join the Primary Care Liaison Service in Wiltshire. The post is an established post which has become vacant due to the previous incumbent moving to another service within AWP. The post involves working as the Primary Care Liaison consultant for a single CMHT catchment are in North, West and East Wiltshire. The post is supported by a Specialty Doctor.

The consultant (post holder) will provide clinical leadership in the team, help triage referrals, assess patients and make recommendations on care, provide advice to colleagues on assessment and management, liaising and working closely with the Intensive Service, Community Mental Health Team and Primary Care. There is a weekly interface meeting which is attended by PCLS, CMHTs, Primary Care Psychology and North Wiltshire Intensive Service. The consultant will work closely with the PCLS Manager to ensure that a safe, efficient and high quality service is delivered by the Team. The Consultant will also provide clinical supervision and management supervision for doctors reporting to them.

The Consultant will deliver advice to service users including undertaking assessments, (jointly where required), making diagnoses, and determining the most appropriate service provision to meet identified needs, including brief interventions where required.

The Consultant will supervise any medical staff providing input in to the service.

  • To actively participate in clinical supervision.

Work collaboratively with the Recovery, Intensive and Inpatient Services to facilitate transitions through the care pathway according to the identified care cluster.

  • The Consultant is expected to contribute to the development of services in line with best practice and nationally accredited standards.
  • Responsible with the team members for the identification of appropriate care cluster and identifying service users who require access to specialist services
  • Understand and participate in the maintenance, monitoring and evaluation of service specific performance indicators and targets.

The Consultant is expected to respond to all Advice and Guidance requests within 3-5 working days in accordance with the new PCLS Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). The requestors will primarily be GP, ARRS' Workers, RMN's based in GP surgeries, and at times, although scarce, other medical specialists based in Acute and Community Hospitals

Training and supervision of junior medical staff

Medical and MDT teaching and supervision

Regular attendance at the PCLS Team MDT meetings.

Participate in QI

We are AWP (Avon and Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust) a diverse organisation with over 5,000 dedicated staff providing inpatient and community-based mental health care. title: Locum GP - Maternity Cover
descriptionHtml:
Alton Surgery is looking for a friendly and supportive Locum GP to cover 5 clinical sessions a week for a period of maternity leave for one of our partners, for a minimum of 14 weeks. The role will start mid January 2027.

We pride ourselves on being a kind and compassionate practice, serving our small rural population of 2700 patients. You will be joining a well-established multidisciplinary team who put patient centred care at the forefront of their work.

The GP is required to work as an autonomous practitioner, responsible for the provision of medical services to the practice population, delivering an excellent standard of clinical care.

Sessions are to be delivered as follows:

5 Clinical Sessions of 4hrs 10 minutes and an additional administrative time of 2hrs 20 minutes.

Monday 8.30 6.30

Tuesday 8.30 6.30

Wednesday or Friday 1 clinical session to be discussed with the applicant

We are a well-established training practice with resident doctors and GP trainees. We also regularly host Keele University medical student placements.

The practice uses EMIS Web and AccuRx to manage our appointment triages, along with Ardens to efficiently manage patient care and demand. We regularly have high achievement across QOF and QIF along with high levels of screening and immunisation uptake.

Our team consists of 2 GP partners, 1 Practice Nurse and 1 CSA along with an excellent team of dispensers, administrative staff and management.

Through the ARRS scheme we also have access to an expansive MDT including First Contact Physio, Clinical Pharmacist, Pharmacy Technician, Care Coordinator, Mental Health Practitioner, Counsellor, Health & Wellbeing Coach and a team of Social Prescribers.

We hold regular clinical meetings for all clinical members of staff to share ideas, best practice and support each other. We also hold regular meetings for the whole practice team to distribute information and encourage collaboration across the practice.

title: GP Partner
descriptionHtml:
Golden Valley Practice is a small, high-achieving rural dispensing practice caring for 5,800 patients in south-west Herefordshire. We are looking for an experienced GP to join us as a partner for 4 to 6 sessions per week and play a meaningful part in the future of the practice.

Continuity and relationship-based general practice remain central to how we work. We know our patients, often care for several generations of the same family, and believe there is real value in the personal general practice that comes from knowing both the patient and their wider circumstances.

We are looking for an experienced and clinically confident GP who shares those values and cares about the quality of service we provide. Someone with the maturity and sound judgement that partnership requires: kind, dependable, good with people and willing to get stuck in.

As a GP Partner, you will undertake the full range of general practice while sharing responsibility for the clinical, operational and financial success of the partnership.

Alongside your clinical work, you will contribute to the wider running and development of the practice, including clinical governance, quality and patient safety, workforce and service development, financial and strategic decision-making and the responsibilities associated with delivering our NHS contracts.

Partnership responsibilities will be shared according to the needs of the practice and the skills and interests of individual partners.

We work from our main surgery in Ewyas Harold and branch surgery in Peterchurch, covering the beautiful Golden Valley and surrounding countryside towards the Black Mountains. Our main surgery is approximately 25 minutes from Hereford and 20 minutes from Abergavenny.

Our size allows us to retain a strong emphasis on continuity of care, while dispensing is an important part of both the service we provide to our rural population and the financial strength of the practice.

We have excellent patient feedback and strong clinical performance. We have pharmacist and pharmacy technician support and work closely with our community nursing, palliative care and wider primary care colleagues.

We have worked hard to make the working life of a GP sustainable. Routine appointments are 15 minutes and clinical workload is capped at 25 patient contacts per day. We use GP Automate and our GP Assistant reviews the majority of incoming Docman correspondence so that only items requiring clinical input reach a GP.

We are a successful dispensing practice with strong clinical performance and very competitive partner remuneration. As the practice premises are not partner-owned, joining the partnership does not require the substantial property investment associated with many traditional GP partnerships. We offer six weeks' annual leave and one week's study leave pro rata, together with generous protected administrative time for partnership responsibilities.

title: Salaried General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Central Surgery is seeking a motivated and committed GP to join our large 2 site friendly but progressive practice. Located in the town of Barton-upon-Humber with a branch surgery in the village of Goxhill.

Our team consists of 5 partners, 4 salaried GP's, ANP's, ACP's, Practice Nurses, HCA's and a Pharmacist, along with supportive reception and admin teams. We are a proactive member of the North Care Network and have a further team of additional roles including First Contact Physiotherapists, Clinical Pharmacists, and Social Prescribing Link Workers.

The Surgery is committed to the ongoing development of all our staff and are proud to be a training practice to GP registrars and medical students, working with Hull and York Medical School.

We are looking for an enthusiastic GP to join our multi-disciplinary team; someone who will help deliver a high level of patient care and be a key member of staff, undertaking both clinical and educational duties.

We are happy to receive applications from both experienced and newly qualified GP's.

  • 6-8 Sessions
  • Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems, whether self-referred or referred from other health care workers within the organisation.
  • Assessing the health care needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems.
  • Screening patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness.
  • Admitting or discharging patients to and from the caseload and referring to other care providers as appropriate.
  • Compiling and issuing computer-generated acute and repeat prescriptions.
  • In general, the post-holder will be expected to undertake all the normal duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.

About Central Surgery

We are a large semi-rural dispensing practice, serving our local community, with approx 17000 patient.

Rated as good by the CQC, we consider our surgery to be a dynamic forward thinking practice, advancing in times of change.

Working with the PCN, we provide care aligned to both national and local enhanced services, achieving high results for both QOF and IIF.

title: Consultant in Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
Applications are warmly invited for the position of Substantive Consultant in Anaesthesia with a specialist interest in Obstetric Anaesthesia, to join our dynamic and thriving A.C.S.A. accredited anaesthetic department at the Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust.

We are looking for committed anaesthetists of proven ability who can contribute fully to both clinical and managerial roles within the department. Candidates should bring skills or knowledge that will enhance and expand the services already provided at the Royal United Hospital. An ability to embrace change and develop services for more effective care delivery will be considered an asset.

The appointee will work clinically at the RUH (Royal United Hospital) Combe Park site and at Sulis Hospital (owned by the RUH). This post is a standard 10PA contract. Comprising 8.5 PAs Direct Clinical Care (including on call) and 1.5PAs Supporting Professional Activities in line with the national Consultant contract.

The clinical work will include elective and emergency operating lists across a broad range of surgical specialties (except for cardiothoracic, neurosurgery, vascular, burns, transplant, and major trauma) plus pre-operative assessment and peri-operative care.

This job includes a specialist interest in Obstetric Anaesthesia. The maternity services at the RUH have been rated as Outstanding by the CQC in the last 2 assessments. An annual delivery rate of nearly 5000 births and Caesarean Birth rate of 40% are managed by close multidisciplinary working and a culture of continued improvement and development of services, of which anaesthesia is a key contributor. The teams work closely with the Local Maternity Service and are active participants in the regional maternity neonatal patient safety collaborative. The RUH maternity research team is very active in both local and national research

Applicants wishing to work less than full time, or in a flexible working pattern, are welcomed and will be fully considered.

We are proud to be part of BSW Hospitals Group - a formal partnership between the Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust, Great Western Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust and Salisbury NHS Foundation Trust. With a combined workforce of over 17, 600 colleagues, and budget of 1.6 billion the Group is united by a common purpose to deliver the best possible care to over 1 million people.

We are creating a health and care system that works with the people we care for, reducing the differences people currently face in access, experience and outcomes, improving the experience of our colleagues and tackling shared challenges like sustainability and finances. Every improvement we make across our Group will be guided by what creates the greatest benefit for our colleagues, our patients, our communities and our partners.

By working together, we make a real difference for our patients, each other, and our community. Every role matters in delivering the exceptional, person-centred care we're proud of.

title: Remote/Hybrid Clinical Prescribing Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:

This exciting new role provides the opportunity to work with the General Practice and alongside a team of pharmacists and pharmacy technicians to support the delivery of pharmacy services in general practice.

You will be part of a dynamic, forward-thinking, pharmacy team delivering medicines management across a PCN with the support of a named pharmacist.The team comprises a clinical pharmacist, pharmacy technicians, a Lead Pharmacist and GP clinical colleagues, providing appropriate clinical supervision, support and multidisciplinary working.

You will be responsible for the care management of patients with chronic diseases and undertake clinical medication reviews, responding to medication queries, signing prescriptions, and to proactively manage people with polypharmacy and multi-morbidities.

You will have the opportunity to attend meetings at practice, PCN, and ICB level, deliver training to practice and pharmacy team colleagues, mentor students and junior colleagues, and develop innovative services in response to local gaps in healthcare.

patients in GP practices

Reduce inappropriate polypharmacy and wasteful prescribing through clinical medication

review

Reconcile medicines following hospital discharge and work with patients and community

pharmacists to ensure patients receive the medicines they need post discharge.

Contribute to reductions in medicine related hospital admissions and readmissions by

supporting patients to get the best outcomes from their medicines and identifying and

addressing medicines related issues

between primary care professionals including the promotion of the repeat dispensing service

We are a busy multidisciplinary team comprising GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, pharmacists, mental health practitioners, physiotherapists and dedicated administrative and reception teams. We work closely with our local Primary Care Network and wider health and community services to provide joined-up care for our patients.

We embrace innovation and modern ways of working, including digital technology and AI-supported tools, to improve efficiency and support our clinicians and patients.

Our practice values are Excellence, Caring, Integrity and Teamwork. We believe in supporting our staff, encouraging professional development and creating a positive environment where everyone is valued and can make a difference.
