title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Salaried GP to join the friendly, experienced, and supportive clinical team at Springfields Medical Centre.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a well-established, forward-thinking GP training practice dedicated to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care in a supportive environment that values the professional development and wellbeing of its clinical team.

The successful candidate will join us as a Salaried GP working 4sessions per week, with clinical responsibilities delivered through a combination of telephone and face-to-face consultations.

The successful candidate will undertake the full range of duties expected of a Salaried GP in accordance with the practice's contractual and enhanced service commitments.Responsibilities will include:

  • Conducting face-to-face and telephone consultations.
  • Providing home visits and visiting patients in residential and care home settings where clinically appropriate.
  • Reviewing, authorising, and signing prescriptions.
  • Participating in the practice duty clinic on a shared rota.
  • Managing patient queries, clinical correspondence, referrals, results, and associated paperwork.
  • Completing clinical administration to support safe and effective patient care.
  • Working collaboratively with the wider multidisciplinary team to deliver high-quality, patient-centred services and contribute to the ongoing development of the practice.

Springfields Medical Centre is a thriving, CQC-rated Excellent general practice serving approximately 8,700 patients in Warrington. We are committed to providing high-quality, compassionate, and patient-centred care, supported by a culture of teamwork, continuous learning, and innovation.

Our practice is led by a skilled multidisciplinary team comprising 3 GP Partners, 3 Salaried GPs, and 4 Practice Nurses. We work collaboratively to deliver safe, effective care while maintaining a friendly and supportive working environment where every team member is valued.

As an accredited GP Training Practice, we are passionate about developing the next generation of healthcare professionals. We provide training placements for GP Registrars creating an environment that encourages learning, mentorship, and professional development.

We work collaboratively with neighbouring practices through our Primary Care Network and the Warrington Innovation Network (WIN), sharing expertise, driving service innovation, and working together to improve health outcomes for our local community.

At Springfields Medical Centre, we believe that looking after our staff is fundamental to delivering outstanding patient care. We foster a positive and inclusive workplace where wellbeing, professional growth, and continuous improvement are actively encouraged, making our practice an excellent place to build a rewarding career.

title: Fixed Term Consultant in Acute Medicine
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for the post of a Fixed Term Acute Medical Consultant within an expanded assessment area medical team. This new model will involve working across existing assessment areas, including support of same day emergency care which has been facilitated with a brand new £2.4 million unit.

PREVIOUS APPLICANTS NEED NOT APPLY

title: Salaried GP  4-6 Sessions | Supportive Practice | Slough
descriptionHtml:
Bharani Medical Centre is seeking a confident and enthusiastic Salaried GP to join our established and supportive clinical team in Slough.

We care for approximately 18,000 patients across three nearby sites and offer a structured working environment supported by experienced GP partners and a comprehensive multidisciplinary team.

Our digital-first working model is designed to provide clinicians with a predictable and manageable workload while maintaining high standards of patient care.

We offer approximately 15 consultations per clinical session, dedicated administrative time, no traditional duty doctor rota and infrequent home visits. Working days can be agreed in advance, with 46 sessions available.

We are particularly interested in clinically confident GPs who can work independently and manage a broad range of presentations. Previous experience working in general practice following qualification would be advantageous.

Informal discussions via Microsoft Teams are warmly encouraged.

The successful candidate will provide comprehensive general medical services to registered patients, working independently while contributing to our multidisciplinary team.

Main responsibilities include:

  • Undertaking approximately 15 patient consultations per clinical session, predominantly telephone-first, with face-to-face assessments when clinically appropriate.
  • Assessing and managing acute presentations, chronic conditions and complex clinical problems.
  • Prescribing safely, requesting investigations, reviewing results and arranging appropriate referrals.
  • Managing clinical correspondence and associated tasks through Anima Documents, with dedicated administrative slots.
  • Managing occasional additional urgent appointments, including childhood emergencies, according to clinical need.
  • Undertaking home visits where appropriate, although these are infrequent.
  • Maintaining accurate clinical records using EMIS Web, Anima and Accurx.
  • Participating in clinical governance, quality improvement, safeguarding and continuing professional development.

Bharani Medical Centre is a well-established, GP-led practice providing NHS primary care to approximately 18,000 patients across three nearby sites in Slough.

Our experienced multidisciplinary team includes GP partners, salaried GPs, advanced nurse practitioners, clinical pharmacists, first-contact physiotherapists, practice nurses and administrative colleagues.

We pride ourselves on providing high-quality, patient-centred care within a friendly, supportive and collaborative working environment.

We have invested in digital systems, including EMIS Web, Anima and Accurx, to improve clinical efficiency, streamline administrative workflows and support sustainable working arrangements.

We recognise the importance of clinical independence, professional development and a healthy work-life balance. Our working arrangements are informed by BMA salaried GP guidance and recognised contractual standards.

We encourage open communication, shared learning and clinical innovation, while ensuring colleagues feel supported and valued.

We welcome clinicians who are confident, motivated and enthusiastic about contributing to a progressive general practice team.

title: Consultant in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry - North Somerset CAMHS
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic & dynamic Consultant Psychiatrist to join North Somerset CAMHS. This post offers an exciting opportunity to help shape & develop a well-established service within AWP CAMHS.

Based in the Core Community CAMHS Team, you will provide psychiatric assessment, consultation & treatment for children & young people with mental health needs. Working alongside experienced consultants & multidisciplinary colleagues, you will support therapeutic pathways including CBT, DBT, trauma-focused therapy/EMDR & family therapy.

The role combines direct clinical work with opportunities for service development & leadership. You will undertake psychiatric assessments and interventions, provide specialist consultation & formulation, and support multidisciplinary decision-making.

North Somerset CAMHS has approved Core and Higher Psychiatry Training placements, with opportunities for teaching and supervision.

As part of AWP CAMHS, the service is implementing the i-THRIVE model, offering opportunities to influence service transformation, develop specialist interests & contribute to innovative care.

You will join experienced consultants and a wider CAMHS network across Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire, including Learning Disability CAMHS, the Intensive Support and Hospital Assessment Team, and specialist services including Thinking Allowed, Be Safe and the Young People's Substance Misuse Team.

Full time/Part-time applications welcomed.

Clinical Responsibilities

This is an exciting opportunity to join a multidisciplinary CAMHS team, providing specialist assessment, diagnosis, management and treatment for children, young people & families experiencing severe & complex mental health difficulties.

Clinical Activity

You will undertake psychiatric assessments, provide clinical reviews & contribute to effective treatment planning. The role includes offering specialist consultation and advice to colleagues and partner agencies, working closely with education, social care, primary care & other services to support positive outcomes for young people.

You will provide expert psychiatric input across a varied caseload, including medication management, mental state monitoring, formulation and joint working with care coordinators and multidisciplinary colleagues. There will also be involvement in urgent clinical work where required.

Leadership and Service Development

As a senior clinician, you will provide clinical leadership within the multidisciplinary team, supporting high standards of care and contributing to service development and quality improvement. Working alongside senior clinical and operational colleagues, you will help shape responsive, evidence-based services for the local population.

Special Interests

The post offers opportunities to develop specialist clinical interests aligned with service priorities and local needs, supporting both professional development and the ongoing enhancement of CAMHS provision.

We are AWP (Avon and Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust) a diverse organisation with over 5,000 dedicated staff providing inpatient and community-based mental health care. We provide services from a range of locations to approximately 1.8 million people living in Bath and North East Somerset (B&NES), Bristol, North Somerset, South Gloucestershire, Swindon, across the county of Wiltshire and in parts of Dorset. Our outstanding people promote mental health and wellbeing. The expertise and resources within AWP are dedicated to a person-centred approach for those who use our services and for all employees. We recognise that happy and fulfilled employees give better care.

Please note that Avon & Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust is not currently a sponsor under the GMC Sponsorship Scheme. As a result, we regret to inform you that we are unable to consider applications from individuals who require GMC sponsorship.

descriptionHtml:

The role requires experience in genital dermatology, including the assessment and management of complex genital skin conditions and competence in performing genital skin biopsies.

The successful candidate will provide clinical leadership, supervise and educate junior medical and nursing staff, and contribute to a positive multidisciplinary learning environment.

They will lead research, audit and quality improvement activities, helping to expand the department's research portfolio, develop collaborative projects, present findings at regional and national meetings, and contribute to peer-reviewed publications.

We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Consultant in Sexual Health and HIV to join the Barking Integrated Sexual Health and HIV Service.

The successful candidate will provide consultant leadership in delivering high-quality, integrated Sexual Health and HIV care, managing complex cases, providing expert clinical advice, supporting multidisciplinary working, and supervising and teaching junior staff.

The role includes leading service development, clinical governance, audit and research, with opportunities to expand the department's research portfolio and drive innovation.

The post holder will also provide specialist genital dermatology services, including the assessment and management of complex genital dermatoses and performing genital skin biopsies.

Applicants should demonstrate specialist expertise, excellent clinical judgement, leadership, communication skills, and a commitment to patient-centred care and continuous service improvement.

We're an organisation that is getting better and better and our improvements are driven by a determination to deliver care we're proud of and our patients are happy with.

They are benefitting from a new electronic patient record (we were the last acute trust in London to introduce one) and our maternity services have been rated good by the Care Quality Commission.

We operate from two main sites - KGH in Goodmayes and Queen's Hospital in Romford. We have two busy emergency departments with more than 346,000 people visiting them last year. We're campaigning to secure the £35m we need to transform the A&E at Queen's and get rid of corridor care.

We're proud of our regional Neurosciences Centre, Radiotherapy Centre and Hyper Acute Stroke Unit. We're also part of the North East London Cancer Alliance.

We run a Women's Health Hub in Ilford; an Ageing Well Centre in Hornchurch; and Community Diagnostic Centres (CDC) at Barking Community Hospital and at St George's Health and Wellbeing Hub. These CDCs are open 12 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The majority of our 8,400 staff - who come from 146 different countries - live in the three diverse London boroughs we serve and are from black, Asian and minority ethnic groups. Many can work flexibly and more than 400 of them are on our Ofsted accredited apprenticeship programmes. We're proud to be a London Living Wage employer.

The post holder will work closely with GPs and the wider multidisciplinary team to support safe, effective, and evidence-based prescribing. Innovative ideas are welcomed, and excellent communication skills, enthusiasm and motivation are essential skills for a successful candidate.

The role will primarily involve:

  • Conducting structured medication reviews, including for patients with polypharmacy
  • Undertaking clinical communication reviews to support safe prescribing and continuity of care
  • Managing hypertension and lipid reviews in line with local and national guidelines
  • Supporting medicines optimisation and improving patient outcomes
  • Providing advice and support to patients and clinical staff regarding medicines use

In addition, the post holder will be responsible for encouraging the development of better understanding of the principles of medicines optimisation throughout the practice teams and promoting good practice in line with therapeutic developments. This will involve assisting the Practices in achieving national requirements, NICE implementation and utilisation of medicines optimisation initiatives.

We are a long-established practice based in the small market town of Chester le Street. We have a growing patient population, currently at approx. 12,700 and we have a sister practice in Coxhoe with approx. 7,100 patients. There are 8 GP Partners, 1 non clinical Partner/Practice Manager, 6 Salaried GP's, 5 Nurse Practitioners, a large admin/reception team and a variety of ARRS funded staff. All staff are committed to delivering high-quality, patient centered care. We pride ourselves on our collaborative team culture and continuous learning. The practice works closely with the wider Primary Care Network and offers a supportive environment for all staff to develop and utilise their skills.

employer: James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Haematologist
descriptionHtml:
James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (JPUH) is seeking to appoint an enthusiastic and motivated Consultant Haematologist to join our established and supportive Haematology team.

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a high-quality, patient-focused service within a rapidly developing Trust that is committed to innovation, clinical excellence, education, and research. We are looking for a consultant who shares our values and is passionate about delivering outstanding care to patients across Norfolk and Waveney.

Located on the beautiful east coast of Norfolk, the Trust offers an excellent work-life balance, access to stunning coastal scenery, and strong regional links with specialist centres including Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital and Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge.

This is asubstantive 1.0 WTE Consultant Haematologist post comprising 10 Programmed Activities (PAs), based at James Paget University Hospital.

  • Full-time position working Monday to Friday
  • 10 PA contract in the first instance
  • Additional PAs may be available by mutual agreement
  • Participation in the consultant on-call rota, currently 1:5, with prospective cover arrangements
  • Out-of-hours on-call commitment covering periods outside Monday to Friday, 09:00-17:00

The final job plan will be agreed with the Clinical Lead within three months of appointment, taking into account the successful candidate's experience, specialist interests, and service requirements.

The Haematology Department provides a Level 2B BCSH-compliant service and delivers comprehensive care across a wide range of malignant and non-malignant haematological conditions.

The department is actively involved in National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) and cancer research studies, supported by a dedicated Clinical Trials team and specialist research nursing support.

Multidisciplinary Working

The service maintains strong regional partnerships through:

  • Twice-weekly MDT meetings with Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital
  • Monthly specialist MDT teleconferences with Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge
  • Close collaborative working for autologous and allogeneic stem cell transplant pathways

The successful candidate will:

  • Deliver high-quality inpatient and outpatient haematology care.
  • Participate in the consultant on-call service.
  • Contribute to the development and delivery of malignant and non-malignant haematology services.
  • Provide specialist advice to hospital colleagues and primary care clinicians.
  • Participate in multidisciplinary team (MDT) meetings and regional specialist networks.
  • Support clinical governance, audit, service improvement, and research activities.
  • Undertake undergraduate and postgraduate teaching.
  • Contribute to the education and supervision of specialty trainees and other healthcare professionals.
  • Work collaboratively with nursing, pharmacy, laboratory, and allied health professional colleagues.

At JPUH, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We are proud of our supportive culture and commitment to developing our staff throughout their careers.

As part of our team, you will benefit from:

  • A welcoming and collaborative consultant body
  • Strong links with regional tertiary haematology centres
  • Opportunities to participate in clinical research and trials
  • Dedicated administrative and secretarial support
  • Modern facilities including an expanded day treatment centre
  • Educational and leadership development opportunities
  • A Trust committed to innovation, improvement, and staff wellbeing

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are a happy, highly motivated and forward-thinking PMS Partnership based in the historic town of Petersfield, Hampshire and looking for a Salaried GP.

This is a 6 sessions per week vacancy and you would hold a patient list as well as covering duty lists.

We are looking for this post to commence December 2026.

The population we serve is diverse is predominantly an affluent area. We achieve highly at the Quality and Outcomes Framework each year, seek out new opportunities and are the host practice for the East Hants PCN. We have approximately 32 members of staff and are a highly regarded training practice welcoming GP trainees, F2 doctors and medical students.

Salary and benefits package will be competitive.

The post holder will be responsible for a patient list and will carry out all associated clinical and administrative work nationally associated and accepted as being part of managing a patient list.

Salaried GPs at the practice undertake 10-minute appointments (although this can be changed to 15 minutes if required), part of the duty rota alongside dedicated administrative time built into the working day to support safe and effective patient care.

About us

The wider team Includes:

  • Three clinical GP Partners
  • One Salaried GP, One GP Retainer.
  • Five Nurses, two Phlebotomists/Health Care Assistants

title: Clinical Endoscopist
descriptionHtml:
The Clinical Endoscopist is responsible for providing high-quality diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopy procedures, ensuring safe, effective, and patient-centred care. Working autonomously within their scope of practice, the post holder will perform upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopic procedures, contribute to early diagnosis and treatment pathways, and support delivery of national waiting time and cancer targets. The role includes clinical assessment, patient management, service development, audit, and multidisciplinary team working to improve patient outcomes and experience. The post holder will also contribute to training, quality improvement initiatives, and the ongoing development of endoscopy services in line with local and national standards

Work independently and unsupervised as an expert Advanced Practitioner in performing diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopy procedures, demonstrating advanced levels of clinical judgement, discretion and clinical decision making.

To be a highly experienced specialist advanced practitioner, with expert knowledge and skills in the field of Endoscopy Services, undertaking holistic assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of programmes of care in accordance with the British Society of Gastroenterology and Joint Advisory Group standards.

To support senior nurse leadership within the endoscopy unit.

To develop and continuously focus on improving patient centred care and overall experience within the endoscopy care pathway.

Why colleagues think we are "a great place to work!"

What does Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust offer you?

As part of our BHT family, you'll benefit from learning and development opportunities to support your career progression.

Alongside NHS benefits of generous annual leave entitlement and pension scheme, you'll have access to NHS discount schemes.

We provide a range of health and wellbeing services to promote a healthy, happy workforce.

What do we stand for?

Our vision is to provide outstanding care, support healthy communities and be a great place to work.

Our mission is to provide personal and compassionate care every time.

We are working hard to increase diversity at all levels within the trust. We believe a diverse workforce can have a positive effect on both staff wellbeing and patient outcomes.

We welcome applications from black, Asian and minority ethnic candidates, LGBTQ+ candidates, candidates with disabilities and care-experienced candidates.

We are proud to achieve the Gold award for the Armed Forces Covenant and support applications from the Armed Forces Community. Please contact Pam.Daley@nhs.net (our Armed Forces Covenant Lead) if you would like guidance or assistance with your application.

We make employment decisions by matching our service needs with the skills and experience of candidates, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender identity, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation.

employer: The Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow for Oncology and Complex Arthroplasty
descriptionHtml:
The Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to employ a Senior Fellow in Orthopaedic Oncology and Joint Reconstruction on a 12 month fixed term contract. The appointee will have orthopaedic oncology and joint reconstruction commitments principally to allow for consultant level cover to orthopaedic oncology sessions and the responsibility for inpatient care of those orthopaedic oncology and arthroplasty patients.

The appointee will be expected to provide teaching and advice to medical students from Birmingham University whilst on their oncology attachment to the Royal Orthopaedic Hospital. Teaching will take place during normal clinical commitments.

During the week research sessions will be made available for ongoing research and audit commitments.

The post holder will be expected to play an active role in the Hospital's clinical audit programme in accordance with criteria set by the Trust and by the Royal College of Surgeons.

Clinic and operating theatres times may vary depending on availability.

It is anticipated that the appointee will work with each Consultant within the service thus gaining maximum experience.

This is not an exhaustive list of duties, and a regular review will take place with the postholder as part of their ongoing development and performance management.

The Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest specialist orthopaedic units in Europe. We offer planned orthopaedic surgery to people locally, nationally and internationally.

Our Trust is a very special hospital; big enough to deliver world class services and small enough to offer exceptional patient and staff experience. We offer a working experience unique in the West Midlands and we're always on the lookout for passionate people to join our award-winning team.

The ROH is an equal opportunities employer. We employ people of difference and are committed to growing an inclusive culture, where difference is celebrated, and people feel able to bring their whole and authentic self to work.

We are a Disability Confident Leader and offer a range of inclusive, family friendly and flexible working arrangements and policies, to support our people in the workplace. Flexible working requests will be considered.

The Trust is committed to the Disability Confident Interview Scheme and will offer an interview to disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for a vacancy and consider them on their abilities.

If you have a disability and need any support with your application or require any reasonable adjustments to be implemented please do get in touch with the Recruiting Manager for this position so that the team can support you.

title: Consultant in Histopathology
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of Substantive Consultant in Histopathology.

There are several posts available for the successful applicants, with potential job-sharing or less than full-time appointments. The successful applicant would join a team of 32 consultants. We work in an oligo-specialist setting - colleagues are encouraged to take part in 2-3 subspecialties, becoming part of the respective teams. In preparation for the approaching retirement of our perinatal Pathologist colleague, we especially welcome applicants with experience in paediatric/perinatal Pathology, or those willing to undertake speciality training provided in collaboration with training centres. Applications from colleagues with skin and GI specialisation are also welcomed, though other subspecialty interests can be accommodated.

Our vision is to create a large and diverse department to provide individuals with personalised and flexible working patterns to support their professional interests and development.

We welcome all applications irrespective of age, disability, gender, sexual orientation, race or religion. Additionally, people with disabilities will be offered an interview providing they meet the minimum criteria for the post. The Trust operates job share and flexible working.

Exceptional locums who are applying for specialist registration via the portfolio pathway may be considered.

The Histopathology team works in a purpose built modern, light, and airy building on a green field site which has been commended for its design and infrastructure by external assessors. It is next to the research park and university campus near the Sports Park. Each consultant has their own or a shared office with up-to-date IT equipment including voice-recognition software.

Workload is controlled by an exit allocation system based on Royal College of Pathologists points, allowing consultants to protect SPA time and provide coverage for job-planned activities outside routine reporting.

Our well-equipped laboratory is UKAS accredited to ISO15189:2022 standards, fully staffed and BMS cut-up is well established. Private practice and work for HM Coroners are optional extras. A number of consultants work part-time, and we actively encourage flexible working, utilising our new digital pathology solution, to ensure a healthy work/life balance. We train and employ advanced practitioners in dissection in Breast and Urology, and reporting in GI and Skin pathology.

As a university teaching hospital, we have developed our research and development strategy in partnership with the University of East Anglia. The successful applicant will not only have the opportunity of training the future generation of pathologists (we have up to 12 ST1-5 trainees at any time and host FRCPath Part 2 exams every other year) but could also participate in undergraduate teaching.

Join us at the Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital and be part of a workforce of over 10,000 staff!

The NNUH is one of the largest NHS trusts in the UK, providing first-class acute care for around one million people, living in Norfolk and surrounding areas. We are a teaching and research hospital, at the forefront of innovation, home to state-of-the-art facilities, such as the Quadram Institute. We are pleased to work closely with the University of East Anglia, providing teaching opportunities for our staff and placement opportunities for their students. We attract some of the best and leading professionals from across the country and are proud that our workforce represents 94 countries from across the world.

We are a friendly, collaborative hospital, working with local services and home to N&N Hospitals Charity

We can offer you the full range of NHS benefits/discounts and in addition:

  • Flexible working hours
  • Fast Track Staff Physiotherapy Service
  • Multi Faith prayer room
  • Discounted gym memberships
  • Excellent pension scheme and annual leave entitlement
  • Wagestream - access up to 40% of your pay as you earn it
  • Free Park & Ride service direct to NNUH site
  • Free 24-hours confidential counselling support
  • On-site Nursery
  • On-site cafes offering staff discounts
  • Support in career development
  • Flexible staff bank
  • Salary Sacrifice schemes including lease cars, Cycle to Work scheme and home electronics

title: Maternity Cover - GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an enthusiastic and committed GP to join our friendly and supportive team at Woodley Centre Surgery on a fixed-term basis to provide maternity cover.

The role offers 6 sessions per week across three days, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, providing an attractive and consistent working pattern. The salary is £11,000 per session per annum (£66,000 per annum for 6 sessions), in line with our existing salaried GP team.

You will work as an integral part of our clinical team, providing high-quality, patient-centred care and contributing to the day-to-day delivery of general practice. We are looking for someone who enjoys working collaboratively and would like to become part of the practice team for the duration of the maternity cover

The successful candidate will provide high-quality, patient-centred general medical services as part of our established multidisciplinary practice team. Duties will include face-to-face, telephone and online consultations, assessment and management of acute and long-term conditions, prescribing, referrals, reviewing investigation results and completing associated clinical administration.

The postholder will maintain accurate clinical records, contribute to continuity of care and work collaboratively with our GP, nursing, clinical and Care Navigation teams. They will also participate in clinical governance, safeguarding and other practice activities appropriate to a salaried GP role.

Woodley Centre Surgery is a modern, well-equipped practice located in the vibrant town of Woodley, with excellent transport links to Reading and the wider Thames Valley.

We are an established training practice comprising of two surgeries. We are providing medical services to a list of 13700 patients across the two sites, with a multi-disciplinary team of GPs, Paramedic, PNs, Pharmacist and Pharmacy Technicians, HCAs, Health and Well-Being team and a supportive non-clinical team.

employer: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow
descriptionHtml:
King's Kidney Care provides adult nephrology, dialysis and renal transplant clinic services to a diverse patient population, estimated at 1.2m, based both locally in South-East London and in areas of Kent, Woolwich/Greenwich, Bromley and Sydenham. The current work of the Unit includes the care of about 1200 patients with end-stage renal failure (ESRF). Of these patients, about 600 are on haemodialysis, 100 on PD and 500 have functioning renal transplants. The Unit provides in-centre, satellite and home haemodialysis. A low clearance clinic (eGFR <20mls/min) provides care for over 450 patients.

This work includes an expanding service at King's Princess Royal University Hospital site, Bromley, and outreach services alongside dialysis units at Darent Valley Hospital, Dartford and Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Woolwich.

The Renal Service provides a referral and diagnostic service for people with kidney disease. This includes outpatient clinics and the facilities for admission for diagnostic procedures, including renal biopsy and renal angiography. In addition, the Unit cares for patients with acute kidney injury (AKI) and admits about 160 AKI cases per year. It has clinical interests in Anaemia, Liver-Renal Disease with a growing liver-kidney transplant programme, Sickle Cell Disease, HIV, Lupus/Vasculitis and Pregnancy.

Together with other colleagues to provide a service for patients. This includes all aspects of treatment and relevant management duties for the proper functioning of the Care Group.

Shared responsibility with other colleagues for providing 24 hours, 7 days a week cover for the Unit on a rota basis. Responsible also for covering colleagues' periods of annual leave and short-term sickness.

Participation in Multi-disciplinary Meetings.

Contribution to audit and clinical governance programmes.

Responsible for outpatient clinic commitments in peripheral hospitals as agreed with the Care Group management team.

Contribute to the Care Group research interests in accordance with the Trust's R&D framework.

Contribute to the audit programmes, Morbidity and Mortality, clinical governance programs and learning from Deaths.

Conduct all activities within the contracted level of service and operating plan for service(s).

Be aware of, and comply with, all Trust infection prevention and control policies, to include hand hygiene, personal hygiene, environmental and food hygiene.

Prepare for and undertake the protective interventions that you are responsible for in a manner that is consistent with evidence-based practice and maintaining patient safety.

The Trust provides a full range of local and specialist services across its five sites. In June 2026, we launched our new strategy for 2026-31. Our vision is to transform healthcare, and we have agreed six strategic ambitions to help us improve care for patients, and the working lives of our staff.

Our six strategic ambitions are deliveringhigh-quality patient care; creating a great place to work; leading pioneering research, innovation and education; building strong and successful partnerships; providing timely and efficient care; and ensuring long-term financial sustainability.

We have also agreed four new organisational values - Caring, Collaborative, Inclusive, Innovative - and these underpin everything we do, and how our teams interact with the patients under our care.

We are at a pivotal point in our history and we require individuals who are ready to join a highly professional team and make a real, lasting difference to our patients and our people.

King's is committed to delivering Sustainable Healthcare for All via our Green Plan. In line with national Greener NHS ambitions, we have set net zero carbon targets of 2040 for our NHS Carbon Footprint and 2045 for our NHS Carbon Footprint Plus. Everyone's contribution is required in order to meet the goals set out in our Green Plan and we encourage all staff to work responsibly, minimising their contributions to the Trust's carbon emissions, waste and pollution wherever possible.

employer: South West London and St Georges Mental Health NHS Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Kingston Hospital
descriptionHtml:

Consultant Liaison Psychiatrist

employer: The Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialty Doctor - Anaesthetics
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking to recruit One substantive specialty doctor anaesthetist to our current department of 22 whole time consultants. These posts have arisen due to expansion.

The Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is located in Birmingham and is an independent trust providing high quality and multidisciplinary care for patients undergoing orthopaedic, spinal (including complex spine) and oncological surgery. The Trust is a tertiary referral centre for both these specialties and revision arthroplasty surgery.

Applications are invited from enthusiastic and highly motivated anaesthetists to join our friendly and supportive department. Currently we have 28 consultants, 5 SAS doctors, 7 Anaesthetic Associates in Theatres and between 4-8 rotating registrars from the Birmingham school of Anaesthesia.

Within our department are five substantive specialty doctor anaesthetists who cover first on call duties with the registrars. The post holder will work within the Anaesthetic team and will undertake theatre and on call duties.

The successful candidate will undertake perioperative care of the patients undergoing orthopaedic surgery. He/she will administer general, regional or combined anaesthesia. The candidate will be expected to know the basic and advanced skills of managing anaesthetic emergencies in patients of all age groups.

He / she will cover the High Dependency Unit and attend cardiac arrests and critically ill patients on the ward. He / she will participate in the inter-hospital transfer of the critically ill patients. The candidate will ensure that he / she follow up the patient in the post-operative period and has understanding of and practiced regional anaesthesia.

There are also seven Anaesthetic Associates (AA) working in our department. They work under the supervision of a consultant anaesthetist in line with RCOA recommendations in a ratio of 1:1 or 1:2. Twin theatre working is embedded in our rota.

The Anaesthetic Department provides anaesthesia services for all orthopaedic surgical procedures being carried out in the hospital including interventional radiology. We currently also have consultants contributing to pre-assessment, HDU, acute and chronic pain and perioperative medicine. We are also in the process of developing an acute pain service to complement the critical care outreach service already in place.

The Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest specialist orthopaedic units in Europe. We offer planned orthopaedic surgery to people locally, nationally and internationally.

Our Trust is a very special hospital; big enough to deliver world class services and small enough to offer exceptional patient and staff experience. We offer a working experience unique in the West Midlands and we're always on the lookout for passionate people to join our award-winning team.

The ROH is an equal opportunities employer. We employ people of difference and are committed to growing an inclusive culture, where difference is celebrated, and people feel able to bring their whole and authentic self to work.

We are a Disability Confident Leader and offer a range of inclusive, family friendly and flexible working arrangements and policies, to support our people in the workplace. Flexible working requests will be considered.

The Trust is committed to the Disability Confident Interview Scheme and will offer an interview to disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for a vacancy and consider them on their abilities.

If you have a disability and need any support with your application or require any reasonable adjustments to be implemented please do get in touch with the Recruiting Manager for this position so that the team can support you.

For more information:

To find out more about us, our work and our inspiring team, please visit www.roh.nhs.uk

title: Consultant in Global Public Health
descriptionHtml:
UKHSA is leading the Public Health Approaches to Violence: Interventions, Surveillance & Evidence (PAVISE) project, a three-year initiative delivered in partnership with Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) and the WHO Collaborating Centre for Violence Prevention. The project aims to support implementation of a coordinated, evidence-based public health approach to violence prevention across UKOTs through violence surveillance, prevention, early intervention, workforce development, research, evaluation and regional collaboration.

The PAVISE Project sits within the UK Overseas Territories (UKOTs) Health Security Programme which is funded by the Overseas Territories Resilient Economies and Security and Stability programme at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). The UKOTs Health Security Programme works in partnership with UKOT governments, regional organisations and UK government partners to strengthen health security and health system resilience across the Territories.

For full details, please refer to the attached Job Description & Person Specification.

o Provide expert public health advice and technical assistance to UKOT governments and health systems on violence prevention, including violence against women and girls, and related public health priorities.o Lead delivery of technical outputs across assigned project workstreams.o Support development, co-design and implementation of evidence-based public health approaches to preventing violence and reducing its impacts.o Contribute to development of policy frameworks, guidance documents, standards and implementation tools.o Support development and implementation of violence surveillance systems across UKOTs including contribution to production of epidemiological profiles, public health intelligence products and violence prevention needs assessments.o Support UKOTs to adopt public health approaches to violence prevention through strategic engagement and technical advice.o Facilitate and contribute to multi-agency workshops and partnership events involving health, policing, education, safeguarding and community sector partners.o Support development of sustainable public health capabilities within health systems and Ministries of Health.o Provide mentoring and supervision to project staff, trainees and public health registrars as required.o Support design and implementation of project evaluation frameworks and monitoring systems.

For full details, please refer to the attached Job Description & Person Specification.

We pride ourselves as being an employer of choice, where Everyone Matters promoting equality of opportunity to actively encourage applications from everyone, including groups currently underrepresented in our workforce.

UKHSA ethos is to be an inclusive organisation for all our staff and stakeholders. To create, nurture and sustain an inclusive culture, where differences drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our workforce and wider communities. We do this through celebrating and protecting differences by removing barriers and promoting equity and equality of opportunity for all.

Please visit our careers site for more information https://gov.uk/ukhsa/careers

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Join our friendly and supportive GP team at Hama Medical Centre

Hama Medical Centre is a well-organised, forward-thinking practice with a friendly and supportive team. We are looking for a motivated Salaried GP to join our established clinical team and become part of a practice that values teamwork, high-quality patient care and a positive working environment.

We operate a total triage model using SystmConnect, helping us to manage patient demand safely and effectively. The role offers a varied clinical week, with a mixture of triage/on-call work and pre-booked appointments, providing both flexibility and continuity of care.

We offer a BMA-compliant job plan, with protected time appropriately allocated within the working week. You will be well supported by experienced GP colleagues, the wider practice team and our well-established PCN.

This is an excellent opportunity for a GP looking to work in a supportive, well-run practice where colleagues work together and where there is scope to develop your role alongside your clinical commitments.

Working 6 sessions across a Wednesday, Thursday, & Friday.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • In accordance with the practice timetable, as agreed, the post-holder will make themselves available to undertake a variety of duties, including surgery consultations, telephone consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking, and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork and correspondence in a timely fashion.
  • Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems, whether self-referred or referred from other health care workers within the organisation.
  • Assessing the health care needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems.

KEY REQUIREMENTS

  • First Medical Degree either MB or MBBS, plus one foundation year as a Medical Practitioner
  • GP Specialist training
  • GMC registration
  • Royal College of General Practitioners membership
  • Experience as a GP
  • Awareness of the duties of a doctor and good medical practice

For more information, please see supporting documents.

PICS is the employer for this role. We collaborate with patients and partners to design and deliver clinically robust health and social care solution through Community Services, Out of Hospital Services, GP Practices, and Primary Care Networks. Find out more about us: http://picsnhs.org.uk/.

Benefits of working for PICS

We offer a comprehensive package which includes:

  • NHS Pension 2015 Scheme (subject to eligibility)
  • Alternative government-based scheme (subject to eligibility)
  • Competitive leave entitlement that includes maternity, paternity and adoption leave, study leave allowance, and sickness provisions
  • Access to education and training opportunities, depending on your role (CPPE Pharmacy, NHS England Roadmap for First Contact Practitioners, apprenticeship schemes, support professional development)
  • Working in a multi-disciplinary team with support from a wide variety of professionals
  • A flexible approach to a work-life balance
  • Cycle to work scheme (subject to eligibility)
