title: Chief of Care Group
descriptionHtml:
CHIEF OF CARE GROUP

Senior Accountable Leadership Role

Posts Available:

  • Medicine Care Group
  • Women, Children, Young People and Families Care Group
  • Cancer Centre and Clinical Services Care Group

Swansea Bay University Health Board is implementing a clinically led Care Group model, aligning services around patient pathways to improve outcomes, experience and sustainability. This is a unique opportunity to shape how health services are designed and delivered for the population of Swansea Bay.

As Chief of Care Group, you will provide strategic leadership across a whole Care Group, holding overall accountability for quality, safety, patient experience, operational performance and financial sustainability. Working within a triumvirate model, you will lead the Care Group Clinical Director and Care Group Operational Director, ensuring cohesive, clinically informed and values-driven leadership.

You will lead service transformation, drive pathway improvement, promote staff engagement and ensure services are organised around the needs of patients, carers and communities. The role requires a visible, collaborative leader who can work across organisational boundaries and contribute to regional and system-wide priorities.

Applicants should indicate their top three Care Group preferences within their application and refer to the accompanying Care Group structure document for further information.

Interview dates: 11, 16 and 18 December

Hours: Minimum 6 sessions (3-days)

  • Act as the Accountable Officer for the Care Group, with overall responsibility for quality, safety, patient experience, operational performance and financial stewardship.
  • Provide line management and leadership to the Care Group Operational Director and Care Group Clinical Director, ensuring clarity of roles, effective decision-making and collective accountability within the triumvirate model.
  • Hold executive accountability for the effective management of professional standards and concerns within the Care Group, including oversight of consultant and senior clinician job planning, workforce utilisation and programmes to improve clinical productivity, ensuring safe, sustainable and value based clinical services.
  • Lead and sponsor the design and delivery of integrated, pathway-based models of care, ensuring services are organised around patient need rather than organisational or geographical boundaries.
  • Ensure a clinically led and prudent approach to decision-making, balancing benefit, harm and value while reducing unwarranted variation and inequality.
  • Provide assurance to Executive leadership and the Board through robust Care Group governance, including learning from complaints, incidents, mortality reviews and patient feedback, in line with Listening to People and Duty of Candour

Swansea Bay University Health Board is one of the largest public service organisations in Wales, with an annual budget of approximately £1.7 billion and a workforce of around 14,700 people. As a major employer in South West Wales, we play a pivotal role in improving health, wellbeing and life chances for the communities we serve.

We provide NHS care to a population of around 390,000 people across Swansea and Neath Port Talbot, delivering services across acute, community, mental health and primary care settings. We also host a range of specialist and tertiary services for patients from across Wales and beyond, including burns and plastics, renal services, cardiac surgery and specialist neonatal care.

Our services are delivered across Morriston Hospital, Singleton Hospital and Neath Port Talbot Hospital, alongside a comprehensive network of community and mental health provision. We also hold responsibility for commissioning primary care services, working in partnership to ensure care is accessible, timely and delivered as close to home as possible.

employer: Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust
title: Medical Director
descriptionHtml:
As Divisional Medical Director, you will share accountability for all aspects of the Diggory Division alongside the Managing Director and Director of Nursing. You will provide strong, compassionate clinical leadership, helping to shape the strategy, culture, and future direction ofmental health services within the Directorate.

You will be central to our transformation journey, ensuring clinical quality, developing the next generation of clinical leaders, and embedding research and innovation across services. You will represent CNWL in key system forums, influence regional strategy, and champion the delivery of high-quality, inclusive care.

Interviews will be held mid-January 2027

The postholder will be based in London but will be expected to maintain a regular and visible presence across the full geographical footprint of Diggory Division, including services in Milton Keynes and Surrey. This is a fundamental requirement of the role, ensuring accessible clinical leadership, effective engagement with staff and service users, and strong relationships with local partners. The postholder must therefore be willing and able to travel regularly between sites as required.

CNWL (Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust) is one of the largest and most diverse community and mental health Trusts in the country. We have received a rating of "good" from the CQC; we care for people across the life course, from preconception through to the end of life. We have a wide range of outstanding partners and work across vibrant and expansive geography.

Our Trust is structured into three Operational Divisions, working alongside centralised corporate support services. Each Division is made up of borough teams and cross-boundary specialised Directorates. Each Division is managed by a team of three - a Managing Director, Director of Nursing and a Medical Director. These three report, respectively, to the Chief Operating Officer, the Chief Nurse and the Chief Medical Officer.

The Divisional teams work closely, along with their Borough and Service line leaders, with the local authority, public health, PCNs and other statutory and non-statutory partners.

title: Locally employed doctor in Haematology

The post holders will contribute to the delivery of a high-quality service, helping to drive a multi-disciplinary team approach to care within the specialty.

Duties will include

  1. Providing support for Core Doctors and Foundation Doctors working in Haematology
  2. Participation in audit and research
  3. Maintain continued professional development.

Although this post is not approved for postgraduate training, the duties are the same as the existing specialty training posts. The successful candidate will be assigned a consultant clinical supervisor and will be encouraged to maintain an educational portfolio with appropriate assessments to their level of experience. There are regular departmental lunchtime teaching sessions which are open to all medical staff to attend. Here at Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust, we are proud to provide expert, compassionate care for our local population. We are ranked as the third in the country for research, embedding education and training across the organisation. Our main hub is the Queen Alexandra Hospital, which is one of the largest hospitals on the south coast employing over 8,700 staff.

employer: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Acute Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The post holder will join a successful and dynamic team that have helped transform Acute Medical Care at Royal Derby Hospital. Our vision is 'to be a pinnacle for best practice and patient care across our emergency and urgent care pathways. We will integrate our services with the wider urgent care network to ensure patients receive the best care possible at the right time and in the right place'.

The Royal Derby Hospital has secured significant funding to reconfigure and redesign our Emergency, Urgent and Acute Care Services to ensure we have the facilities and pathways to meet the changing needs of our patients. We are expanding and redesigning our emergency department, collocating same day emergency care service, urgent care and primary care services. Our assessment units will be expanded and we will provide focus to frailty and mental health pathways. In this context we continue to aim to add further Consultants to our team.

Your clinical role will be working across the Medical Assessment Unit (MAU) Medical Same Day Emergency Care (mSDEC) and provide in reach to our Emergency Department (ED) at the Royal Derby Hospital . You will work 1:6 weekends.

MAU is a 57 bedded unit. When working in MAU for the day you will be one of a team of 3 Acute Medicine Consultants contributing direct clinical care to patients alongside the Junior doctor/ assistant clinical practitioner (ACP) workforce and ward MDT. We also work closely with all our medical specialities who provide Speciality Consultant In reach/Ward rounds 1-2 times per day, 7 days per week.

Our improved Same Day Emergency Care Centre was relaunched at a new on-site location during 2018 and has a dedicated nursing team and a junior doctor workforce. As part of rota commitments you will contribute to Consultant shifts in SDEC.

As a trusted organisation at the heart of our communities, we recognise the important role we can play in supporting the public, patients, our own people and local partners in achieving the best of health for the local population and the communities in which they live by providing Exceptional Care Together

Our fundamental Values of Compassion, Openness and Excellence underpin how we intend to work as a Trust and the associated behaviours are becoming embedded in all aspects of how we work.

In return we will offer:

o Development opportunities, including both professional and leadership developmento On-going support through every step of the way from recruitment to when you join our team and beyond.o A variety of other staff benefits including employee assistance programme, discounted gym membership, onsite fitness classes, car schemes

Key Facts about our Trust:

o We see on average 4810 OP appointments per day.o We are the 4th busiest Trauma & Orthopaedic outpatients department in England - an average of 2077 per week.o An average of 1115 patients are seen in A&Es across our network every day - 3rd largest in the country.o Our hospitals admit an average of 195 emergency patients daily.o Last year we undertook almost 33,700 planned surgical operations in our 57 operating theatres.o We are one of only 7 Trusts nationally with more than 50 operating theatres.o We carry out more than 140 elective procedures each working day.

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Paediatric and Perinatal Pathologist
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a substantive Consultant Paediatric and Perinatal Pathologist to join our Cellular Pathology department. The post is a (whole) full time Consultant post with 10 programmed activities (PAs) and the post holder will be based at St. George's Hospital. The post will include perinatal post-mortem (autopsy) pathology, placental pathology and routine paediatric surgical pathology.

The appointee is expected to have had specialist training in paediatric and perinatal pathology and to have passed the Final Paediatric Pathology Fellowship Exam of the Royal College of Pathologists or equivalent

The appointee, together with consultant colleagues in the Department, will be responsible for the provision of the paediatric and perinatal pathology reporting service. This will include:

Participation in the perinatal and hospital consented paediatric post-mortem service.

- Reporting placentas.

- Reporting routine paediatric surgical pathology.

- Involvement in relevant clinicopathological meetings and MDTs.

- Contribution to the training and supervision of junior medical staff.

Participation in the coroner's paediatric post-mortem service is not a compulsory requirement of this post. The post holder will however be permitted to undertake commensurate Coronial post-mortem work outside the NHS Consultant Job Plan subject to clinical lead approval, Coronial agreement, time shifting and service constraints.

The successful candidate will be expected to work with professional colleagues and local managers in the efficient running of the Service and will share with Consultant colleagues in the medical contribution to management. The successful candidate will be expected to participate in the Trust's system of governance, and audit and maintain their CME/CPD.

St George's, Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals and Health Group cares for a population of four million people in South West London and North East Surrey.Our sites include St George's Hospital, one of 11 major trauma centres in the UK and the largest healthcare provider and major teaching hospital in the area; St Helier Hospital, home to the South West Thames Renal and Transplantation Unit and Queen Mary's Hospital for Children; and Epsom Hospital, home to the South West London Elective Orthopaedic Centre (SWLEOC).

After years of collaboration, our two Trusts became a hospitals group in 2021. While remaining as two separate Trusts, being a hospitals group will help us to collaborate more closely on research, and the development, education, and training of our 17,000-strong workforce.

At gesh we are committed to supporting flexible working arrangements. Applicants are encouraged to discuss any flexibility they may need during the recruitment process.

employer: North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum or Substantive Consultant Ophthalmologist - Medical Retina
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to hire both a Locum (12 month) and a Substantive (permanent) Consultant.

We are looking for a dynamic and forward-thinking Consultant Ophthalmologist - Medical Retina to complete a supportive team of specialists covering North Cumbria. At NCIC, we have an ambition to deliver outstanding hospital and health services to half a million people. employer: Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in General Adult Community Psychiatry
descriptionHtml:
CNWL are currently looking for a full time permanent Consultant Psychiatrist, to provideinput to a high functioning communitymental health team as part of a multi-disciplinary service (South Kensington Mental Health Hub -CMHH).

The role is to provide a comprehensive assessment and NICEconcordant treatment to all patients requiring secondary community mental health services input.

AAC to be held on 4-Dec-2026

*Job Description pending Royal College approval*

This post is a full time (1.00 WTE - 10 sessions) Consultant Psychiatrist replacement post in our South Community Mental Health Hub (CMHH). The South K&C Community Mental Health Hub is based at 1 Nightingale Place and at Violet Melchatt, 30 Flood Walk (the triage function of the SK&C CMHH).

The team is multi-disciplinary and well resourced. It consists of two PCNs (Brompton PCN and South Kensington and Chelsea PCN). The South Hub team's caseload is around 600-650 patients. employer: Doncaster & Bassetlaw Teaching Hospitals NHS FT

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Halesowen 24 sessions per week | Wednesdays and Fridays

Join a forward-thinking practice that puts patients and people first.

We are looking for an enthusiastic, committed and patient-focused GP to join our team in Halesowen through the Additional Roles Reimbursement Scheme (ARRS).

This is an excellent opportunity for a GP who enjoys delivering high-quality general practice, working collaboratively with colleagues and contributing to the ongoing development of a progressive primary care service.

We are a CQC-rated Good practice with a strong commitment to clinical quality, continuous improvement and staff wellbeing. We recognise that the best patient care is delivered by a supported, valued and motivated team.

The role

Working 24 sessions per week on Wednesdays and Fridays, you will provide high-quality, evidence-based general medical services to our registered patient population.

The role will involve:

Clinical consultations: Assessing, diagnosing and managing patients presenting with a broad range of acute and chronic conditions, using face-to-face and remote consultations as appropriate.

Clinical decision-making: Working autonomously within your competence, recognising when onward referral or escalation is required, and maintaining safe clinical practice.

Continuity and coordination of care: Supporting patients with ongoing healthcare needs and working effectively with the wider multidisciplinary team to ensure appropriate follow-up and coordinated care.

Prescribing and clinical management: Making safe, evidence-based prescribing decisions and managing clinical risk in line with current guidance and practice policies.

Accurate clinical documentation: Maintaining clear, timely and comprehensive patient records, including appropriate coding, safety-netting and follow-up arrangements.

Teamworking: Communicating effectively with GPs, nursing colleagues, ARRS professionals and administrative staff to support efficient patient care.

Quality and improvement: Contributing to clinical governance, significant event discussions and service improvement initiatives, helping us continually enhance the care we provide.

Our practice and culture

We believe that a positive working environment is fundamental to delivering excellent patient care. As a CQC-rated Good practice, we are committed to maintaining high standards while continuing to develop and improve our services.

Staff wellbeing is important to us. We value open communication, mutual respect, teamwork and a sustainable approach to work. We want our clinicians to feel supported, listened to and able to make a meaningful contribution to the practice.

employer: Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Research Fellow in Dermatology
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for an exciting 12-month full-time Clinical and Translational Research Fellowship within the National Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB) Service at Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children, London.

This unique fellowship offers an exceptional opportunity for a paediatrician or dermatologist to gain specialist clinical and academic experience at one of the world's leading centres for the care of children and young people with epidermolysis bullosa. The successful candidate will become an integral member of our multidisciplinary team, providing specialist care for patients with EB whilst contributing to pioneering translational research.

A particular highlight of this fellowship is the opportunity to play a leading role in MISSION EB DELIVER, an innovative open-label clinical study investigating EBSTROCEL mesenchymal stromal cell infusions for patients with epidermolysis bullosa. Working closely with the Clinical Research Facility at Great Ormond Street Hospital, the successful candidate will gain first-hand experience in delivering an advanced cell therapy programme, including patient assessment, infusion procedures, clinical trial delivery and longitudinal follow-up care.

This is a new post aimed for a doctor who wishes to acquire unique experience in a subspecialty of pediatric dermatology with some clinical and in addition the unusual opportunities to take part in research and the running of a clinical trial MISSIONEB-Deliver an open study of mesenchymal intravenous Stromal cell infusions, CRODStrom in children with recessive dystrophic Epidemolysis bullosa.

We are committed to recruiting the best person for the job through a fair, open and consistent process that is free from bias and discrimination.

We are working towards becoming an anti-racist organisation. This means creating a workplace where every colleague feels seen, heard and valued, and where racism in any form has no place. Our anti-racism commitment is backed by action through our Anti-Racism Statement and action plan, developed in collaboration with our REACH staff network.

We actively challenge discrimination, dismantle barriers and embed equity across all aspects of our workforce, including recruitment, progression and development. All applicants will receive equal consideration regardless of race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, health condition or employment history.

We particularly welcome applications from ethnically diverse communities, people with disabilities or long-term health conditions, and LGBTQ+ community members. We are proud to be a Disability Confident Employer, a member of the Business Disability Forum, and a Stonewall Diversity Champion.

Our staff networks, including REACH, PRIDE, ENABLED and Women's Networks, are active and executive supported. These employee-led networks play a vital role in shaping an inclusive culture at GOSH and are open to all colleagues.

Together, we are building a culture where inclusion is not optional - it is essential.

title: PCN ARRS General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Rugby Health Primary Care Network is looking to expand our team by seeking to employ experienced or newly qualified General Practitioners.

(Applicants cannot have been employed as a GP in a substantive post within a Rugby Health practice in the past 12 months).

We are offering up to 9 sessions per week (FTE) with a start date as soon as possible. Candidates may apply for a part-time (minimum 4 sessions) or a full-time role.

Working across 2 of our 12 practices alongside our multi-disciplinary teams, the post-holder will perform as an autonomous general practitioner working independently and with other health care professionals to assess, diagnose and treat the conditions of patients attending within a primary care setting. This will include the provision of expert professional advice to patients, carers and colleagues thereby ensuring the maintenance of clinical excellence as well as involvement in the provision of education and training to GP Registrars and other staff.

The following are the core responsibilities of the Salaried GP. There may be, on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels:

The delivery of highly effective medical care to the entitled population

The provision of services commensurate with the primary care contract

Generic prescribing adhering to local and national guidance

Effective management of long-term conditions

Processing of administration in a timely manner, including referrals, repeat prescription requests and other associated administrative tasks

On a rotational basis, undertake telephone triage and duty doctor roles

Maintain accurate clinical records in conjunction with good practice, policy and guidance

Work collaboratively, accepting an equal share of the practice workload

Adhere to best practice recommended through clinical guidelines and the audit process

Contribute to the successful implementation of continuous improvement and quality initiatives within the practice

Accept delegated responsibility for a specific area (or areas) of the QOF

Attend and contribute effectively to practice meetings as required

Contribute effective to the development and maintenance of the practice including clinical governance and training

Ensure compliance with the appraisal process

Prepare and complete the revalidation process

Please view the full job description for a complete overview of all responsibilities for this post.

Rugby Health PCN Rugby Health is a private limited company wholly owned by all the Rugby GP practices. As a GP led organisation, we represent 12 GP practice shareholders and cover circa 126,600 patients. We describe our work as building on the core of current primary care services to enable greater provision of proactive, personalised, coordinated and more integrated health and social care. Our aim is to move from reactively providing appointments to proactively caring for the people and communities we serve.

Why Work For Us?

  • On-site parking at GP practices
  • Flexible hours and working arrangements considered from day 1
  • Dynamic and adaptable team
  • Training and support, enabling you to develop within the role

Additional information:

  • Access to your own car will be required to travel across practices within the PCN to meet the needs of the business
  • Right to work checks
  • All applicants invited for interview will need to prove their right to work in the UK for the duration of their employment

  • Please ensure you complete all sections of the application form fully and accurately as incomplete applications may not be shortlisted.

title: Radiographer
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an experienced HCPC-registered Diagnostic Radiographer to provide imaging for patients undergoing elective orthopaedic and spinal surgery.

You will perform post-operative orthopaedic X-rays and provide mobile C-arm fluoroscopy in theatre, including support for spinal procedures. Working with the theatre and ward teams, you will help coordinate imaging around operating lists and discharge plans.

This is an opportunity to help establish the imaging service within a new surgical hub.

The successful candidate will:

  • Perform post-operative orthopaedic X-rays and intra-operative imaging within your competence and agreed scope of practice.
  • Operate mobile C-arm equipment safely during orthopaedic and spinal procedures.
  • Check patient identity, imaging requests and pregnancy status where relevant, following agreed procedures.
  • Work within your employer entitlement under IR(ME)R, ensuring exposures are justified and authorised through the agreed pathway.
  • Optimise image quality and radiation dose, following IR(ME)R, IRR17 and local radiation protection rules.
  • Position and support patients safely, taking account of post-operative pain, mobility and surgical precautions.
  • Complete equipment checks and quality assurance tasks, escalating faults or image quality concerns promptly.
  • Maintain accurate imaging and exposure records, ensuring images are available for clinical review.
  • Follow agreed escalation pathways for urgent concerns, unexpected findings and radiation incidents.
  • Maintain infection prevention standards and work safely within the sterile theatre environment.
  • Work with the multidisciplinary team and contribute to audit, service improvement and safe imaging workflows.

One Health Group was established in Sheffield in 2004 and has steadily and successfully grown to become a significant healthcare provider in the region. Commissioned by the NHS, we provide services for patients referred for Orthopaedics, General Surgery, Spine, Urology and Gynaecology and with clinics located in over 30 locations across Yorkshire, Derbyshire, Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire and Lincolnshire, we bring healthcare closer to where people live. We are committed to clinical excellence, and our mission is to provide innovative, high quality medical and clinical services for our patients, optimising outcomes so they can quickly continue healthy lives.

OHG Surgical Hub is a new specialist elective surgical facility being developed to provide high-quality care for patients undergoing major orthopaedic and spinal procedures.

Our service includes:

  • One modern operating theatre.
  • Three-bay recovery unit.
  • Twelve inpatient bedrooms.
  • Dedicated pre-assessment and outpatient facilities.

We specialise in elective surgery, including:

  • Total hip replacement.
  • Total knee replacement.
  • Revision arthroplasty where clinically appropriate.
  • Spinal procedures including ACDF, cervical decompression, lumbar decompression, discectomy and spinal fusion procedures.

We are developing a clinical team focused on delivering safe, compassionate and high-quality patient care.

employer: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with Special Interest in Paediatrics
descriptionHtml:

title: Locum Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
This is a Locum Consultant Dermatologist role, offered for a fixed term period of 12 months. The post is offered on a part time contract for approximately 7 PA.The post will commence as soon as possible. The successful applicant will join a team of dermatologists who work closely with the plastic surgery department to provide a skin cancer service at Southmead Hospital Operating Unit (HOU). We provide a general dermatology service and have close links with the dermatology department at City Hospital Operating unit with whom we are developing a Group Clinical Service, led by the Medicine Division at City & Weston HOU.

The dermatology service is a local and regional service primarily covering Bristol and South Gloucestershire populations, but we also provide an SSMDT and accept tertiary referrals for patients with complex skin cancer in the South-West. We also deliver specialist services such as Mohs' micrographic surgery, Laser, Biologics for Eczema, Vulval dermatology, and Psychodermatology. The post-holder will join a team of 7 Consultant Dermatologists, 1 Specialty Doctor, 3 specialist nurses and 6 Resident Doctors employed at Southmead.

The Dermatology Department is within the Surgical Directorate at Southmead and is currently managed together with Plastic Surgery to improve skin cancer patient pathways. The Dermatologists see approximately 9,500 new patients and 8,000 follow ups per year. There is a dedicated area of outpatients in the Brunel building at Southmead Hospital that houses both Dermatology, Plastic Surgery, local anaesthetic skin surgery theatres, procedure rooms and a Mohs laboratory.

The post-holder will be based at Southmead Hospital but may be asked to provide a Dermatology clinic in a community setting or in another hospital location. NBT Dermatology clinics are also run at Cossham Hospital, Kingswood.

The job plan will include Outpatient Clinics, Surgery, Management of internal referrals from ED or the Hospital bed base. Teledermatology and Advice and Guidance will be delivered remotely.

The post holder may be asked to work flexibly including the consideration of evening clinics. Currently the service delivers clinics at Southmead Hospital and Cossham Hospital, Kingswood. The postholder will be will be primarily based at Southmead HOU but may be asked to provide a dermatology clinic in a community setting or in another hospital location including (but not limited to) Bristol Royal Infirmary, Weston General Hospital and South Bristol Community Hospital.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust brings together more than 28,000 staff to deliver over 160 clinical services across thirteen hospital locations, operating from three main sites at Southmead, Bristol city centre and Weston.With an annual turnover of 2.6 billion, we are now one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom.

title: Consultant Radiologist
descriptionHtml:
Job Overview

Join the Radiology Team at James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

An exciting opportunity has arisen for a motivated and forward-thinking Consultant Radiologist to join the Radiology Directorate at James Paget University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust. We are looking for an enthusiastic clinician who is committed to delivering high-quality patient care and helping to shape the future of imaging services within a modern and progressive NHS organisation.

You will work alongside a supportive team of Consultant Radiologists and multidisciplinary colleagues, providing a comprehensive range of diagnostic and interventional radiology services. The successful candidate will play a key role in maintaining excellent clinical standards, supporting service development, and contributing to innovative ways of delivering care for our local population.

As a teaching hospital, we are committed to education, training, research, and professional development. You will have opportunities to supervise and mentor junior doctors, radiographers, and other healthcare professionals while contributing to undergraduate and postgraduate medical education.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a friendly, collaborative department that values innovation, teamwork, clinical excellence, and continuous improvement.

As a Consultant Radiologist, you will share responsibility with colleagues for the delivery of a comprehensive and high-quality radiology service across the Trust. Your clinical duties will include reporting and specialist input across a range of modalities, which may include plain film radiography, ultrasound, CT, MRI, fluoroscopy and image-guided intervention.

The post holder will contribute to:

  • Emergency and acute imaging services.
  • Cancer and Faster Diagnostic Pathway services.
  • Urgent and routine outpatient imaging.
  • National screening programs ( Breast and Lung Cancer Screening) where appropriate.
  • Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) meetings across a range of specialties.
  • Service improvement and transformation projects within the department.

You will participate in the consultant on-call rota and provide cross-cover during annual, study, and professional leave. The role also involves providing expert radiological advice to clinical colleagues across the Trust and working closely within multidisciplinary teams to ensure the highest standards of patient care.

In addition, there will be opportunities to contribute to teaching, training, governance, audit, and departmental development

JPUH serves a population of approximately 250,000 people across Great Yarmouth, Lowestoft, and surrounding communities in Norfolk and Suffolk. Our vision is to provide excellent patient-centred care while fostering a culture where staff can thrive, develop, and reach their full potential.

Our busy and dynamic Radiology Department performs more than:

  • 70,000 X-rays annually
  • 50,000 CT and MRI scans annually
  • 30,000 ultrasound examinations annually

The Clinical Team currently comprises 15 Consultant Radiologists, reporting radiographers, sonographers and trainees rotating from Norwich Radiology Academy.

  • Specialist Registrars from NNUH

employer: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Histopathologist in Gastrointestinal & Cytopathology
descriptionHtml:
King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is one of London's foremost teaching trusts, combining clinical excellence with a culture of innovation. We are seeking an outstanding Consultant Histopathologist to join our forward-thinking department at an exciting moment in its evolution.

Our recent transition to fully digital pathology reporting has transformed how we work -- offering flexibility, efficiency, and a platform for the future. Cross-site reporting across King's Denmark Hill and Princess Royal University Hospital in Orpington means genuine variety in your practice, with the benefits of a large, well-resourced trust and strong, collaborative teams at both sites.

You will manage a diverse, high-volume caseload with rich subspecialty exposure, supported by close MDT integration and digital infrastructure. Academic opportunities are available through our partnership with King's College London, with scope for research, audit, and teaching at all levels.

If you are a resourceful, ambitious histopathologist ready to embrace digital-first working and the opportunities of a truly multi-site trust, we would love to hear from you.

The Histopathology department at Denmark Hill undertakes histopathology (including frozen sections), diagnostic cytopathology (excluding cervical cytology) and autopsy pathology.

We are looking to recruit a locum consultant. This is a replacement post, timetabled for 8 PA per week, however there is scope to expand this to a full time (10 PA) role should the candidate prefer this. The post will require the post holder to play an active role in the general running of the department, with specialist interests in Gastrointestinal pathology, Cytopathology. If desired, autopsy work can be arranged by mutual consent with the Clinical Leads and local Coroner. The successful candidate will join an impressive team dedicated to providing a first-class patient-centred service.

Potential applicants will be welcome to visit the department and discuss this post.

You must be fully registered with the GMC and hold a Licence to Practice and be on the Specialist Register, or within six months of attaining your CCT or equivalent to be eligible for interview.

The Trust provides a full range of local and specialist services across its five sites. The trust-wide strategy of Strong Roots, Global Reach is our Vision to be BOLD, Brilliant people, Outstanding care, Leaders in Research, Innovation and Education, Diversity, Equality and Inclusion at the heart of everything we do. By being person-centred, digitally-enabled, and focused on sustainability, we aim to take Team King's to another level.

We are at a pivotal point in our history and we require individuals who are ready to join a highly professional team and make a real, lasting difference to our patients and our people.

King's is committed to delivering Sustainable Healthcare for All via our Green Plan. In line with national Greener NHS ambitions, we have set net zero carbon targets of 2040 for our NHS Carbon Footprint and 2045 for our NHS Carbon Footprint Plus. Everyone's contribution is required in order to meet the goals set out in our Green Plan and we encourage all staff to work responsibly, minimising their contributions to the Trust's carbon emissions, waste and pollution wherever possible.

title: Consultant in Diabetes and Endocrinology
descriptionHtml:
Northumbria Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to expand it's services for Diabetes and Endocrinology as we develop and strengthen our 10 year strategy for the future.

We are looking to recruit full-time Consultant Physicians, both newly qualified and with post CCT experience in Diabetes & Endocrinology and General Medicine.

We would love to see applications from existing and new consultants with interests in ante-natal care, young person's care, footcare and endocrinology. We would also welcome applicants who have an interest in developing their leadership skills, services associated with technology, education and research.

The successful applicants will also be expected to strengthen locality-based service delivery of Diabetes & Endocrinology services building our out of hospital model of care.

This post will be based at either North Tyneside General Hospital or Wansbeck General Hospital (this is yet to be determined) but will be trustwide with clinics on other trust sites.

There is the potential option to include some General Medicine on-call within the job plan which would be based out of the Northumbria Specialist Emergency Care Hospital.

Please note we reserve the right to close this vacancy prior to the closing date once the required number of suitable applications have been received.

The successful candidate (s) will be jointly responsible for the provision of diabetes, endocrinology and general medical services to the population of Northumbria and will be encouraged to develop a sub-specialist interest to complement the other members of the department

The appointee(s) will provide continuing clinical responsibility for patients under his/her care and assume responsibility for and facilitate contact from members of staff with delegated duties for patient care.

The appointee would also continue to provide educational and clinical supervision to trainees in specialty and general medicine.

The post holder will be required to participate in clinical audit activities including clinical audit meetings.

A typical week would consist of 10 Programmed Activities (PAs), including an allocation of 1.5 SPAs for Supported Professional Activities. Additional SPAs will be available dependant upon service need. A proposed job plan has been outlined in the job description and will be agreed on commencement of appointment.

The post holder will be expected to participate in the provision of cover on a shared basis with colleagues for periods of annual, sickness and study leave, except for prolonged absence where locum cover may be necessary.

The post holder will also contribute to the acute general medicine rota in the out of hours periods at the Northumbria Specialist Emergency Care Hospital (currently 1 in 7 weekends).

We manage three major locality hospitals at North Tyneside, Wansbeck and Hexham, plus a number of smaller community hospitals and clinics from Tynemouth to Berwick on Tweed, covering one of the largest geographical areas of any NHS trust in the country. Leading in innovation and quality - opening a state of the art Northumbria Specialist Emergency Care Hospital, the first of its kind in England. Do you want to work in one of the best performing NHS organisations in England? Work in an organisation that supports its staff and focuses on staff experience as much as it does the experience of its patients? You can live and breathe in an area that has the cleanest air, cost effective living, great nightlife, some of the best schools with a wealth of history available on your doorstep. Sound too good to be true? Well it isn't, this is what you get when you work for Northumbria Healthcare, this is the Northumbria Way! Please read 'applicant guidance notes' before submitting your application.

title: Consultant Medical Oncologist - Colorectal & Breast
descriptionHtml:

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Ivy Medical Group is a forward-thinking, supportive, and patient-centred GP practice serving our local communities. We are looking for an enthusiastic and committed Salaried GP to join our friendly, multidisciplinary team.

This is an exciting opportunity to work within a well-established practice that values clinical excellence, teamwork, and innovation. You will be supported by our experienced GP Principal, GP's, Advanced Clinical Practitioner, Nurses, Pharmacists, Administrators, and an approachable management team who are committed to creating a positive working environment.

Whether you are an experienced GP or looking for your next career move, we offer a welcoming practice culture where your contribution is valued and your wellbeing matters.

Join us and become part of a team dedicated to delivering high-quality primary care while supporting one another to achieve the best outcomes for our patients and staff.

So why this position? We have an excellent team of staff all motivated, committed and passionate to provide the very best care to our patients. We provide a positive safe environment and culture in which to practice medicine. The post will have the opportunity to provide minor surgery as well as understanding how a dispensing practice functions. We support our clinical team to engage in practice improvement and contributing to the future of the practice.

We are a training practice for medical students and GP registrars. There will be an opportunity to be involved with teaching and training of medical students and registrars. We will be improving our practice premises in the 5 years ahead providing up to date facilities.

We include 6 weeks annual leave with bank holidays in addition. There is one week study leave in addition. Indemnity fees are covered.

We have a list size of 6500 and a full team including GPs, Nurses, HCA, ACPs, Dispensers, Reception, Secretarial and Administrative staff. We employ apprentices to help train our next generation. We have strong links with our PCN, we are a part Arrow PCN.

Ivy Medical Group is a progressive, patient-focused practice serving a diverse population. We are committed to delivering high-quality healthcare while creating a supportive and rewarding environment.

Our multidisciplinary team includes GPs, ACPs, Clinical Pharmacists, First Contact Physiotherapists, Social Prescribers, Nursing Team, and dedicated Admin and Reception colleagues. We work collaboratively to provide safe, effective, and responsive care to our patients while supporting one another in a culture of respect and continuous improvement.

We recognise the challenges facing modern general practice and have developed systems and processes that allow clinicians to focus on delivering excellent patient care. Our leadership team is, supportive, and committed to staff wellbeing, professional development, and maintaining a positive work-life balance.

Working at Ivy Medical Group offers the opportunity to be part of an organisation that embraces innovation, values teamwork, and encourages individuals to contribute their ideas and expertise. We support learning and development, participation in service improvement initiatives, and opportunities to develop special interests.

We are proud of our friendly and inclusive culture, where everyone is valued and recognised for the contribution they make to patient care, Ivy Medical Group offers a welcoming environment in which you can thrive professionally whilst making a meaningful difference to the communities we serve.

title: General Practitioner - Primary Care Streaming
descriptionHtml:
Looking for a GP role that combines the variety of primary care with the pace and clinical challenge of an acute hospital environment? Primary Care 24 (PC24) is recruiting GPs to join our Primary Care Streaming Service within the Linda McCartney Centre at the Royal Liverpool University Hospital. You will be providing high-quality assessment and management for patients presenting to urgent and emergency care.

What will I be doing?

  • Provide high quality holistic clinical care, using skills and experience in accordance with the GMCs Good Medical Practice (2024), demonstrating care, compassion, dignity and respect
  • Make independent, professional decisions to address individual patient issues effectively
  • Evaluate and address the urgent healthcare needs of patients presenting with undiagnosed and undefined conditions.
  • Prescribe treatments appropriately, adhering to national guidance and the local formulary.
  • Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems..
  • Work as part of a multidisciplinary team to facilitate the safe and timely referral and/or admission of patients who require same day hospital care, following the principal that it is preferential to refer on to medical/surgical teams, whilst referral to ED should only occur if a medical/surgical referral is less appropriate.
  • Maintain accurate and contemporaneous electronic medical records with the PC24 clinical system.
  • Perform any other duties as agreed with the Medical Director, Clinical Lead or Head of Service to meet the needs of the service/organisation.

About us Primary Care 24 (PC24) is a not-for-profit social enterprise established in 2004, predominately delivering NHS contracts. The majority of our surplus is reinvested in patients and staff. We believe that primary healthcare should be accessible for everyone and are committed to delivering the best quality care we can, challenging social exclusion and working locally, where and when we can, to support our communities. We combine the best of the NHS with social enterprise innovation, developing solutions for NHS primary care and caring for our clinicians so that they can, in turn, care for our patients. Come join our proud team!

title: Portfolio General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
South Coast Alliance (SCA) is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Portfolio General Practitioner to join our team, working across services in Portsmouth and South East Hampshire.

We are looking for a GP who is passionate about delivering high-quality, patient-centred care, enjoys working collaboratively and is keen to contribute to the ongoing development of our services.

At South Coast Alliance, we are committed to supporting professional development, innovation and a positive working environment, giving you the opportunity to develop your interests while making a meaningful difference to patient care.

The Portfolio GP will deliver high-quality, patient-centred care across South Coast Alliance services in Portsmouth and South East Hampshire, undertaking face-to-face, telephone and remote consultations.

The role involves assessing, diagnosing and managing a range of acute and urgent conditions, making appropriate referrals, prescribing safely and maintaining accurate clinical records.

Alongside clinical duties, the postholder will have opportunities to contribute to clinical leadership, education, quality improvement, service development and clinical governance, working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams to improve patient care and service delivery.

South Coast Alliance (SCA) is a collaborative healthcare organisation delivering primary and urgent care services across Portsmouth and South East Hampshire.

We work in partnership with local healthcare providers to deliver safe, effective and high-quality patient care, supporting patients to access the right care, in the right place, at the right time.

Our services bring together experienced GPs, nurses, allied health professionals and operational teams, working collaboratively to meet the needs of our local communities.

At SCA, we are committed to continuous quality improvement, clinical excellence and workforce development. We encourage innovation, shared learning and professional development, creating a supportive environment where our staff can make a positive difference to patient care.

title: Consultant Audiological Physician
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Consultant Audiovestibular Physician to join our established Audiology and ENT service within Hywel Dda University Health Board. This is an opportunity to work collaboratively with clinical, medical, professional and managerial colleagues to provide high-quality, patient-centred care whilst contributing to the ongoing development of Audiovestibular Medicine services across the Health Board.

The successful candidate will be responsible for the assessment, diagnosis and management of paediatric and adult patients with hearing and balance disorders, including infants identified through the Newborn Hearing Screening Programme, children with permanent hearing impairment requiring diagnostic evaluation, and adults presenting with tinnitus, progressive hearing loss, vertigo, balance disorders and unexplained audiological symptoms. Working closely with colleagues across ENT, Paediatrics, Audiology, Therapy Services, Primary Care and wider multidisciplinary teams, you will play a key role in delivering safe, effective and coordinated care.

  • Deliver a comprehensive Audiovestibular Medicine service for paediatric and adult patients across Hywel Dda University Health Board, providing specialist assessment, diagnosis and management of hearing and balance disorders.
  • Assess and manage infants identified through the Newborn Hearing Screening Programme, children with permanent hearing impairment requiring diagnostic evaluation, and adults presenting with tinnitus, progressive hearing loss, unexplained audiological symptoms, vertigo, balance disorders and falls.
  • Provide clinical leadership in the development and enhancement of Audiovestibular Medicine services within the wider ENT framework, supporting service innovation, pathway development and the delivery of high-quality, patient-centred care.
  • Work collaboratively with clinical, medical, professional and managerial colleagues, leading and participating fully within multidisciplinary teams across ENT, Paediatrics, Audiology, Therapy Services, Primary Care and community services.
  • Provide specialist advice and leadership in the management of complex audiological and vestibular cases, supporting coordinated care across all Health Board sites and participating in domiciliary consultations where required.

Hywel Dda University Health Board plans and provides NHS healthcare services for people living in Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire, and bordering counties.

We have over 13,000 staff and together we provide primary, community, in-hospital, mental health and learning disabilities services.

We work in partnership with the three local authorities, as well as public, private and third sector colleagues, including our valued team of volunteers.

Our services are provided in:

  • Four main hospitals: Bronglais Hospital in Aberystwyth; Glangwili Hospital in Carmarthen; Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli; and Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest
  • Five community hospitals: Amman Valley and Llandovery hospitals in Carmarthenshire; Tregaron Hospital in Ceredigion; and Tenby and South Pembrokeshire hospitals in Pembrokeshire
  • Two integrated care centres: Aberaeron and Cardigan in Ceredigion, and several other community settings
  • 47 general practices (six of which are health board managed practices); dental practices (including four orthodontic); 97 community pharmacies; 43 general ophthalmic practices; and 8 ophthalmic domiciliary providers
  • Numerous mental health and learning disabilities services

employer: North Tees & Hartlepool NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant - Palliative Care
descriptionHtml:
The successful candidate will be expected to work as part of North Tees and Hartlepool (NTUH) fully integrated Palliative Care team across hospital community and hospice settings as required. This post will involve a minimum of 1.5 sessions per week of regular hospice clinical work. This maybe in either one of two local hospices: Alice House Hospice in Hartlepool or Butterwick Hospice in Stockton (9 and 8 bedded adult inpatient units respectively).

Hospital and community clinical work will involve face to face and non-face to face patient reviews, as well as advising and supporting the palliative care team and wider healthcare teams with clinical management of patients.

On call duties are in the mainstay non-resident, taking advice calls from hospital, community and hospice settings, as part of University Hospital Tees (UHT) wide consultant rota. There is an expectation that consultants will attend to review patients face to face in a hospice setting out of hours if required to support a doctor in training in exceptional circumstances. Consultants on call are expected to be within 2 hours travel time from the hospices covered on call (located in Middlesbrough, Hartlepool and Stockton).

The successful candidatewill be welcomed to join our dynamic integrated palliative care service at North Tees and Hartlepool (NTH) providing input into community, hospital and hospice settings.

Base and clinical settings primarily based with the North Tees and Hartlepool integrated palliative care team at the University Hospital of North Tees.

  • Expected to work flexibly across hospital, community and hospice settings according to clinical need.
  • A minimum average of 1.5 sessions per week in a hospice is an essential requirement of the post.
  • Regular hospice work will be undertaken at either Butterwick Hospice, Stockton or Alice House Hospice, Hartlepool.
  • Butterwick Hospice is immediately adjacent to the University Hospital of North Tees. Alice House Hospice is located a 25-minute drive away in Hartlepool and includes a satellite office for the hospital and community team within.

Consultant team

The appointee joins a wider group of 10 Palliative Medicine consultants across University Hospitals Tees (a geographical area that covers: North Tees and Hartepool; Middlesbrough, Redcar and Cleveland; and Hambleton and Richmondshire).

North Tees and Hartlepool NHS Foundation Trust and South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust have come together to form University Hospitals Tees. As a result, post holders may be required to work across sites within both organisations.

At UHT our main priority is, and always will be, to provide safe and high quality care to our patients every day; the kind of care we would want for ourselves and our loved ones. We want our organisation to be the best place to work with the right staff, in the right roles, at the right time, to ensure we deliver exceptional patient care and experience.

employer: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Respiratory Medicine
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a full time Consultant Respiratory Physician to join the Complex Home Ventilation and Specialist Weaning Service at Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, primarily based at Royal Brompton Hospital.The successful candidate will join one of the largest and most established specialist ventilation services internationally, providing care to more than 3,000 patients receiving home ventilation, including over 100 patients requiring long term tracheostomy ventilation.The service also provides specialist assessment and management for patients requiring prolonged mechanical ventilation and complex ventilator weaning. This regional service receives over 100 referrals annually and operates through the Lane Fox Unit at St Thomas' Hospital, the Remeo Units and a specialist outreach service based at Royal Brompton Hospital.The post holder will work alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team of respiratory consultants, specialist nurses, physiotherapists, pharmacists, clinical psychologists and speech and language therapists.Applicants are expected to have specialist experience in home ventilation and ventilator weaning, alongside a commitment to clinical excellence, research, education and service development.

Please note that we will be closing the advert after the maximum number of applications have been received, so please apply as early as possible if interested.

The post holder will provide specialist consultant respiratory care within the Complex Home Ventilation and Specialist Weaning Service, primarily based at Royal Brompton Hospital, working collaboratively with colleagues across Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust.

Key responsibilities include:

Providing specialist assessment, treatment and ongoing management of patients requiring home ventilation and prolonged mechanical ventilation.

Supporting the assessment and management of patients referred for specialist ventilator weaning across inpatient and outreach services.Working closely with the multidisciplinary team to deliver safe, effective and individualised patient care.

Contributing to the development of clinical pathways and improvements in service delivery.

Participating in clinical governance, audit, quality improvement and service development.

Supporting clinical research, including recruitment to appropriate clinical trials.

Contributing to medical education, teaching and clinical supervision.Participating in departmental management, service planning and appropriate on call commitments.

The post holder will demonstrate effective clinical leadership and a commitment to high quality patient care.

Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK's largest NHS foundation trusts, providing specialist, hospital and community services.

The Trust comprises five hospitals: Guy's, St Thomas', Evelina London Children's Hospital, Royal Brompton and Harefield, alongside community services in Lambeth and Southwark.

With approximately 22,700 staff, the Trust is recognised for clinical excellence, research, innovation and education. As part of King's Health Partners, we work closely with academic and clinical partners to improve patient care through research and innovation.

The Royal Brompton Lung Directorate provides nationally and internationally recognised specialist respiratory services, including complex home ventilation and specialist weaning.

Our organisational values guide everything we do:

Caring: We put patients first.Ambitious: We innovate and strive for excellence.Inclusive: We respect each other and work collaboratively.

We are committed to providing an inclusive working environment, supporting staff development and delivering high quality patient care.

employer: Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Upper Limb Specialty Doctor in Trauma & Orthopaedics
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of an Upper Limb Senior Specialty Doctor (middle grade) for Trauma and Orthopaedics (T&O) department.This is not a registrar post. This is a senior position for independent upper limb surgery. Please DO NOT apply if you are not proficient in running elective upper limb clinics and theatres independently. This is initially a one-year fixed term post, but extendable thereafter for the right candidate. We expect the candidate to be able to perform hand procedures (carpal tunnel, triggers, Dupuytren's, Trapeziectomy etc) and also basic shoulder procedures including arthroscopy procedures (eg subacromial decompression, capsular release etc) independently. The successful candidate will beindependently managing patient carein outpatient clinics, fracture clinics, virtual fracture clinics, triaging and running elective upper limb and trauma theatres. There will also be opportunities to teach and support more junior staff in the department.We are seeking a dynamic and proactive candidate, with elective upper limb experience, who would be able to make independent decisions in elective upper limb clinics, run elective upper limb theatres, and weekend general trauma lists (1:8). There will be consultant support and potential to do more complex elective upper limb cases jointly with consultants.

The main duties of the applicant include managing and treating T&O patients independently and under consultant supervision, leading and supporting other junior doctors. They will be expected to work as a part of a team and provide support to all staff within the team. TheOrthopaedicDepartment hascentralisedall Trauma Services at Queens Hospital in Romford, with Inpatient Elective activity being undertaken at King Georges Hospital inGoodmayes, with hospital-provided transportation available between sites.We are currently working with our external partners to ensure a streamlined pathway from referral to treatment thus ensuring achievement of the 18-week RTT target.We have a fully-fledged 'virtual fracture clinic' service since December 2019 to enable a more robust triage service and reducing the amount of unnecessary face-to-face appointments in fracture clinics, that patients are asked to attend following their A&E/UCC attendance. This is coupled with a more intuitive system of referring patients directly to the correct sub-specialty clinic for further treatment under the most relevant consultant.

We're an organisation that is getting better and better and our improvements are driven by a determination to deliver care we're proud of and our patients are happy with.

They are benefitting from a new electronic patient record (we were the last acute trust in London to introduce one) and our maternity services have been rated good by the Care Quality Commission.

We operate from two main sites - KGH in Goodmayes and Queen's Hospital in Romford. We have two busy emergency departments with more than 346,000 people visiting them last year. We're campaigning to secure the £35m we need to transform the A&E at Queen's and get rid of corridor care.

We're proud of our regional Neurosciences Centre, Radiotherapy Centre and Hyper Acute Stroke Unit. We're also part of the North East London Cancer Alliance.

We run a Women's Health Hub in Ilford; an Ageing Well Centre in Hornchurch; and Community Diagnostic Centres (CDC) at Barking Community Hospital and at St George's Health and Wellbeing Hub. These CDCs are open 12 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The majority of our 8,400 staff - who come from 146 different countries - live in the three diverse London boroughs we serve and are from black, Asian and minority ethnic groups. Many can work flexibly and more than 400 of them are on our Ofsted accredited apprenticeship programmes. We're proud to be a London Living Wage employer.

title: Salaried GP - GP Reimbursement Scheme
descriptionHtml:
We are delighted to offer an opportunity for a Salaried GP to join our friendly and supportive team at St Hilary Group Practice under the 2026/27 GP Reimbursement Scheme.

We are looking to recruit a GP for 4 sessions per week, ideally working Monday, Tuesday afternoon and Thursday afternoon. There may be some flexibility in the working pattern for the right candidate.

The post is offered on an initial 6 month fixed-term contract , with the potential for extension beyond this date, subject to practice requirements and funding arrangements.

We are offering a salary in line with the BMA salaried GP pay range, NHS Pension Scheme membership and 6 weeks annual leave with bank holidays (pro rata).

In accordance with the agreed practice rota, the post holder will undertake the usual duties associated with the role of a Salaried GP, including

Face to face and telephone consultations

Assessment, diagnosis and management of acute and chronic conditions

Prescribing in accordance with local and national guidance

Effective management of long term conditions

Reviewing and acting upon investigation results and clinical correspondence

Processing referrals, prescriptions and associated clinical administration in a timely manner

Maintaining accurate and contemporaneous clinical records

Providing continuity of care where appropriate

Working collaboratively with the wider practice and multidisciplinary team

Participating in practice clinical meetings, audit and quality improvement

Undertaking occasional home visits where clinically required, although the majority are carried out by the PCN Acute Home Visiting Service

The post holder will be expected to work collaboratively with colleagues and contribute fairly to the clinical workload of the practice.

St Hilary Group Practice is a friendly and supportive PMS training and teaching practice in Wallasey, serving a patient population of just under 6,000.

Education and training are an important part of practice life. We regularly support GP Registrars and Foundation Doctors, as well as welcoming third-year medical students from the Universities of Liverpool and Chester for placements within the practice.

Our clinical team includes GP Partners, a Salaried GP, Practice Nurses, HCAs and a range of clinicians working with us through our Primary Care Network, including pharmacists, paramedics and other additional roles.

We are a proactive member of North Coast Alliance SDU (Wallasey PCN) and work closely with our PCN colleagues to develop and deliver services for our local patient population. This collaborative approach provides access to a wider multidisciplinary team and additional services.

We use EMIS Web as our clinical system and PATCHS to support our total triage model.

Our appointment system is designed to ensure that GP appointment requests are clinically triaged and directed to the most appropriate clinician or service. Triage is undertaken by a dedicated triage GP, supported by our reception team.

We are proud of our strong QOF performance and CQC "Good" rating. We have an experienced and supportive management and administrative team.

Provide emergency cover if needed

11,860 patient practice in a modern purpose built building

Team comprising 4 GP Partners, 3 Salaried GPs, a Nurse Practitioner, along with an experienced and diverse allied healthcare team. The Practice is also a GP Training Practice.

  • Fantastic support in place both clinical and administrative

title: CARE NAVIGATOR
descriptionHtml:
An excellent opportunity has arisen for a enthusiastic, experienced, Care Navigator with the ability to work well under pressure to join our friendly practice team with 4 partners and 9,100 patients. The post is for 21.5 hours per week - Tuesday 1.30pm - 6pm, Wednesday and Thursday 8.30am - 6.00pm (with a 1 hour lunch break). There is a requirement to remain flexible to cover colleagues who may be sick or on holiday.

To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception, secretarial and administrative duties and the provision of administration support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of information (electronic and hard copy) in a timely manner and assisting patients as required. To act as the central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with multidisciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers, in accordance with current polices, including the use of the electronic referral service (ERS).

This is a very busy practice with a supportive, committed team. The successful candidate will need to be able to cope well under pressure, prioritise and think on their feet.

Benefits include NHS Pension Scheme, free on-site parking, Blue Light Card Discount Scheme Membership (on application).

employer: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Consultant Obstetrics & Gynaecology with interest in EPAU, EGU
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Obstetrics & Gynaecology with interest in EPAU, EGU and resident on call

This post has arisen due to consultant expansion in the department. The post will enable us to maintain an adequate level of gynaecology activity against the background of a need for consultant cover of the labour ward and adequate supervision of the junior doctors required with the current curriculum. The post holder will be required to work in a hybrid rota including resident on call for obstetrics and gynaecology at the Women and Children's Hospital, Hull Royal Infirmary.

The on-call rotas are being reviewed with the planned consultant expansion, and it is highly likely the on-call element would change with further proposed expansion.

The post holder will participate in the resident consultant on-call rota for Obstetrics and Gynaecology at the Women and Children's Hospital, Hull Royal Infirmary. Consultant expansion is underway, and the on-call model is evolving towards a sustainable structure with dedicated resident obstetric consultant cover supported by separate consultant on-call provision for gynaecology.

The post holder will join a team committed to delivering safe, high-quality, consultant-led care in accordance with national standards. The post holder will be expected to contribute towards supporting specialist services such as Early Pregnancy Unit, Emergency Gynaecology and Ambulatory Gynaecology. Additional qualifications in Ultrasound are most welcome, and support offered to incorporate this valuable skill into departmental education for juniors& midwives& appropriate SITM provision.

Successful candidates would be encouraged to maintaining and improving governance within the department. The post holder may also be required to contribute to the Termination of Pregnancy service if they do not have a conscientious objection to providing this service.

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

title: Specialty Doctor in Acute Ophthalmology (CESR training opportunities)
descriptionHtml:
The Manchester Royal Eye Hospital Acute Service is one of the leading Ophthalmic Emergency Services within the United Kingdom and has a long history of leadership in this field nationally.

The successful candidates will be expected to work as part of a multidisciplinary team with the aim to expand the service further with innovative leadership, ideas, audit, and research projects.

It is anticipated that the successful applicants will already be a GMC registered Ophthalmologist and have passed the Part 1 FRCOphth and Refraction examination, with significant experience in Ophthalmology and a wish to complete their training through the 'Certificate confirming Eligibility for Specialist Registration' (CESR) route.

There is an expectation that the program will involve multi site working across Greater Manchester. The individual timetable will be matched by the CESR lead in conjunction with the needs of all the doctors on the rotation. In doing so the timetables will vary based on the subspecialty department the doctor is attached to. With each attachment there would be an expectation of undertaking acute referrals (including inpatients on different sites)/ emergency department sessions set within the doctor's program.

It would be expected that the successful candidates would possibly participate in the general ophthalmology 1st/2nd on call rota (approximately 1:9 with prospective cover and weekend working) and will be scheduled into the regional teaching on a Wednesday afternoon as part of SPA. Please note, this is 7 day service and the job plan might include working over the weekend and/or evenings.

Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) is a leading centre of clinical excellence, renowned for pioneering patient care, advanced medical research, and a collaborative multi-speciality environment. We are the largest provider of specialist services, and our Oxford Road Campus in Manchester is the largest health academic campus in Europe - a great place to progress your career.

With over 30,000 employees, a turnover exceeding £3 billion, and 10 hospital and community services, join our team to help us deliver outstanding healthcare to our diverse communities.We offer an engaging and supportive environment, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technology. Research and Innovation are at the heart of our work, offering opportunities to lead research that shapes the future of medicine, working alongside experts, advancing clinical practice, and improving patient outcomes.At MFT, we foster a culture where every colleague is valued and empowered to thrive. Your expertise is recognised, your ambitions are supported, and your impact is felt at every level. Whether you want to develop your clinical skills, pursue research interests, or seek leadership opportunities, MFT provides the ideal environment to achieve your medical or professional aspirations.If you are dedicated to driving clinical innovation and delivering compassionate patient care, join us to shape tomorrow's healthcare; where clinical excellence, innovation, and your career will thrive.

title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Hampton Surgery would like a GP to join our team.

We are a small surgery (4000 patients) that is growing in size and we pride ourselves on balancing continuity, traditional patient care and innovation.

We are set in a rural village location and we also care for patients at three traveller sites and a 50 bedded care home. We run patient information evenings and try to take a pro-active role in the small village of Hampton-in-Arden. Our patients are supportive and appreciative. employer: Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Paediatric Dermatology (Part-Time- 5 PAs) Vascular
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen within the Paediatric Dermatology Department at Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children for a 5 PA Consultant Paediatric Dermatologist post. The successful candidate will provide high-quality outpatient clinics for children with complex dermatological conditions and will contribute to inpatient dermatology reviews, ward referrals and the ongoing management of admitted patients. They will play a central role in the management of complex vascular anomalies, including the use of systemic and novel therapies, as well as in the care of a wide range of other paediatric skin disorders. In addition, they will undertake laser treatment for complex dermatological conditions.

The successful candidate will participate in multidisciplinary team meetings with colleagues from paediatric dermatology, histopathology, genetics, plastic surgery, interventional radiology and other paediatric subspecialties, contributing expert input to the management of complex cases. They will also participate in the 1:4 paediatric dermatology on-call rota, providing senior clinical advice and support.

Applicants must be on the GMC Specialist Register in Paediatrics or Paediatric Dermatology, or be within six months of CCT in Paediatrics at the time of interview. Applicants applying via the Portfolio Pathway (formerly CESR) must be on the Specialist Register in Paediatrics or Paediatric Dermatology at the point of application.

Applicants must have extensive experience in paediatric dermatology, including the management of complex and emergency presentations. They must also have extensive experience in the management of patients with complex vascular anomalies, including the use of systemic and targeted therapies, and experience in independently performing laser treatments in paediatric dermatology patients. Please see the person specification for further information.Based in central London, GOSH offers flexible working, support with childcare and travel, excellent training and development opportunities, and assistance with finding accommodation.

If you wish to discuss the role further, please contact Dr Mary Glover, Consultant Paediatric Dermatologist, at mary.glover@gosh.nhs.uk.

All applicants are strongly encouraged to apply electronically via www.jobs.nhs.uk. We welcome applications from all sections of the community.

GOSH is committed to recruiting the best person for the job, based solely on their ability and individual merit as measured against the criteria for the role; through a process that is fair, open, consistent and free from bias and discrimination.

We are committed to being a diverse and inclusive employer and foster a culture where all staff are valued, respected and acknowledged. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, age, disability status or length of time spent unemployed.

We particularly welcome applications from BAME communities, people with disabilities and/or long-term health conditions and LGBT+ community members.

We have policies and procedures in place to ensure that all applicants and employees are treated fairly and consistently. We are proud to be accredited as a Disability Confident Employer, a member of Business Disability Forum and a Stonewall Diversity Champion.

We have active and Executive supported BAME, LGBT+ and Allies, Disability and Long-Term Health Conditions and Women's staff networks. Staff networks are employee-led groups formed around interests, issues and a common bond or background. Staff network members create a positive and inclusive work environment at Great Ormond Street Hospital by actively contributing to the Trust's mission, values and efforts specific to inclusion. All of our staff networks are open to any employee.
