employer: The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust
title: Post CCT Fellowship in Sarcoma Surgery
descriptionHtml:
This post is intended for surgical trainees who wish to dedicate further time to training in specialist surgical oncology. For this reason this post is likely to be most suitable for those who are at the latter stages of or have completed their Specialist Training Programme. The successful applicant will work on the Soft Tissue Sarcoma (STS) and malignant melanoma (MM) units at The Royal Marsden Hospital.

Approximately eight hundred new cases of STS are referred to the RMH every year and are treated by a multidisciplinary team. All new cases are reviewed at a weekly multidisciplinary meeting where management is discussed. This provides the Registrar with an unparalleled experience. Surgical management includes soft tissue tumours of the limbs and limb girdle, intra- abdominal and trunk, and minimally invasive surgery where appropriate. About 5% of these patients will require reconstruction of skin and soft tissue. There will be opportunities for clinical research and the preparation of papers for presentation and publication.

Similarly, there is a multidisciplinary team handling patients with malignant melanoma. There will be ample opportunities to learn techniques of lymph node dissection, isolated limb perfusion and laser vaporisation of in-transit metastatic melanoma, and the administration of intra-lesional therapies.

The unit provides a diagnostic service for patients referred under the suspicion of sarcoma through a series of linked diagnostic centres in the region who initially assess patients and suspicious cross-sectional imaging is reviewed in a dedicated diagnostic MDT on Friday morning. Patients with likely diagnoses of sarcoma then brought for assessment at the Royal Marsden. The successful applicant will be involved in this diagnostic pathway.

The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust is a world-leading cancer centre. Our role is to offer our patients the best cancer care available anywhere in the world, and to continue to make a global contribution to finding better ways of diagnosing and treating cancer. We employ over 4,500 staff in a diverse range of careers including nursing, medical, science, radiography, pharmacy, occupational therapy, finance and administrative services. We have two hospitals - one in Chelsea, London, and one in Sutton, Surrey - as well as a Medical Daycare Unit in Kingston Hospital.

At The Royal Marsden, we deal with cancer every day, so we understand how valuable life is. When people entrust their lives to us, they have the right to demand the very best. That's why the pursuit of excellence lies at the heart of everything we do.

At the heart of the hospital is our dedicated team. We offer a stimulating and dynamic working environment, a wide range of staff benefits, learning and development opportunities and clear career pathways. There are opportunities to work flexibly across a range of areas and specialities and we welcome flexible working requests from point of hire to support employees work life balance. We are looking for employees who aspire to excellence, share our values and can play a crucial role in our on-going achievements.

employer: Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Consultant Interventional and Diagnostic Radiologist
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a candidate interested in a consultant radiologist post to join our team at Barking Havering, and Redbridge University Hospital Trust.

We are looking for an enthusiastic consultant to join our well established, dedicated and supportive radiology team to serve a population of 750,000.

The post holder will be primarily located at Queen's/ King George Hospital, Romford, but may require working at Barking CDC at Barking and St. George's CDC at Hornchurch.

The post holder is expected to:

is expected to share an office with another colleague with access to a PACS reporting station.

is expected to provide general Interventional Radiology across trust sites.

is expected to report cross-sectional images performed on the MRI and CT scanners at the CDC centres, King George's and Queen's Hospital.

contribute to the general duty roster and hot reporting sessions.

is expected to contribute to the specialist and general MDTs with other colleagues in rotation.

is expected to share an on-call commitment with existing IR consultants.

is expected to have, a PC and in addition a reporting workstation for remote access to images for on-call purposes

To adhere to the appropriate clinical and quality standards, liaise effectively and on a timely basis with colleagues, general practitioners, community services and all healthcare agencies and maintain and promote team and multi-disciplinary working.

To maintain confidentiality about sensitive data as per Trust's information governance guidelines.

  • To make use of physical skills in carrying out roles and responsibilities wherever appropriate.
  • To make judicious use of the resources and systems made availableby the Trust.

To participate in the development and implementation of policy and/ or management of radiology services.

To attend and participate in departmental governance meetings including investigations of incidents and audits where necessary.

To attend and participate in operational and clinical meetings where these are deemed essential to the running of the department and/or service.

To acquire and maintain the required level of evidence-based practice within your area of special interest.

To comply with all the trust and departmental policies in relation to job planning, appraisal and leave.

To deputize for an absent consultant or associate specialist colleague on occasions where this is necessary to complete core services in a timely manner.

We're an organisation that is getting better and better and our improvements are driven by a determination to deliver care we're proud of and our patients are happy with.

They are benefitting from a new electronic patient record (we were the last acute trust in London to introduce one) and our maternity services have been rated good by the Care Quality Commission.

We operate from two main sites - KGH in Goodmayes and Queen's Hospital in Romford. We have two busy emergency departments with more than 346,000 people visiting them last year. We're campaigning to secure the £35m we need to transform the A&E at Queen's and get rid of corridor care.

We're proud of our regional Neurosciences Centre, Radiotherapy Centre and Hyper Acute Stroke Unit. We're also part of the North East London Cancer Alliance.

We run a Women's Health Hub in Ilford; an Ageing Well Centre in Hornchurch; and Community Diagnostic Centres (CDC) at Barking Community Hospital and at St George's Health and Wellbeing Hub. These CDCs are open 12 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The majority of our 8,400 staff - who come from 146 different countries - live in the three diverse London boroughs we serve and are from black, Asian and minority ethnic groups. Many can work flexibly and more than 400 of them are on our Ofsted accredited apprenticeship programmes. We're proud to be a London Living Wage employer.

title: Pharmacy Technician
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen to work as a Pharmacy Technician in our Churchill, Canbury, Orchard and Berrylands Primary Care Network (CCOB PCN). We care for approximately 50,000 patients, based in four practices across the borough of Kingston; this role will be based at The Churchill Medical Centre and The Orchard Practice.

This is a unique opportunity for an enthusiastic and dynamic Pharmacy Technician with excellent communication skills to join us. We already work with a team of prescribing clerks and a clinical pharmacist across our practices and are keen to expand our team. The role will support the practice teams within our network to ensure the delivery of safe, effective and efficient systems for repeat prescribing, medicines optimisation, reducing medicines waste and maximising patient outcomes. The Pharmacy Technicians will work alongside prescribing clerks and clinical pharmacists as well as with the GPs and Nurses based in the practices.

employer: Doncaster & Bassetlaw Teaching Hospitals NHS FT
title: Clinical Fellow in Anaesthesia with Interest in Bariatric Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
This new post is a permanent Clinical Fellow post in Anaesthesia, offering an excellent opportunity for a highly motivated and enthusiastic doctor to join a friendly and well-established Anaesthetic Department.

The post is designed for doctors seeking to consolidate and further develop their clinical experience in preparation for application to ST4 Anaesthesia training.

At DBTH we offer a Tier 3 Weight Management Service, including access to specialist Bariatric surgery. A small group of senior anaesthetists undertake these operating lists most weeks, mainly at our Bassetlaw site. From an anaesthetic perspective these lists offer the opportunity to learn more about safe anaesthesia for patient's living with obesity; including managing the high risk airway, intra operative care of the bariatric surgical patient and opiate sparing analgesia strategies. As severe obesity is becoming more prevalent in our patient population, the skills learnt in these lists can then be applied to a wide range of surgical specialities.

Where service needs allow, elements of daytime clinical work can be tailored to support the candidate's individual interests and career goals, including the development of subspecialty experience.

The department provides a supportive environment with structured supervision, training opportunities and clear pathways for development and progression.

The Clinical Fellow will:

Provide safe and effective anaesthetic care across theatres, critical care and obstetrics

Participate in elective and emergency operating lists

Contribute to the management of patients within critical care units

Provide obstetric anaesthesia including labour ward and emergency cover

Participate in the full shift on-call rota, including nights and weekends

Work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team

Where service needs allow, there will be opportunities to tailor daytime clinical activity in line with the candidate's interests, including exposure to subspecialty areas such as critical care, obstetrics, trauma, vascular, paediatrics or pain.

The post includes:

A minimum of one consultant-attached list per month to support supervised learning and development

Allocation of a dedicated Clinical Fellow supervisor, with regular meetings to support portfolio development, career planning and progression toward ST4.

Attendance at weekly consultant-led anaesthetic teaching sessions

Provision of 1 Supporting Professional Activity (SPA) per week (equivalent to 4 hours) for study, portfolio development, audit and professional development

Additional responsibilities include:

Supporting service delivery across all Trust sites

Participating in clinical governance, audit and quality improvement activity

Supporting teaching and training of junior doctors and multidisciplinary staff

Doncaster & Bassetlaw NHS FT is one of Yorkshire's Leading acute trusts, serving a population of more than 420,000 across South Yorkshire, North Nottinghamshire, and the surrounding areas. Our services are based over three main hospital sites employing over 6,000 colleagues.

It is our goal to give those who join Team DBTH the tools and opportunities to grow their career, so whether you spend just one year or fifty with us, it's our pledge to help youDevelop,BelongandThrive,Here.

As an organisation that supports flexible working, we want to be sure that you can work in a way that is best for us and for our patients, and for you. Speak to us about how we might be able to support a flexible working arrangement. If it works for the service, we will do our best to make it work for you.

As an equal opportunities employer, we encourage applicants from all sectors of the community, particularly from under-represented groups including those with disabilities, members of our ethnic minorities and LGBTQ+ communities.

We offer a range of benefits including:o Extensive range of learning opportunitieso NHS Pension Schemeo Generous holiday entitlement in line with Terms & Conditionso Comprehensive health and wellbeing supporto NHS Car Lease schemes and a range of salary sacrifice schemeo Discounts on restaurants, getaways, shopping and finance through external providers.

employer: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
The UHDB Dermatology Department is looking to recruit two full-time Consultant Dermatologists to join our team as part of an exciting expansion of the service.

There are three vacancies available within the team: two posts primarily based across the FNCH/Derbyshire sites and one post primarily based across the QHB/Staffordshire sites.

While all successful candidates may be required to work across sites in line with service needs, each role has a designated primary base location.

Please clearly state your preferred site base (FNCH/Derbyshire or QHB/Staffordshire) within the supporting information section of your application.

A prospective Job Plan will be agreed with the successful candidate, setting out their clinical commitments, responsibilities and objectives, alongside appropriate time for teaching, research, education and managerial responsibilities.

The Job Plan will include a clear schedule of commitments and agreed personal objectives linked to the wider priorities of the Dermatology service. The support required to enable the successful delivery of these objectives will also be agreed through the job-planning process.

Maintenance of the highest clinical standards in the management of a Dermatology Service

To share with colleagues responsibility for the day-to-day management of the Dermatology Service.

Teaching & training of junior staff, medical students

To participate in NIHR portfolio studies

To actively participate in both departmental & Trust matters concerning Clinical Governance & audit.

To have responsibility for ensuring active participation in continuing medical education (CME).

Further information about the role can be found in the attached Job Description. We encourage applicants to read these carefully before applying.

As a trusted organisation at the heart of our communities, we recognise the important role we can play in supporting the public, patients, our own people and local partners in achieving the best of health for the local population and the communities in which they live by providing Exceptional Care Together

Our fundamental Values of Compassion, Openness and Excellence underpin how we intend to work as a Trust and the associated behaviours are becoming embedded in all aspects of how we work.

In return we will offer:

o Development opportunities, including both professional and leadership developmento On-going support through every step of the way from recruitment to when you join our team and beyond.o A variety of other staff benefits including employee assistance programme, discounted gym membership, onsite fitness classes, car schemes

Key Facts about our Trust:

o We see on average 4810 OP appointments per day.o We are the 4th busiest Trauma & Orthopaedic outpatients department in England - an average of 2077 per week.o An average of 1115 patients are seen in A&Es across our network every day - 3rd largest in the country.o Our hospitals admit an average of 195 emergency patients daily.o Last year we undertook almost 33,700 planned surgical operations in our 57 operating theatres.o We are one of only 7 Trusts nationally with more than 50 operating theatres.o We carry out more than 140 elective procedures each working day.

title: Consultant in Acute Medicine *With up to £28k Bonus*
descriptionHtml:
Acute Medicine is an essential pillar of urgent care at UHBW. We have ambitious plans to grow the service at Weston General Hospital with the expansion of our Acute Medical Unit, Same Day Emergency Care Unit, and optimising clinical pathways.

You will have a unique opportunity to lead and shape the future of the service. You will be joining an enthusiastic, collaborative multi-disciplinary team that is committed to driving forward the Trust vision for Acute Medicine.

Our service is comprised of a 28 bedded Acute Medical Unit (Sandford Ward), Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) unit, Waterside 16 Bedded General Medicine and the Medical Take in Emergency Department. Part of the Weston General Hospital team, we work closely with colleagues in the Emergency Department, Care of the Elderly, Respiratory Medicine, Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Surgical and Trauma & Orthopaedics specialities. We work closely with colleagues within Bristol hospitals and would be happy to review cross site working arrangements.

As well as joining a welcoming, talented team in a beautiful town, we offer:

Competitive recruitment and retention incentives of up to £20K (pro-rata for fixed term posts)

Relocation allowance and support of up to £8K (in line with Trust Relocation policy)

Negotiable job plans up to a maximum of 12PAs

Ability to pursue specialist interests e.g., research, teaching, leadership, and cross-specialty working.

The successful candidate will provide clinical leadership and direction for the multi professional team in the management of the acute medical patients. It is expected that they will lead ward rounds, direct the management of patients, perform practical procedures, teach both junior medical and other staff, attend multidisciplinary meetings, take part in the governance activity of the department, participate in the management and administration of the service and liaise with other professionals both within and outside the Trust as required.

University Hospitals Bristol & Weston NHS Foundation Trust (UHBW) is one of the largest acute Trusts in the country, with a workforce of over 13,000 staff and 100+ different clinical services across 10 sites, serving a population of over 500,000 people across Bristol and Weston. UHBW has been rated by the CQC as 'Good' overall and our staff are proud to deliver excellent care to patients. As a forward-thinking multi-award-winning Trust, committed to improving patient care, our world-leading research and innovations are having a positive local and global impact.

Join us and you can enjoy city living, be in the countryside or by the seaside, with easy access to all the Southwest offers. UHBW is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults.

As an equal opportunities' employer, actively working towards a diverse workforce, we aim to create a workforce that represents the diversity of our community and are committed to designing our services around the needs of patients and their loved ones. Anonymous information will be used from your application to ensure we're meeting our pledge.

employer: Ashford & St. Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:
This is an ideal opportunity for a post CCT candidate to work and gain experience in a medium sized District General Hospital.

title: Locum Consultant Medical Oncologist
descriptionHtml:
There is an exciting opportunity to join the dynamic Oncology Team at Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust and Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust, in a locum role covering Neuroendocrine and GI oncology in a growing service in Northwest London. ICHT is the regional cancer centre for an inner North West London population of approximately 2 million and is the largest recruiting centre to clinical trials in this sector.

This is a new additional post due to expansion of clinical activity, and to support research priorities for the trust. This post as per current job plan would ideally suit a medical oncologist although expressions of interest from clinical oncologists with a specialist interest in systemic anticancer treatments for these tumour sites, would also be welcome. This post is a new post, locum for one year, with a view to substantive appointment.

The Trust offers specialist care for almost all cancers (excluding paediatrics and sarcoma) and is a lead site for the National Gestational Trophoblastic Disease service (only one of 2 centres in England). There is a 50% component of the work at both ICHNHST & Frimley Health NHS Foundation and 50% ICHNHST. The former consists of working on the King Edward VII (outpatients) Windsor, & Wexham Park Hospital sites. The rest of the weekly responsibilities are out-patient clinics at Hammersmith Hospital (with occasional Charing Cross site for the inpatient care rotation shared by all consultants).

This 10PA post will:

Work collaboratively with the ICHT NET team across oncology, surgery, endocrine and nuclear med teams to provide care to patients of Northwest London and wider networked units

support the delivery and management of the GI medical oncology service for Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust

Work collaboratively, offering cross cover, recruitment to and assessment of trials, active metastatic disease & complex case discussion with Prof Rohini Sharma for NET and Prof Harpreet Wasan for GI oncology

Offer support and training to all non-consultant grade doctors within the unit.

Boost the departments research output

At Imperial College Healthcare you can achieve extraordinary things with extraordinary people, working with leading clinicians pushing boundaries in patient care.

Become part of a vibrant team living our values - expert, kind, collaborative and aspirational. You'll get an experience like no other and will fast forward your career.

Benefits include career development, flexible working and wellbeing, staff recognition scheme. Make use of optional benefits including Cycle to Work, car lease schemes, season ticket loan or membership options for onsite leisure facilities.

We are committed to equal opportunities and improving the working lives of our staff and will consider applications to work flexibly, part time or job share. Please talk to us at interview.

title: Lead GP - Broadmead Medical Centre
descriptionHtml:
Shape the Future of General Practice at Broadmead Medical Centre. Join an Award-Winning City Centre Practice and Lead a Team Making a Real Difference.

Broadmead Medical Centre is looking for an experienced and inspiring Lead GP to provide clinical leadership within our vibrant city centre practice. Serving a richly diverse patient population, this is an exciting opportunity to combine clinical excellence with dedicated leadership time, helping shape the future of patient care, workforce development and service improvement.

Working closely with our Primary Care Operations Manager, Lead Nurse and Deputy Medical Director, you will play a pivotal role in supporting our multidisciplinary team, driving quality improvement and fostering a positive, inclusive culture where both patients and colleagues can thrive.

Please Note: Sponsorship is not available for this role

Why Join Our Team?

Make a Meaningful Impact

  • Lead a practice serving a diverse patient population, including young professionals, students, refugees, asylum seekers, people experiencing homelessness and those with complex health and social needs.
  • Help reduce health inequalities and improve access to high-quality healthcare for underserved communities.
  • Influence how care is delivered and developed within an organisation committed to innovation and patient-centred care.

A Genuine Leadership Opportunity

  • Enjoy a blended role combining clinical practice with protected leadership time.
  • Provide visible and supportive leadership to GPs and the wider multidisciplinary team
  • Shape service development, quality improvement initiatives, clinical governance and workforce development.
  • Work alongside an experienced and supportive Practice Leadership Team.

Supportive, Collaborative Culture

  • Be part of a multidisciplinary team including GPs, Advanced Nurse Practitioners, Pharmacists, Physician Associates, Social Prescribers and Nursing colleagues.
  • Benefit from regular leadership meetings, clinical discussions and protected team time.
  • Work within an organisation that values relationship-based leadership, collaboration and continuous learning.

Professional Development and Influence

  • Develop your leadership experience within a respected and growing social enterprise.
  • Support and mentor colleagues, trainees and future clinical leaders.
Recognising Your Value
  • Competitive salary (£106,900 - £115,000 pro rata), NHS pension, enhanced pay rates, and medical indemnity cover.
  • Full-time role for 37.5 hours per week, but we would also welcome applications from candidates seeking part-time hours.
  • Generous annual leave entitlement (30 days + bank holidays) plus additional study leave.

You'll combine your clinical expertise with a passion for improving services, helping us respond to the needs of our patients while creating an environment where staff feel valued, supported and able to do their best work.

This role would suit someone who enjoys building strong relationships, working collaboratively and making a positive difference beyond their own clinical sessions. Whether you're already in a leadership position or looking for your next challenge, you'll have the opportunity to help shape the future of Broadmead Medical Centre and leave a lasting impact on both patients and colleagues.

We welcome applications from candidates seeking part-time hours andare happy to discuss flexible working arrangements.

title: Junior Locally Employed Doctor in Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:

title: Radiology Academy Subspecialty GU Curriculum Lead
locations: Flexible across the North West Region, United Kingdom
descriptionHtml:
The Subspecialty Curriculum Lead will oversee the coordination and delivery of the School's Academy curriculum within the defined radiology sub-specialty. This will be specific to the core training years from ST1 - ST3.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

title: Trust F2 in Trauma and Orthopaedics
descriptionHtml:

title: Locum Consultant Physician in General Medicine

employer: Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant - Interventional & Diagnostic Radiologist
descriptionHtml:

The post holder will be primarily located at Queen's/ King George Hospital, Romford, but may require working at Barking CDC at Barking and St. George's CDC at Hornchurch.

is expected to share an office with another colleague with access to a PACS reporting station.

is expected to provide general Interventional Radiology across trust sites.

is expected to report cross-sectional images performed on the MRI and CT scanners at the CDC centres, King George's and Queen's Hospital.

contribute to the general duty roster and hot reporting sessions.

is expected to contribute to the specialist and general MDTs with other colleagues in rotation.

is expected to share an on-call commitment with existing IR consultants.

is expected to have, a PC and in addition a reporting workstation for remote access to images for on-call purposes

Clinical / operational responsibilities To adhere to the appropriate clinical and quality standards, liaise effectively and on a timely basis with colleagues, general practitioners, community services and all healthcare agencies and maintain and promote team and multi-disciplinary working.

To maintain confidentiality about sensitive data as per Trust's information governance guidelines.To make use of physical skills in carrying out roles and responsibilities wherever appropriate.To make judicious use of the resources and systems made availableby the Trust.

To participate in the development and implementation of policy and/ or management of radiology services.

To attend and participate in departmental governance meetings including investigations of incidents and audits where necessary.

To attend and participate in operational and clinical meetings where these are deemed essential to the running of the department and/or service.

To acquire and maintain the required level of evidence-based practice within your area of special interest.

To comply with all the trust and departmental policies in relation to job planning, appraisal and leave.

To deputize for an absent consultant or associate specialist colleague on occasions where this is necessary to complete core services in a timely manner.Please check attached JD for full details of the main duties

We're an organisation that is getting better and better and our improvements are driven by a determination to deliver care we're proud of and our patients are happy with.

They are benefitting from a new electronic patient record (we were the last acute trust in London to introduce one) and our maternity services have been rated good by the Care Quality Commission.

We operate from two main sites - KGH in Goodmayes and Queen's Hospital in Romford. We have two busy emergency departments with more than 346,000 people visiting them last year. We're campaigning to secure the £35m we need to transform the A&E at Queen's and get rid of corridor care.

We're proud of our regional Neurosciences Centre, Radiotherapy Centre and Hyper Acute Stroke Unit. We're also part of the North East London Cancer Alliance.

We run a Women's Health Hub in Ilford; an Ageing Well Centre in Hornchurch; and Community Diagnostic Centres (CDC) at Barking Community Hospital and at St George's Health and Wellbeing Hub. These CDCs are open 12 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The majority of our 8,400 staff - who come from 146 different countries - live in the three diverse London boroughs we serve and are from black, Asian and minority ethnic groups. Many can work flexibly and more than 400 of them are on our Ofsted accredited apprenticeship programmes. We're proud to be a London Living Wage employer.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist Integrated Care Team Older People (West)
descriptionHtml:
We are delighted to offer an excellent opportunity for a full-time Consultant Psychiatrist to join Humber's established Hull Integrated Care Team for Older People (HICTOP). This is a rewarding and influential role based within the City of Hull, with clinical responsibility for the West Hull Community Mental Health Team.

This post carries no inpatient responsibility, though the successful candidate will benefit from access to three well-established inpatient facilities serving Hull and the East Riding.

What You'll Be Doing

As a key member of our service, you will:

  • Provide medical leadership within a highly skilled, supportive multi-disciplinary team.
  • Contribute to the ongoing development and innovation of the team's clinical approach.
  • Participate in the specialist Consultant on-call rota for Old Age Psychiatry and Learning Disability.

What We Offer

  • A minimum of 2.5 Supporting Professional Activities (SPAs) as standard for a full-time post.
  • Flexibility to explore additional SPA time for activities aligned with the Trust's wider ambitions.
  • An excellent peer support network.
  • Opportunities to become a clinical supervisor and further professional development.
  • A generous relocation package to ensure a smooth and supported transition into your new role and community

If you're passionate about shaping outstanding mental health care for older people and are looking for a role where your leadership truly makes a difference, we would love to hear from you.

About You

We're looking for someone who is committed, forward-thinking, and dedicated to high-quality patient care. You will need:

  • Full GMC registration.
  • MRCPsych UK or an equivalent postgraduate qualification.
  • Inclusion on the Specialist Register for Old Age Psychiatry, or to be within 6 months of CCT in Old Age Psychiatry.

We think differently about our psychiatry roles and will work with you to develop an opportunity that works for you. We will support you to balance high quality patient care with pursuing your own special interests within psychiatry, as well as offering opportunities for management and leadership roles.

Whether your focus is on developing your skills for management, research, teaching or innovative service provision, we are here to listen and understand how we can support you to reach your goals.

We are an award winning and CQC rated good health and social care Trust delivering integrated services across Hull, East and North Yorkshire.Find out more on our website

We are a forward thinking and dynamic Trust with a real commitment to staff development. We value our colleagues and invest in them to ensure they have the right skills to deliver outstanding care.

We are proud to score above or equal to the average for all NHS People Promise theme areas demonstrating our commitment to improve the experience of working in the NHS for everyone. Wherever you work we know you will receive a warm welcome and all the support you'll need to get you started.

We recognise the positive value of diversity and promotes equality whilst challenging discrimination. We welcome and encourage job applications from people of all backgrounds.

Work life balance is about having influence and flexibility over when, where and how you work. If the work pattern for this role does not meet your needs, we welcome an application and are happy to discuss working arrangements that differ from those advertised.

We offer a unique range ofbenefitsthat go above and beyond other NHS Trusts including an enhanced leave package and health and wellbeing support.

From city to countryside, market towns to moors you'll find a place to call home including some of the most affordable places to live in the UK.

title: Salaried GP 4-sessions
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a 4 sessionSalaried GPto join our large, friendly and supportive practice in South Bristol.

Bridge View Medical is an established practice and Primary Care Network in its own right. We have 4 sites in South Bristol all close to the bustling harbourside and vibrant North Street.

With c39,000 patients cared for by a wonderful team of 150 dedicated Partners and staff, we pride ourselves on being a larger practice with all the benefits this has to offer while still retaining a friendly and supportive culture.

We are a teaching, training and research practice and recently became the proud recipient of South Bristol Academy Teaching Practice Award for our outstanding contribution to medical teaching.

We operate a personalised patient list offering continuity of care as we strive to provide quality patient care and job satisfaction for our staff.

As well as carrying out a full range of GP services, you will have the opportunity to develop special interests and run clinics such as minor ops, womens health, diabetes & menopause clinics

We are a 14 Partner and 26 Salaried GP practice, supported by a large team of Pharmacists (many of whom are prescribers), Physios, Paramedics, Dietitian, Physician Associates, ANPs, Nurses and HCAs. Most visits are carried out by our extended clinical team.

We have dedicated admin support including a docman team and a pharmacy hub for prescription queries together with an excellent team of Care Coordinators responsible for triaging and patient bookings.

We are rated "Good" by CQC in all areas and rated "Excellent" as a training practice.

employer: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: Trust Doctor (Emergency Department)
descriptionHtml:
We have an exciting opportunity for a Trust Service Post Doctor, for a fixed term contract starting immediately in the Emergency Department.

The successful applicants will join an enthusiastic team that supports and delivers a modern, comprehensive emergency service. A small, friendly department with big ideas and a commitment to improving our service by embracing change and innovation.

This is a great opportunity to gain broad clinical experience between foundation and specialty training in a beautiful part of the country.

For more detail about the main duties of this role, please see the job description section below. As a key member of the Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, you will be joining an exceptional team working together to help our patients to stay healthy, when they need it most.

Stretching across Northern, Eastern and Mid Devon, we have a workforce of over 15,000 staff, making us the largest employer in Devon. Our core services, which we provide to more than 615,000 people, cover more than 2,000 square miles across Devon, while some of our specialist services cover the whole of the peninsula, extending our reach as far as Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly.

We deliver a wide range of emergency, specialist and general medical services through North Devon District Hospital and the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital (Wonford).

Alongside our two acute hospitals, we provide integrated health and social care services across a variety of settings, including community inpatient hospitals, outpatient clinics, and within peoples own homes. We also offer primary care services, a range of specialist community services, and Sexual Assault Referral Centres (SARC).

Our state-of-the-art equipment, leading technologies and strong links to local universities put us at the forefront of research and innovations, enabling us to provide world-class care to our local communities.

Its never been a more exciting time to join the Royal Devon, as youll help to shape our services as we continue along our integration journey.

title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Cardiology Electrophysiology and Devices
descriptionHtml:
This is a new post of Clinical Fellow that supports our very busy electrophysiology service in both adult and paediatric electrophysiology. The post is whole time and at ST6+ level on the Specialist Registrar scale. The job will be split between the Bristol Royal Hospital for Children and the Bristol Heart Institute. The 2 hospitals are on the same grounds with physical links between them. The Bristol Royal Hospital for Children is the Regional Centre for Paediatric Cardiology & Congenital Cardiac Surgery for the Southwest and South Wales. The Bristol Heart Institute similarly serves patients from across the region, including adults with congenital heart disease, requiring complex electrophysiology procedures and devices.

It is envisaged that the post-holder will contribute to the electrophysiology service, including catheter ablation and devices, as well as inherited cardiac conditions. The post holder is expected to undertake a research/audit project during the fellowship and may have an opportunity to participate in the SpR out of hours On Call Cardiology (or Peadiatric Cardiology) service. The post holder will be expected to work in close collaboration with the Consultant Electrophysiologists as well as having close liaison with other disciplines, particularly the cardiac physiologists and arrhythmia nurses.

Shortlisting details and interview arrangements will be communicated via email therefore please ensure you check your email account regularly.

The successful applicant will be appointed as a senior fellow in cardiac electrophysiology and devices. The work programme will include up to 6 weekly sessions in the adult and paediatric EP/devices cath lab in rotation with all the EP consultants, at least one weekly paediatric EP clinic, and one admin session. The post holder will also be required to provide inpatient EP consultations for paediatric and adult patients. In addition to the clinical activities, there will be a whole day equivalent dedicated to audit and research. It is expected that the appointed fellow will undertake clinical audit and will supervise more junior doctors undertaking EP audits. Furthermore, the fellow will be required to set up and run a research project during his post. Finally, there is an educational EP meeting that runs every Friday morning and it will be the responsibility of the fellow to organize that meeting activity with the EP lead. The fellow will also be expected to contribute to the monthly arrhythmia teaching sessions to the paediatric cardiology department.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust brings together more than 28,000 staff to deliver over 160 clinical services across thirteen hospital locations,operatingfrom three main sites at Southmead, Bristol citycentreand Weston.

With an annual turnover of £2.3 billion, we are now one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom. Our hospitals are spread across Bristol and Weston, join us and you can enjoy the very best of both worlds; city living within a stone's throw of the countryside or beside the seaside, both with easy access to all that theSouth Westhas to offer.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust values all people as individuals. As an equal opportunities employer actively working towards a diverse workforce we aim to recruit andretaina workforce whichrepresentsthe rich diversity of the local population at all levels and are committed to designing our services around the needs of individual patients and those around them. Anonymous information will be used from your applicationin order toensurewe'remeeting our pledge.

employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Junior Clinical Fellow in Neuro ICU
descriptionHtml:
This Junior Clinical Fellowship in Neurocritical Care offers a fantastic opportunity to gain knowledge, skills, and experience of working in a tertiary multidisciplinary team. It would be an ideal post for those at F3 level or Core Training who wish to strengthen an application for speciality training in the fields of Anaesthesia, ICM, Neurology, Neurosurgery, ACCS, or Emergency Medicine.

This 1 year fixed-term post offers plenty of supervised hands-on learning and teaching in Neurocritical care, with many opportunities to learn airway skills, central venous and arterial cannulation, and all other practical and theoretical facets on this busy but vibrant ICU.

The successful applicants will participate in twice-daily consultant-led ICU ward rounds, conduct daily clinical reviews of critically unwell patients, and be involved in all aspects of their daily medical care. Excellent teamworking, communication and documentation skills are required. There is plenty of opportunity for leaning and development of skills under expert supervision. The JCF will be part of the on-call team for the Neurosciences ICU, supervised at all times by the resident Airway doctor tier.

The Neurosciences Intensive Care Unit is a specialist tertiary-referral ICU within the West Wing, a wing of the John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford, UK. The John Radcliffe Hospital is a world-renowned teaching hospital integrating acute and elective services with clinical research and education. The Neuro-ICU works closed with Oxford Critical Care, the Major Trauma Centre, and the Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Specialist Surgery departments to provide both emergency and elective care to patients with intracranial or head and neck diseases.

The Neuro-ICU is a busy ICU but with a strong ethos of learning, equality, and multidisciplinary engagement. The Junior Clinical Fellows are genuinely welcomed and are an essential part of this Consultant-led team.

employer: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Cellular Pathology
descriptionHtml:
We have a vacancy arise for a Consultant post in Cellular Pathology. This will be based be based at Royal Blackburn Hospital. and is a full time, permanent post.

The working week will be - Monday-Friday 9am to 5pm with no expectation of providing on call for this post.

The successful applicant will join our team of consultants and will be required to provide a comprehensive histopathology service.

You will be expected to co-operate with other members of the Pathology Directorate to ensure effective administrative arrangements are made in the laboratory, which will include: -

  • Recruitment and appointment of junior medical staff, BMSs and secretarial staff having dealings with the histopathology department.
  • The arrangement of rosters of staff, the allocation of duties to them and their instruction in necessary organisational matters.
  • Co-ordination with staff in other professional disciplines and health care workers outside the hospital.
  • Attendance at Board meetings and other committees when pathology issues are being discussed and to participate in resource management.
  • Continuing management responsibility by agreement with other consultants in the Cellular Pathology Department, specifically for the service in their charge and for administrative duties associated with these services and the proper functioning of the department, though they may delegate certain responsibilities to the senior staff within the department.

Royal Blackburn Hospital is a major referral centre for HPB, Head & Neck and Urology Cancer Services and we also receive cancer resections from Colorectal, Breast and Gynae Units. It is a national screening unit for Bowel cancer screening patients. The Department is recognised for 4 Cellular pathology STs and in addition supported by 2 Senior Clinical Fellows.

Applicants are expected to be experienced in all aspects of histopathology and non-gynae cytology and there are opportunities to develop special interests although experience in breast, urology, colorectal and skin pathology would be more beneficial to the post.

Our Hospital is situated close to the motorway networks and at close proximity to beautiful countryside of Ribble Valley and the Lake District and is 40 minutes away from Manchester.

title: Specialist Grade Doctor in Community Sexual and Reproductive Health
descriptionHtml:
This is an 8 PA NHS Specialist Grade Doctor post in Community Sexual and Reproductive Health. The Post Holder will be employed by Midlands Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust (MPFT). The post will be based within the Stafford and Branston Sexual Health Services.

We are seeking to recruit a Specialist Grade Doctor who demonstrates experience of leadership in SRH as well as a wide experience in all aspects of CASH and GUM. Strong team-working skills and a keen interest in training, education and service development are essential.

This post will act as the Contraception Lead for the services and provide high-quality evidence-based holistic care for patients with sexual health needs incorporating both contraception and GU medicine.

The Post-Holder will be required to play a leadership role within the sexual health teams. There will be a significant commitment to teaching, including CoSRH training, and supervision of junior medical and nursing staff.Active contribution to audit and clinical governance will also be expected.

Midlands Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust Inclusion service offers psychological and drug & alcohol services, in the community, and in prisons, and has contracts across the country.

As an organisation we serve a population of 1.5 million and currently employ around 9000 members of staff.

We have a wide range of exciting opportunities for people looking to work in a truly integrated NHS organisation. By joining MPFT you will become part of a team who are empowered and supported to deliver care in a way which is consistent with our values:

  • Putting people at the heart of what we do
  • Empowering people to improve care and wellbeing
  • Delivering better health, better care in partnership

Please note: If you use Artificial Intelligence (AI) as part of your application, we encourage you to review the Trust's guidance on the use of AI within the recruitment process. Further information can be found on Join Us :: Midlands Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust or www.mpft.nhs.uk/joinus

Please note, we may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Parish Fields Practice is a friendly, established GMS practice serving around 8,500 patients in rural Norfolk. We are looking for aforward-thinking, friendly and team-focused Salaried GPto join our supportive and welcoming practice.

We are proud of the strong sense of teamwork across our practice. We believe that providing excellent patient care is a shared responsibility, and that staff should feel supported, valued and able to enjoy their working environment.

We are looking for a GP who shares this ethos and who will provide a high standard of clinical care while working collaboratively with colleagues across the practice and our wider Primary Care Network.

Whether you are an experienced GP or looking for a supportive environment in which to develop your career, we would love to hear from you.

We are looking for a GP who:

  • Provides a consistently high standard of patient-centred clinical care.
  • Works collaboratively and positively with colleagues across the whole practice team.
  • Has a flexible and approachable attitude and enjoys being part of a close-knit team.
  • Contributes to clinical discussions, practice development and quality improvement.
  • Is keen to work collaboratively with our wider Primary Care Network and the additional roles within it.
  • Supports a positive culture where colleagues look out for one another and share responsibility for delivering high-quality care.

Parish Fields Practice has a diverse and experienced multidisciplinary team, including a Nurse Practitioner, Clinical Pharmacist, Social Prescriber, Mental Health Practitioner & First Contact Physiotherapists, alongside our GP team, nursing, HCA, administration, reception and dispensary colleagues.

Teamwork is one of the things we are most proud of. Our clinical and non-clinical teams work closely together, with an emphasis on communication, mutual support and treating colleagues with the same respect that we aim to provide to our patients.

We also place a strong emphasis onstaff wellbeing. Our Practice Nurse leads a successful workplace wellbeing programme, which has included team days out, quiz nights, regular wellbeing lunches and other opportunities for colleagues to spend time together outside of the usual working environment.

Our GP Partners remain clinically involved and are approachable, supportive and valued members of the wider practice team. We believe that everyone has an important role to play, regardless of their position within the practice.

Our newly appointed Practice Manager is an experienced Advanced Nurse Practitioner, bringing a strong understanding of the clinical pressures faced by primary care professionals and the importance of creating a supportive environment in which clinicians can do their best work.

If you are looking for a practice whereteamwork, mutual support and staff wellbeing genuinely matter, we would be delighted to hear from you.

title: Consultant Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
Job description is pending Royal College approval

This is a substantive post for which 10 PA's are available.

This post would provide consultant psychiatric input to the team for the 10 PAs (6 PA's GMAIC, 4 PA's Crisis service) across the week. Out of hours, the consultant input comes from the medical on call rota. The post holder will join a dynamic and supportive Directorate and CAMHS Consultant peer group.

This is a new post, and the successful candidate will develop the role with the acute care team and liaise with the community CAMHS and inpatient services collaboratively.

Role Summary:

The consultant psychiatrist will provide medical oversight within which they will provide clinical consultation to the Crisis team and GMAIC for assessment, management and treatment of the young people who present with mental health disorder.

They will join the team and contribute to face to face assessments for complex, uncertain and significant risk presentations including YP requiring assessment under the framework of the mental health act and inform clinical judgments on appropriateness and suitability for admission to inpatient services. Where this not deemed to be clinically required or appropriate, they will provide guidance and make alternate recommendations including on the use of crisis services and offer follow up.

They will provide supervision to NMP within Crisis and GMAIC service.

The role will encompass collective working and strengthened relationships with community CAMHS and inpatients in Pennine and CAMHS services across Greater Manchester.

They will collectively work with adult mental services for transition of YP reaching 18 and require ongoing care.

They will liaise with Inpatient services, attend escalation meetings and provide second opinion to neighboring GMAIC teams when required.

A pivotal role is the need for excellent communication and liaison with key professionals providing an interface between community and inpatient services.

We are proud to provide high quality mental health and learning disability services, both inpatient and in the community across five boroughs of Greater Manchester - Bury, Oldham, Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside and Glossop.

Our vision is for a happier and more hopeful life for everyone in our communities and our staff work hard to deliver the very best care for the people who use our services. We're really proud of our#PennineCarePeopleand do everything we can to make sure we're a great place to work.

All individuals regardless of race, age, disability, ethnicity, nationality, gender, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, religion or belief, marriage and civil partnership are encouraged to apply for this post. We would also encourage applications from individuals with a lived experience of mental illness, either individually or as a carer.

employer: Lancashire & South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist - General Adult CMHT, Ribble Valley
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Psychiatrist - General Adult Psychiatry, Hyndburn and Ribble Valley CMHT (10PA)

We are seeking to recruit a substantive Consultant Psychiatrist in General Adult Psychiatry to work as part of the Hyndburn and Ribble Valley Community Mental Health Team (CMHT). This is a full time (10PA) post based at The Mount, Accrington. The post holder would be expected to participate on the Consultant On Call rota, for which additional remuneration would be payable.

The Hyndburn and Ribble Valley CMHT is one of six in Pennine Lancashire. You will be working as part of an MDT and would carry a compact caseload of the most complex and unstable cases, as well as supporting and advising other team members.

Applicants should hold full GMC registration and be included on the Specialist register of the GMC or they should be eligible for entry to the Specialist Register within 6 months of the interview date.

It is a requirement that applicants are Section 12 Approved at the time of commencing employment and have or are eligible to have Approved Clinician Status. Remuneration will be as set out in the terms of the New Consultant Contract according to previous experience.

The role:

At least 2.5 SPAs as standard for a full time post (we would be flexible in looking at enhancements to support other activities that support the wider ambitions of the Trust).

Excellent peer support group

Study leave budget of £3000 over 3 years or up to £5000 over 3 years for newly qualified Consultants

Opportunities to be a clinical supervisor

Relocation package available.

At our Trust, we're really keen to develop our Consultant workforce and nurture their areas of interest in a flexible way where possible. Come and have a chat with us about what your special interest or development area and build a suitable job plan with us. We also have an extremely active Medical Education department and support our Consultants in becoming Clinical & Educational Supervisors and nurturing their interests in this area. There are also opportunities to have a role in Digital Leadership if this is a passion for any of our Consultants.

title: Nursing Associate
descriptionHtml:
This role is being advertised on behalf of Littleborough Group Practice. The successful applicant will be directly employed by the Practice

Littleborough Group Practice is looking for an experienced Nursing Associate to join our nursing team on a fixed-term basis. The role is 15 - 20 hours per week, on Mondays and Tuesdays. It starts with an initial 3-month contract, with a view to extending for a further 6 months. We are also open to a long term, self-employed locum.

This post is for an experienced Nursing Associate who can confidently run long-term condition review clinics from day one. You must have at least 12 months post-qualification experience working in General Practice. Applications from trainee Nursing Associates, or from applicants whose General Practice experience is limited to training placements, will not be considered.

How to apply Please send your CV and a short covering statement to shaz.khan4@nhs.net. Your statement should outline your General Practice experience and which annual reviews you currently carry out.

Closing date: 30 November 2026. We may close the advert early if we receive enough suitable applications, so early applications are encouraged.

  • Carry out annual long-term condition reviews for patients with diabetes, hypertension, CKD, CHD, asthma and COPD, within your scope of practice and with escalation to the Practice Nurse or a prescriber where needed
  • Carry out learning disability and mental health annual health checks
  • Record clinical data accurately on EMIS using the appropriate templates, so that care meets QOF requirements
  • Phlebotomy, ECGs, blood pressure monitoring, foot checks, inhaler technique checks and other routine nursing tasks
  • Provide health promotion and self-management advice
  • Work with the wider clinical team to support recall and reduce care gaps
  • Follow practice policies on infection control, safeguarding, chaperoning and information governance

Littleborough Group Practice is a GP training practice in Littleborough, Greater Manchester, with around 8,500 patients. The practice is rated Good by the CQC. We are part of Pennines PCN and have a full multidisciplinary team, including GPs, an Advanced Nurse Practitioner, a Practice Nurse, a Minor Illness Nurse and a Healthcare Assistant. You will join a friendly, well-supported team that takes pride in good chronic disease management.

employer: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board
title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Neurosurgery
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen to join the Neurosurgical Department at Cardiff and Vale University Health Board as a Senior Clinical Fellow in Neurosurgery.

The successful applicant will join a busy tertiary neurosurgical service providing emergency and specialist care to patients across South and Mid Wales. Working alongside the consultant neurosurgeons and wider multidisciplinary team, the post offers broad experience in general neurosurgery, with opportunities to develop subspecialty interests according to the successful candidate's experience, development objectives and service requirements.

The role includes participation in consultant-led operating lists, outpatient clinics, ward-based care and neurosurgical multidisciplinary team meetings. The post holder will also participate in the middle-grade neurosurgical on-call rota.

The post is fixed term for 12 months and is not formally recognised as a training post. However, the successful candidate will have access to clinical and educational opportunities comparable with the doctors in training alongside whom they will work.

the post is available from February 2027 for 12 months.

The successful applicant will:

  • Provide clinical care for neurosurgical inpatients, including assessment, investigation, treatment planning and ongoing review.
  • Support the assessment and management of emergency and elective neurosurgical patients.
  • Attend consultant-led neurosurgical operating lists and outpatient clinics.
  • Participate in neurosurgical MDT meetings and other relevant departmental meetings.
  • Contribute to the middle-grade on-call rota for general neurosurgery.
  • Work effectively with consultants, resident doctors, nursing staff and the wider multidisciplinary team.
  • Participate in clinical audit, quality improvement and service-development work.
  • Contribute to the teaching of undergraduate medical students, nursing staff and postgraduate trainees.
  • Attend and contribute to the department's educational programme.
  • Maintain appropriate clinical records and undertake the administrative responsibilities associated with patient care.

The post holder will work with the department's consultant neurosurgeons across operating lists, clinics, MDTs and general clinical commitments. The JD also requires participation in teaching and the Neurosurgery on-call rota.

Cardiff and Vale University Health Boardis one of the largest Integrated Health Boards in the UK, employing over 15,000 staff, providing over 100 specialist services. Working across 6 hospital sites, we have a diverse range of career opportunities to offer. Serving around 500,000 people living in Cardiff and the Vale of Glamorgan, we are focussed on the health and care needs of our local population whilst working with our partners to develop regional services.

Our mission is"Caring for People, Keeping People Well",and ourvision is that every person's chance of leading a healthy life should be equal. As an organisation we are unashamedly ambitious for our population's health, rising to the challenges of today and tomorrow through our 10-year strategy, Shaping our Future Wellbeing. We are contributing to a healthier Wales with great emphasis placed on innovation and improvement, learning from around the world and leading the way in clinical research. Partnership working is strong at Cardiff and Vale, and we work closely with our staff and our community.

Cardiff, the thriving Welsh capital, is a fantastic city to live and work in with an abundance of sports, arts and cultural attractions. employer: Ashford & St. Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:

We are looking for 2 Consultants in Anaesthesia with specialist interests (please see JD) to join our talented and enthusiastic team of over 50 consultants and 10 specialty doctors, working in a friendly and flexible department. The opportunities have been created by a combination of replacement posts and service expansion.There is an on-call commitment included in this post, the supplement is 3%. Each session equates to 1.25 PAs. The job plan will be across St Peter's Hospital and Ashford Hospital cross sites.

Our vision is to create a centre of excellence, where staff have the opportunity to work in an environment of continuous learning and professional development. This role forms part of the Department of Anaesthesia where we are proud of our effective multidisciplinary team working between medical, nursing, management and support staff. We are also supported by a strong team of Staff grade, Associate Specialists, Middle Grade Fellows and Trainee Anaesthetists.

Our plans are ambitious, why not come and join our team?

Dr Toc Husain

Email: thusain1@nhs.net Tel: 01932 722153

INTERVIEWS WILL BE HELD IN PERSON ON 03/12/2026

The main duties for this role will be to:

- Deliver Clinical, Educational and Managerial Services of the highest professional standard at Consultant Level.

- Work with existing consultants and the multi-disciplinary team to provide a high quality well-led service for patients of Ashford & St Peter's, including the diagnosis, investigations, treatment and management of patients, in accordance with Trust policies and practices.

Ashford and St. Peters Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust serves a population of more than 410,000 people living in North-West Surrey, parts of Hounslow and beyond.

Our vision is to be one of the best healthcare Trusts in the country. There has never been a better time to join us in the NHS at ASPH. We are committed to providing continuous professional development and flexibility to shape our workforce around our patient care.

We are expanding our theatres at Ashford Hospital and moving towards this becoming our dedicated elective centre. We want to create a state-of-the-art centre for excellence for planned surgical procedures.

We can offer you the full range of NHS benefits/discounts and in addition:

  • Excellent pension scheme and annual leave entitlement
  • On-site Nurseries
  • On-site staff cafes
  • On-site parking
  • Support in career development

title: Consultant Paediatrician with Ambulatory and Critical Care
descriptionHtml:
Shape the future of acute paediatric care in one of the UK's most beautiful regions.

An opportunity has arisen for a Consultant Paediatrician with a specialist interest in Ambulatory and Critical Care to join our dedicated Acute Paediatric Team at Withybush Hospital. This is a rewarding role for a motivated clinician looking to combine excellent clinical practice with leadership, service development, teaching and research.

As a substantive Consultant within Hywel Dda University Health Board, you will provide high-quality, patient-centred care for children and young people across inpatient, outpatient, ambulatory and critical care services. You will serve as the Named Lead for Paediatric Ambulatory and Critical Care across all Health Board sites, working collaboratively with multidisciplinary colleagues to shape and develop services that meet the needs of our population now and in the future.This role offers the opportunity to make a real impact, contributing senior clinical leadership to the ongoing development and modernisation of Acute and Emergency Paediatric Medicine. Alongside your clinical responsibilities, you will have opportunities to support research, quality improvement, teaching and training, helping to develop the next generation of healthcare professionals while advancing paediatric services across the region.

As a Consultant Paediatrician with a specialist interest in Ambulatory and Critical Care, you will provide high-quality, patient-centred care for children and young people across Hywel Dda University Health Board. Working as part of a supportive multidisciplinary team, you will contribute to the assessment, diagnosis and management of patients requiring acute, ambulatory and critical care services, ensuring the highest standards of care are delivered.

You will play a leading role in the development of paediatric ambulatory and critical care services across the Health Board, helping to shape and enhance pathways of care that improve outcomes and experience for children, young people and their families. As the Named Lead for Paediatric Ambulatory and Critical Care, you will work collaboratively with colleagues across specialties, organisations and healthcare settings to support innovative and sustainable service delivery.

The successful candidate will provide professional leadership within the Acute Paediatric Service, contributing to clinical governance, quality improvement, service development and the delivery of national and local priorities. You will support a positive and inclusive working environment, working closely with colleagues to maintain high standards of clinical practice and staff wellbeing.

Hywel Dda University Health Board plans and provides NHS healthcare services for people living in Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire, and bordering counties.

We have over 13,000 staff and together we provide primary, community, in-hospital, mental health and learning disabilities services.

We work in partnership with the three local authorities, as well as public, private and third sector colleagues, including our valued team of volunteers.

Our services are provided in:

  • Four main hospitals: Bronglais Hospital in Aberystwyth; Glangwili Hospital in Carmarthen; Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli; and Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest
  • Five community hospitals: Amman Valley and Llandovery hospitals in Carmarthenshire; Tregaron Hospital in Ceredigion; and Tenby and South Pembrokeshire hospitals in Pembrokeshire
  • Two integrated care centres: Aberaeron and Cardigan in Ceredigion, and several other community settings
  • 47 general practices (six of which are health board managed practices); dental practices (including four orthodontic); 97 community pharmacies; 43 general ophthalmic practices; and 8 ophthalmic domiciliary providers
  • Numerous mental health and learning disabilities services

employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Hepatologist
descriptionHtml:
This locum consultant post has been established to provide dedicated clinical leadership and capacity within the Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) service, supporting the increasing demand associated with the diagnosis, treatment, and ongoing management of patients with primary liver cancer.

The postholder will work as part of the multidisciplinary hepatology, HPB surgery, oncology, radiology, and transplant teams to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care across the HCC pathway. They will contribute to specialist outpatient clinics, multidisciplinary team meetings, inpatient care, treatment planning, and surveillance programmes, ensuring timely access to investigation, diagnosis, and treatment in line with national standards and best practice.

The role will support service sustainability by improving outpatient capacity, reducing waiting times, enhancing continuity of care, and facilitating the delivery of specialist regional and tertiary HCC services. The postholder will also contribute to service development, quality improvement, clinical governance, teaching, and research activities, helping to strengthen the Trust's position as a leading centre for the management of liver disease and liver cancer.

This appointment will provide additional consultant workforce resilience while supporting the continued growth and complexity of the HCC service, ensuring patients receive safe, effective, and timely specialist care.

The post holders will provide a service to Liver Unit inpatients and outpatients and will support the Transplant Hepatology program as required. The HCC job post holder will be expected to perform weeks of on-call for transplantation (1 in 9) and contribute to regular ward cover as part of the ward team (1 of 5 member Consultant team).

1.Participate in Liver Unit outpatient activity with 3 clinics per week including the HCC clinic and post-liver transplant immunosuppression clinic. The other clinic will be a general Hepatology clinic or post LT HCC clinic.

2.Participate in the management of inpatients with acute and chronic liver diseases. This will include in-patient and out-patient assessment of patients with chronic liver disease undergoing evaluation for liver transplantation.

3.Provide specialist management and input to the HCC service and development of service of the transplant Oncology programme.

4.Participate in MDT meeting in Liver Transplantation, Cancer and Histology. Candidate will provide support specifically for the HCC MDT.

5.Be expected to participate in Liver Unit audit and postgraduate teaching programme.

6.Be expected to participate in clinical research as opportunities arise in sub-specialties such as liver transplantation, viral hepatitis, autoimmune liver diseases, portal hypertension, fatty liver disease, sarcopenia, cancer and portal hypertension.

7.Support the administrative activity of the Transplant Unit.

8.Formal role as Education lead

As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential. For those staff with a disability, including physical disability, long term health condition, mental health or neurodiverse condition, this also means being committed to making reasonable adjustments needed for you to carry out your role.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for enthusiastic GP to join our friendly and supportive practice

We have an opportunity for a salaried GP for 3 -4 sessions per week

Our supportive, collaborative team practice a traditional GP model, whilst still embracing innovation where it helps patients and staff. We are committed to high-quality, holistic care.

Main duties of the job
  • To work closely with your clinical peers and the wider practice team to deliver high-quality, holistic clinical care to our registered patients.
  • Manage your share of both Duty Doctor sessions and sessions consisting of a mix of acute, prebooked and telephone calls.
  • Managing all associated paperwork and admin, with time given to do so.
About us
  • Provide face-to-face, telephone and online consultations, including triage where required.
  • Assess and manage acute and chronic illness.
  • Prescribe safely and undertake medication reviews.
  • Review and act on test results, clinical correspondence and patient-related tasks.

  • Maintain accurate, timely clinical records and appropriate clinical coding.

title: Urgent Care Practitioner / ANP- General Practice
descriptionHtml:
The Panton Practice are looking to recruit a dynamic forward-thinking Paramedic Practitioner / Advanced Nurse Practitioner to join their expanding multi-disciplinary team. We are looking for a person with experience in dealing with acute minor illnesses. We operate on a system of e-Consultations, telephone triaging and same day face to face appointments.

The candidate would need to be able to provide evidence of autonomous practice and be comfortable in patient assessment, use of diagnostic equipment such as ECG to facilitate this and initiating treatment plans although full support will be accessible through the duty team on the day.

This role benefits from good communication skills, IT knowledge and the ability to multi-task, as well as be confident to work on their own, but also as part of a supportive and flexible team. Experience of SystmOne and working in the NHS would be an advantage but is not essential.

The Panton Practice is a large GP training practice

  • GMS list size around 17,000
  • 4 Partners, 3 Salaried GPs, 1 Advanced Nurse Practitioner, 3 Paramedic Practitioners, 2 Practice Nurses and all supported by our Reception and Admin team
  • Established training practice with registrars
  • Most recent CQC inspection, rated Good.
  • Free Parking
  • 30 minutes paid coffee break with all clinical staff in the morning
  • 15 minute appointments with double appointments for complex patients
  • Daily Duty Doctor support
  • Daily clinical supervision
  • Minimum 27 days annual leave, pro rata

Primary Care is evolving, and we are part of the Bournemouth Central Primary Care Network, working with our other local practices to offer further extended services both in and outside of our core hours. These include Physio, Pharmacists, Social Prescribers, Health Coaches and our Frailty Team.

We are a teaching practice for GPs and allied professionals and are developing a strong Multi-Disciplinary Team and feel this is key for better patient care. Every day is different, and you come across new challenges which makes it a very diverse environment. We work in a friendly atmosphere where social events happen throughout the year.

title: GPwSI or Specialty Doctor in Women’s Health
descriptionHtml:
This post offers an opportunity for a Specialty Doctor or GP with a Special Interest in Women's Health to contribute to the delivery and development of innovative group-based clinical carewithin aGeneral Practice setting.

title: Specialty Doctor  in Neurology
descriptionHtml:
We are excited to offer a fixed term Speciality Doctor post in Neurology, created to support the expansion of our service. This is an excellent opportunity to join our team who deliver high-quality neurological care across Hampshire.

About the Team: You will join a team of experienced Consultant Neurologists and a dedicated specialist nursing team with expertise in MS, MND, Parkinson's Disease, Epilepsy, and Neurorehabilitation. The role is supported by an administrative team.

Our vision is to provide outstanding care for every patient. Patient care is at the heart of what we do at our three sites: Basingstoke and North Hampshire Hospital, Royal Hampshire County Hospital in Winchester and Andover War Memorial Hospital. Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust provides medical and surgical services to a population of approximately 600,000 people across Hampshire and parts of West Berkshire.

Our cultural ambition is to have a culture that places people at the heart of all we do, where we all belong, and where learning, improvement and excellence thrive.

employer: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Junior Clinical Fellow - Upper GI and Colorectal
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Junior Clinical Fellow to join our dynamic team. This post will be based across both Chorley and South Ribble District Hospital and Royal Preston Hospital sites - This post is covering maternity leave until 25th July 2027.

This will be a rotational post including clinical duties within the Surgical Assessment Unit for emergency admissions for General Surgery, UGI and Colorectal working alongside the Surgical Advanced Clinical Practitioners, providing clinical assessment and decision making for undifferentiated surgical presentations and support from the Surgical Registrar and Surgeon of the Week Consultant.

There will be opportunity to attend the regular operating sessions of the Clinical Team to assist with major surgery and be trained in basic surgical skills under the close supervision of the Consultant. After a period of supervision, you will be able to assess new and follow up patients under the supervision of a Consultant.

Daily ward round at Chorley and South Ribble District Hospital or Royal Preston Hospital

Attendance at out-patient clinics at Preston and Chorley.

. Surgical Assessment Unit rotation

This post will be part of the 1 in 16 on-call general surgery rota at FY2-CT1/JCF grade level covering Preston and Chorley Hospitals.

Audit and research activities, participation in teaching and training activities for medical and clinical staff is expected.

Assessment of ward referral at Royal Preston and Chorley Hospitals.

Providing support to more junior staff eg FY1 and FY2/ Medical Students.

Weekly programme will typically include 1 clinic, 1 inpatient operative list and 1 diagnostic list.

Modern Education Centres are based at both Royal Preston and Chorley and South Ribble Hospital sites and offer excellent library and study facilities, including PC/Internet support for staff and students.

employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:
The post holder will be part of the genitourinary (GU) radiology team and deliver imaging and biopsy services across the Trust. The post holder will lead/take part in the multidisciplinary team (MDT) meetings. Additional subspecialty interests may be accommodated/supported,
