employer: East and North Hertfordshire Teaching NHS Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow in ENT
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a full-time post of Senior Clinical Fellow in Ear Nose and Throat (ENT) Surgery for 4 months 21 November 2026 to 31 March 2027). title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Saddleworth Medical Practice is looking for a salaried GP to join our supportive, well-established multidisciplinary team, caring for approximately 14,000 patients in a semi-rural setting.

We are a training practice with a strong commitment to learning, teamwork and high-quality patient care.

We offer:

  • Four sessions per week, working Friday plus either Wednesday or Thursday.
  • A 12-month fixed-term salaried position.
  • Salary dependent on experience.
  • Protected learning time.
  • An identified in-practice mentor.
  • Professional medical defence organisation membership fees paid by the practice.
  • Six weeks annual leave plus bank holiday entitlement, pro rata.
  • Paid study leave in accordance with the employment contract.

We welcome enquiries and informal visits from GPs interested in finding out more about the practice and the role.

Responsibilities will include:

  • Assessing and managing patients through face-to-face, telephone and video consultations.
  • Managing acute presentations and supporting patients with ongoing and complex health needs.
  • Undertaking home visits and contributing to duty responsibilities in accordance with the agreed job plan.

Our multidisciplinary team includes GP partners, salaried GPs, nursing and pharmacy colleagues, healthcare assistants and an experienced administrative team.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist (Medical Director Option Available)
descriptionHtml:

title: Joint Chief Medical Officer
descriptionHtml:
Pennine Care and Greater Manchester Mental Health are launching a joint programme to procure and implement a new Electronic Patient Record system. Given the scale and strategic importance of the programme our existing Chief Medical Officer will be seconded on a phased basis to provide executive clinical leadership. This has created a great opportunity for an aspiring Chief Medical Officer to join our Board.

The role will follow a phased increase in hours and accountability: 0.4 WTE from January to June 2027, focused on operational and internal medical leadership; 0.6 WTE from June to December 2027, with enhanced delegation for quality, workforce and governance; and 0.8 WTE from January 2028, progressively assuming strategic, Board, statutory and external responsibilities

You will be an exceptional and experienced medical leader committed to providing visible, values-led leadership during an important period of transition and transformation. You will work closely with the substantive Chief Medical Officer, Chief Executive, Chair, Board colleagues, clinical leaders and system partners to ensure that quality, safety, professional standards and medical leadership remain central to decision-making.

The job profile and supporting documentation provides a detailed overview of the phasing of responsibilities between the substantive Chief Medical Officer and incoming Joint Chief Medical Officer during the transition period.

You will be a medically qualified senior leader with current General Medical Council registration, appropriate specialist credentials and substantial experience at executive, board or system level. You will bring a strong record of leading quality, safety, medical workforce and organisational improvement in a complex healthcare environment. You will be collaborative, inclusive and decisive, with the credibility to engage medical colleagues and the ability to provide objective challenge and assurance at Board level.

We welcome applications from individuals seeking a temporary appointment, secondment or other mutually agreed arrangement alongside an appropriate clinical role within the Trust.

We are proud to provide high quality mental health and learning disability services, both inpatient and in the community across five boroughs of Greater Manchester - Bury, Oldham, Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside and Glossop.

Our vision is for a happier and more hopeful life for everyone in our communities and our staff work hard to deliver the very best care for the people who use our services. We're really proud of our#PennineCarePeopleand do everything we can to make sure we're a great place to work.

All individuals regardless of race, age, disability, ethnicity, nationality, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, religion or belief, marriage and civil partnership are encouraged to apply for this post. We would also encourage applications from individuals with a lived experience of mental illness, either individually or as a carer.

If you come and work for us we will offer a range of benefits and opportunities, including:

  • Generous annual leave entitlement for Agenda for Change and Medical and Dental staff.
  • Flexible working opportunities to support your work/life balance
  • Access to Continued Professional Development
  • Involvement in improvement and research activities
  • Health and Wellbeing activities and access to an excellent staff wellbeing service
  • Access to staff discounts across retail, leisure and travel

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Junior Clinical Fellow in Paediatrics (ST1-3)
descriptionHtml:
This post provides an excellent opportunity to gain ST1-3 level experience in paediatrics, including paediatric subspecialties, at a busy tertiary paediatric centre. It would suit someone looking to expand their paediatric experience in the UK prior to applying for training including FY3 experience. The post offers experience with a wide range of complex and interesting patients and an excellent teaching programme.

The post will be part of the general paediatric ST1-3 on call rota and will provide cover for different areas of paediatric medicine, including inpatient wards, our ambulatory unit and our children's emergency department. The post is a full shift pattern including daytime and out of hours working including night shifts.

Only candidates with relevant experience of paediatrics in the UK will be shortlisted for interview.

The post will be part of the general paediatric ST1-3 on call rota and will provide cover for different areas of paediatric medicine, including inpatient wards, our ambulatory unit and our children's emergency department. The post is a full shift pattern including daytime and out of hours working including night shifts.

St. George's Hospital is a large multi-specialty facility based in Southwest London, offering a wide range of adult, paediatric and neonatal services. It is co-located with a medical school - St. George's, University of London. Children managed at SGH are either local, or regional tertiary patients. There has been a steady increase in the number of paediatric attendees in the Emergency department, in inpatient emergency admissions and outpatient referrals for local children. This reflects the increasing young population in SW Thames. Tertiary children's services at SGH include endocrinology, gastroenterology, infectious diseases, neurology, oncology, allergy, paediatric surgery, PICU, trauma and respiratory medicine. The hospital is the second Trust in London with a helipad.

The department has its own outpatient's department, the Dragon Centre, a child development centre and 5 wards with 57 inpatient beds, a 10 bed PICU/HDU and 36 cot NICU. There are 35 paediatric consultants across all specialties and a fully staffed EWTD compliant middle grade and SHO rota, composed of grid trainees, regional trainees, fellows and F1 doctors.

title: CAMHS Consultant Psychiatrist, Coastal Community & Liaison (£45k RRP)
descriptionHtml:

title: Advanced Care Practitioner - Frailty
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a motivated and experienced Advanced Care Practitioner to join our PCN and work within our Frail Elderly Assessment Team (FEAT). This is an exciting opportunity to deliver high quality patient-centered care to frail patients in their own homes and in our care homes.

The role combines autonomous practice, care coordination, multi-agency collaboration, management of increasing frailty, dementia and end of life care.

The postholder will work at an advanced level of clinical practice, exercising a high degree of professional autonomy and accountability while working within the NMC code and national ACP frameworks.

Work using FEAT and champion evidence-base interventions

Conduct comprehensive geriatric assessments

Monitor medication use and adjust treatment plans as required

Exercise advanced clinical reasoning to diagnose, treat, and manage patients without direct input from a medical practitioner, recognising own professional boundaries and seeking senior clinical support when required.

Provide expert management of frailty syndromes

Escalate concerns appropriately

Identify when clinical presentations fall outside of scope of practice and escalate appropriately to senior clinicians.

Work closely with GPs, OTs, Physios, Care Co-ordinators, Social Prescribers and Community Nursing Team

Attend the MDT meetings and case reviews

Support patients and families

Promote lifestyle self management strategies to optimise health and independence

Carry out clinical decision making such as diagnosing

Completing proactive clinical management plans for care home residents

Conduct regular care plan reviews

Identify patients in need of palliative support and facilitate advanced care planning discussions with patients and families

Communicating and caring for patients who have reduced understanding and insight

Participate in weekly enhanced care home reviews

Undertake daily acute care home visits identifying clinical emergencies or deteriorating patients, ensuring appropriate action

Participate in regular clinical supervision and reflection discussions

employer: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist in Old Age Psychiatry - Easington
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity for an old age consultant psychiatrist to become involved with the Easington community service.

The community teams provide mental health assessments for people who have memory problems or who have other mental health problems requiring secondary care intervention in the locality. Approximately 70% of referrals to the teams are due to organic presentations, most commonly dementia. The team works with patients who are predominantly aged 65 and over. However, the service is defined on the basis of need rather than age, and so people with cognitive presentations who are aged under 65, as well as people younger than 65 who have significant frailty, may be open to the team.

The Clinical PAs are 7.5 PA across the week, to include a combination of clinics at the team base, and home visits.

There is the potential that the Consultant Psychiatrist could be asked to take on Responsible Clinician duties in relation to patients who are subject to Community Treatment Orders and are open to the team, though the number of such patients is expected to be very low.

The post-holder is expected to prioritise Mental Health Act Assessments for their own patients during working hours, and be a qualified DOLS Mental Health Assessor for any patients on their personal caseload. Occasionally, there may be ad hoc Section 49 Mental Capacity Act reports to prepare,

Therefore, it is necessary for the post-holder to have Approved Clinician, Section 12 and DOLS Mental Health Assessor Status, and support can be provided to attain the latter if the prospective applicant does not already hold this status. The postholder will be expected to have a familiarity with important relevant legislation affecting the care of older people with mental illness.

The Trust is eager to support the development of a special interest and this is negotiable either at the time of employment or at the Annual Job Plan Review meeting. The postholder will work with the Locality Manager, General Manager, Lead Psychiatrist and Associate Clinical Director to plan and develop the service in line with the Service Business Plan.

We are one of the largest specialist mental health and learning disabilities trusts in the country, with an annual income of £320m and a workforce of some 6,700 staff operating from around 100 sites in Durham, Teesside, North Yorkshire and York and Selby. We provide a range inpatient and community services to 2m people living in County Durham, the Tees Valley, Scarborough, Whitby, Ryedale, Harrogate, Hambleton and Richmondshire. We also provide additional specialist services to other parts of Northern England.

We deliver our services by working in partnership with eight local authorities and clinical commissioning groups, a wide range of voluntary organisations, as well as service users, their carers and the public.

Psychiatrists are essential contributors to the majority of our mental health teams. Service users expect and are justified to expect collaborative relationships with dedicated psychiatrists who work consistently as part of effective services. descriptionHtml:
University Hospitals Birmingham (UHB) is seeking one Consultant Ortho-Geriatrician to join one of the largest and most ambitious trauma and perioperative services in the UK.

A chance to make your mark

Join a growing, multidisciplinary fragility fracture and perioperative service at University Hospitals Birmingham. We are recruiting one Consultant Ortho geriatrician as part of a Board-supported expansion of care for older people undergoing surgery. This is an opportunity not simply to deliver excellent clinical care, but to help shape how that care is designed, evaluated and improved.

Our service manages approximately 1,000 hip fractures each year and brings together orthopaedic surgeons, specialist nursing, therapy, resident doctors and an expanding orthogeriatric workforce. You will have the support of experienced colleagues and the opportunity to build a sustainable consultant career with clinical, improvement, teaching and academic interests.

A service with momentum

Our recent NOF quality programme reported Q1 2026 crude mortality of 5.7%, with seven of eight NHFD indicators above the national average in the reported period. We are proud of the progress while remaining focused on timely surgery, mobilisation and the experience of older people and their families.

We have developed a curriculum-mapped orthopaedic education programme, with 97% of consultants registered trainers, and are investing in the trauma nurse practitioner workforce and redesigned resident doctor rotas.

Job Summary Continued:

Real-time feedback from 16 patients on Ward 18 was 100% good or very good in the August sample. We use this feedback to strengthen communication, discharge planning and compassionate, person-centred care.

Help us lead the next chapter

* Delirium: improve reliable 4AT assessment, prevention, recognition and management, drawing on learning from the NHFD 2026 report.

* Fragility fracture: strengthen multidisciplinary perioperative optimisation, early mobilisation, discharge and secondary fracture prevention, including fracture liaison pathways.

* Research and improvement: pursue audit, quality improvement and research questions in a high-volume service, with opportunities to work with colleagues across UHB and its wider academic environment.

* Education and leadership: mentor resident doctors and the wider MDT, contribute to governance, and develop a portfolio reflecting your strengths and ambitions.

The post holder will be part of the multi-disciplinary team approach to care with the specialty of Ortho-geriatrician and will be supported by Resident doctor team within Orthopaedics[TL1.1].   • Support planned one-to-one sessions, therapeutic groups and activities, helping patients work towards goals agreed with the multidisciplinary team.
  • Use calm, trauma-informed approaches to help patients manage distress.
  • Follow agreed care plans to support coping skills, reduce self-harm and minimise restrictive practice.
  • Support patients with meals and any associated distress where this is part of their care plan.
  • Help patients take part in community activities and Section 17 leave, following leave authorisations, risk assessments and agreed staffing arrangements.

Do you want to be part of an exciting new work stream to help improve the lives and wellbeing of others?

We are looking for a passionate and motivated individual to join our substance use service on a casual, as and when required basis. This flexible opportunity is ideal for a qualified non-medical prescriber looking to provide specialist prescribing and a range of clinical interventions, working alongside our recovery caseworkers to deliver an effective and comprehensive package of care to service users.

In this role you will:

Prescribe and review medication in accordance with evidence-practice and national and local protocols.

Identify and assess the suitability of service users for in-patient alcohol and opioid detoxification.

Assess physical and mental health needs.

Proactively support the preventions, identification, and treatment of blood borne viruses.

Support service users to adopt health promotion strategies that encourage healthier lifestyles.

Our Values are a critical element of our strategy to create a brighter future for Middlesbrough. They will be at the heart of everything we do and will be the foundation for how we operate, behave and make decisions. Having these values will help you be the best you can be and help Middlesbrough to grow and thrive.

employer: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Paediatric Cardiothoracic Anaesthetist
descriptionHtml:
We are delighted to be able to offer an opportunity for a highly motivated, ambitious individual to join our well-integrated team. The post is advertised as a locum appointment with a substantive advertisement to follow.

The successful candidate will be expected to provide anaesthesia for paediatric cardiothoracic and adult congenital cardio surgery (including transplantation and mechanical support). In addition, the congenital cardiac anaesthesia group provide services for cardiac cath labs, radiotherapy, ENT and bronchoscopy. There is also responsibility to provide anaesthesia for non-cardiac surgery in patients with congenital cardiac disease. The anaesthesia on call commitment is approximately 1:5 whole-time equivalents with prospective cover.

Within post there is a significant commitment to anaesthesia for adults with congenital heart disease and we work closely with our colleagues in the adult cardiothoracic anaesthesia and intensive care departments.

This is a full-time post to provide cover for Congenital Cardiac Anaesthesia. The workload is to a fully flexible annualised job plan.

For an informal discussion and further information regarding the opportunity and Directorate, please contact: Dr Cosmas Leong on 0191 21 39484, or via email at cosmas.leong@nhs.net or Dr Teresa Chila on 0191 2139521, or via email at teresa.chila@nhs.net

employer: East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Cardiologist in Complex Cardiac Devices
descriptionHtml:
This is a full-time 10 PA position, covering a one-year sabbatical, with additional sessions according to the post holder's skill set.

A typical week will include 2-3 sessions of device implantation, together with outpatient, multidisciplinary and other clinical activity reflecting the post holder's complementary specialist interest. For a candidate with expertise in heart failure, this may include heart failure clinics and multidisciplinary working with acute and community specialist nursing teams. For a candidate with imaging expertise, it may include cardiac MRI, cardiac CT or advanced echocardiography. The final job plan will be agreed according to the successful candidate's skills and the needs of the service, with activity delivered across Trust sites.

There is a 1:9 consultant of the week rota (including weekends), covering WHH and QEQM, and a 1:8 emergency pacing rota.

The successful candidate will be competent in complex cardiac device implantation and in the follow-up and management of patients with simple and complex devices. They will understand the recognition and management of device-related complications, including infection, and the indications and pathways for lead extraction.

Cardiac device implantation and the continuing development of the Trust's device service will form the principal specialist component of the post. The post holder will contribute to device multidisciplinary meetings, governance, service development, training and the introduction of newer implantation techniques.

The remainder of the specialist job plan will reflect the successful candidate's complementary expertise. A candidate with heart failure expertise may contribute to inpatient and outpatient heart failure care and provide clinical leadership and support to the established specialist nursing teams. A candidate with appropriate cardiac imaging skills may undertake cardiac MRI, cardiac CT or advanced echocardiography and contribute to the development of those services.

Complementary expertise in areas such as inherited cardiac conditions, maternal cardiology, adult congenital heart disease or cardio-oncology would also be welcomed where this supports a coherent job plan and the needs of the wider cardiology service.

We are one of the largest hospital trusts in England, with five hospitals and community clinics serving a local population of around 800,000 people. Our vision is 'great healthcare from great people'. Everything we do is guided by our values: 'People feel cared for, safe, respected and confident that we are making a difference'. We have a new way of working at East Kent Hospitals, called 'We care'. It's about empowering frontline staff to lead improvements day-to-day. We're looking for compassionate people to be part of our improvement journey for the patients, families and carers we care for every day.

Please note that if you require a Certificate of Sponsorship to work in the UK you must declare this on your application form, even if you currently have a certificate of sponsorship or a work permit for another role and are already working in the country. Please note we are only able to sponsor candidates for a Skilled Worker Visa for roles that are eligible at the time of application.

title: Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
HealthHarmonie, part of Medinet Group, is looking to recruit an experienced Consultant Dermatologist to join its growing community healthcare team on a permanent basis.

This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in delivering high-quality community dermatology services, working in partnership with the NHS to improve patient access, reduce waiting times and provide timely specialist care.

The successful candidate will be responsible for delivering dermatology outpatient clinics within a community setting. Key duties will include:

  • Assessing, diagnosing and managing patients presenting with a range of dermatological conditions.

  • Conducting new and follow-up outpatient consultations.

  • Developing appropriate treatment plans and advising on ongoing patient management.

  • Undertaking dermatological procedures and treatments within their scope of practice, where required.

  • Maintaining accurate clinical records and ensuring appropriate patient documentation.

  • Working collaboratively with the wider multidisciplinary team to deliver safe, effective and patient-centred care.

  • Ensuring compliance with clinical governance, safeguarding and patient safety standards.

Health Harmonie is one of the UK's leading independent healthcare providers, delivering high-quality NHS community services that improve access to specialist care and support the delivery of healthcare closer to patients' homes.

Working in partnership with NHS Integrated Care Boards, Trusts, Primary Care Networks and GP Practices, we provide consultant-led services across a range of specialties including Dermatology, Ophthalmology, Gastroenterology, ENT and Diagnostic Services.

Our focus is on delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care through innovative community pathways, reducing waiting times and improving patient outcomes. We combine clinical excellence with strong governance, modern technology and dedicated operational support to ensure the highest standards of care.

At Health Harmonie, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to creating a supportive and inclusive working environment where clinicians can thrive, develop professionally and make a meaningful difference to NHS patients. Through collaboration, innovation and a commitment to continuous improvement, we help transform the way healthcare is delivered within local communities.

Joining Health Harmonie offers the opportunity to be part of an organisation that is passionate about clinical quality, outstanding patient experience and delivering sustainable healthcare solutions across the NHS.

title: Consultant in Paediatric Stem Cell Transplantation and Haematology
descriptionHtml:
Are you ready to take the next step in your Consultant career, or looking for an exciting opportunity to broaden your experience in a leading specialist centre? Bristol Royal Hospital for Children (BRHC) is seeking a motivated, compassionate and ambitious Paediatric Bone Marrow Transplant Consultant to join our paediatric HSCT programme.

As one of Europe's leading children's hospitals, BRHC is renowned for delivering exceptional patient care, pioneering research and innovation. We are proud of our collaborative culture, commitment to excellence and dedication to improving outcomes for children and young people.

Our Paediatric Bone Marrow Transplant Programme was one of the largest in the UK, focussing particularly on transplant for paediatric malignancy. Following a period of closure related to staffing shortages we have now re-opened the unit and are seeking enthusiastic individuals to expand our transplant offer beyond patients from the South West of the UK. We are aiming to carry out approximately 25 allogeneic transplants annually. Individuals with expertise in stem cell transplantation, alongside other subspecialty interests would be welcome to apply. The job description is for a consultant with an interest in bone marrow transplantation and cytopenias, but for the right candidate we can be flexible with the details of the non-transplant component of the job plan (which is expected to be around 50% of the role).

We Are Looking For Someone Who:

  • Has specialist HSCT experience in line with the current 6th Edition JACIE/FACT Standards.
  • Has experience teaching and training registrars within the department.
  • Demonstrates strong clinical leadership when caring for children and their families.
  • Has excellent communication skills and enjoys working within multidisciplinary teams.
  • Is enthusiastic about service development and innovation in stem cell transplantation, cellular therapies and gene therapies.

This role includes participation in the Consultant on-call rota, including weekend commitments.

Join Our Team

This is an exciting opportunity to join a nationally recognised specialist service, help shape the future of paediatric transplantation and make a lasting difference to the lives of children and families across the UK.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust brings together more than 28,000 staff to deliver over 160 clinical services across thirteen hospital locations,operatingfrom three main sites at Southmead, Bristol citycentreand Weston.

With an annual turnover of £2.3 billion, we are now one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom. Our hospitals are spread across Bristol and Weston, join us and you can enjoy the very best of both worlds; city living within a stone's throw of the countryside or beside the seaside, both with easy access to all that theSouth Westhas to offer.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust values all people as individuals. title: Clinical fellow in Haematology and Oncology
descriptionHtml:
Clinical Fellow (F2/ST1-2) - Haematology and Oncology

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust are pleased to offer a position for a Clinical Fellow in Haematology and Oncology at the Bristol Haematology and Oncology Centre (BHOC).

The BHOC provides Oncology and Haematology services to the former Avon, Somerset and Wiltshire Cancer Network with a catchment population of approximately 2.2 million people. The BHOC houses D603, the inpatient oncology ward, D703, the inpatient haematology, BMT and IEC (immune effector cell therapy) unit and the regional teenage and young adult (TYA) inpatient unit, Area 61, as well as the Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) unit where we receive direct admissions of unwell haematology and oncology patients. The BHOC is also the home of the Radiotherapy department, chemotherapy day unit providing a full range of treatments, the University of Bristol Palliative Medicine group, BHOC Clinical Psychology, the TYA Day Unit and a large Clinical Trials Unit.

There is a 32 bedded Oncology ward incorporating 5 teenage and young adult (TYA) beds and two protected sealed/unsealed source rooms, an out-patient suite and a chemotherapy day unit and radiotherapy unit for oncology patients. The Haematology Unit consists of a 24 bedded ward and day units for patients with both malignant and non-malignant disorders. The Bristol Haemophilia Comprehensive Care Centre and Bone Marrow Transplant service are based on the unit.

Interview Date: W/C 23rd November 2026.

The successful applicant will join our ward teams, based in Oncology but will also have some time working in both areas and on our SDEC unit. The post holders will be required to contribute to the on call SHO rota in BHOC which is a mix of nights, long days, twilights and weekends at varying frequency throughout their time here at BHOC.

The successful applicant will assist in delivering the work of the Haematology and Oncology teams and will have the opportunity to contribute to continuing education, clinical governance and research within the Division, Directorate and Trust. The successful candidate will join existing teams who are enthusiastic and motivated.

employer: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust
title: Junior Clinical Fellow in Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The Emergency Department at the North Middlesex University Hospital has an annual attendance of 190,000 new patients. 27% of attendances are under the age of 16. Acute Medical and Assessment Units are in proximity to the department. There is an emergency Radiography Department adjacent to the ED which is staffed 24 hours a day. There is always A CT scanner available with excellent consultant-based radiology support. Full emergency laboratory facilities including a well-resourced point of care testing room are available. There is a significant trauma workload; the department is part of the London trauma network. The department receives nearly 20% of its workload as ambulance borne. The department has a philosophy of comprehensive patient care where the initial management of the patient is undertaken in the ED and the patient then handed over to in-patient teams. There is an excellent relationship with the in-patient teams with seamless referrals. The case mix has the highest acuity in the Northeast Thames region with preponderance towards medically unwell patients.

The successful candidate will be expected to be fully involved in all aspects of the work of the Accident & Emergency Department under the supervision of the consultant in charge, to whomhe/she will be responsible.The clinical duties include all those that are normally expected in any major Emergency Department, and the below is not an exhaustive list of responsibilities in this role;Provide and maintain a high standard of care for all patients in the EmergencyDepartmentTo review and appropriately manager patients presenting to the EmergencyDepartment, with senior support as required.To ensure that all Trust standards are maintained to ensure a high quality of care to all whoattend any and all services provided by North Middlesex University Hospital NHS Trust.Maintain accurate patient documentationEnsure that patient confidentiality is always adhered to.

The Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK's biggest and most innovative trusts. Our dedicated army of staff care for over 1.6million patients, treat more than 200,000 in A&E, deliver over 8,000 babies and carry out more than 17million tests.

Our size, scale and influence offer you unrivalled career opportunities and a forward-thinking approach to working that works around your lifestyle. From flexible hours and generous benefits, to next level training, we make it easier to take your career to the top

employer: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Paediatrician
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity to join the specialist Paediatric Palliative Care Teamand play a key role in the development of paediatric palliative and end-of-life care services across Birmingham and the West Midlands. The post combines direct clinical care for babies, children and young people with life-limiting conditions with the opportunity to support service development across the Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin (STW) footprint.

Working alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team of consultants, specialist nurses and family support staff, the post holder will contribute to the delivery of high-quality symptom management, advance care planning and holistic family-centred care across hospital and community settings.

This is a 5 PA locum consultant post offering a unique opportunity for an established paediatrician with an interest in palliative care to further develop specialist knowledge and skills within an accredited training centre. Depending on experience, there may be opportunities to work towards paediatric palliative medicine SPIN competencies under consultant supervision.

Applicants must hold full GMC registration with a licence to practise and demonstrate the skills and experience required to work at consultant level within paediatrics.

The successful candidate will join a specialist paediatric palliative care service for babies, children and young people with life-limiting conditions across Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust and the wider West Midlands. Working alongside the existing consultant and specialist nursing team, the post holder will support children with malignant and non-malignant conditions across both hospital and community settings with particular emphasis on the STW footprint.

The work will be in conjunction with and under the supervision of the existing Consultant body. The post-holder will deliver symptom management, advance care planning and end-of-life care, whilst working closely with multidisciplinary teams, community services, hospices and other partner organisations. The post will ideally suit someone with experience of palliative care and children with severe neuro-disability and complexity. The post holder will also contribute to service development, education and the ongoing delivery of high-quality specialist paediatric palliative care across the region.

More information included within the JD.

Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust is the first of its type in the UK. Our Trust was formed in February 2017 to drive forward our commitment to provide the highest quality, world-class physical and mental health care for our women, children and families. Uniting our hospitals means more seamless care; more investment to make greater advances in our specialist treatment and world-leading neo-natal and fetal work. Importantly, it also gives us a greater voice in shaping the future of family-centred care.

Birmingham Children's Hospital is a UK leading specialist paediatric centre with an international reputation in several areas.

Birmingham Women's Hospital is one of two dedicated women's hospitals in the UK, with the busiest single site maternity unit, delivering more than 8,200 babies a year offering a full range of gynaecological, maternity and neonatal care.

Our Trust is committed to creating the best place to work. We believe in promoting and enhancing inclusion, diversity and equality and encourage applications from all areas of the community, who meet the criteria for the role, regardless of age, gender identity, disability, race, religion or sexual orientation.

title: Trust Grade Doctor - Older Peoples Service (Reed Ward)
descriptionHtml:
Are you a post-Foundation doctor looking to build a career in psychiatry? Join Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust as a Trust Grade Doctor and gain exceptional experience within our older peoples inpatient ward based at Julian Hospital, Norwich.

The Trust is seeking a Trust Grade Psychiatry doctor (Clinical Fellow/Core trainee level (CT1-CT3) to join the Older Peoples Mental Health Inpatient Services at The Julian Hospital, Bowthorpe Road, Norwich on Hammerton Court.

The Julian Hospital is a mental health hospital with 70 beds for older people situated on Bowthorpe Road in Norwich.

There are five inpatient wards at the Julian hospital. The functional wards are Sandringham ward (male) and Blickling(female).

Apply now and take the next step toward a rewarding future in mental health care!

This is a Trust Grade post aimed at doctors who are equivalent of CT1-3 trainees in terms of experience. The post holder will provide day-to day psychiatric and physical health reviews of the patient group under the care of a consultant psychiatrist. The post holder will be an integral member of the multidisciplinary team and be involved in all aspects of the service work including attending relevant meetings.

There are also opportunities to observe assessments in other settings. The post provides an excellent opportunity for doctors with an interest in training in Psychiatry.

Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust provides child and adult mental health services, learning disability, wellbeing and eating disorder services across Norfolk and Suffolk.

We are also offering:

  • Dedicated SPA time of up to 25% of working hours
  • £2000 annual paid study leave (on application and approval) in addition to CPD
  • NHS benefits package including contributory pension, redundancy. Including paid annual leave, sick leave and maternity leave.
  • Appraisals and revalidation completed by the Trust
  • Friendly Colleagues

employer: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Otology Fellow
descriptionHtml:
University College London Hospitals is seeking to appoint an Otology Fellow who has a commitment to high-quality patient care, innovative service models, delivery of performance targets, and excellence in education/training. This is a 12 month fixed term contract.Informal enquiries about the post are welcome. Please contact Mr Azhar Shaida (ashaida@nhs.net) ENT Consultant and Clinical Lead for Auditory Implants; or Nadeem Bashir (nadeem.bashir@nhs.net) General Manager, Surgical services at RNEDHEDH

The full shift working pattern is arranged across a rota cycle of 14 weeks

This post provides advanced otology and auditory implant surgery. This would suit a post-CCT trainee who would like to gain more experience in the field of otology and auditory implants. Previous extensive operative experience in this area would enhance the training opportunities for the successful applicant. This post is not recognised for training by the SAC in Otolaryngology but applications for recognition of training will be fully supported.This provisional job plan is subject to agreement and change.

The post holder will, under the clinical supervision of Mr Azhar Shaida, be responsible for the provision of specialist ENT services to the Royal National Throat Nose and Ear Hospital. This will include:

a) Diagnosis and treatment in the specialist clinics they attendb) Actively participate in the departmental researchc) To carry out specialist Otology lists in the event of theatre availability due to consultant leaved) Ability to educate and carry out surgical training to specialist otological trainees

University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UCLH) is one of the most complex NHS trusts in the UK, serving a large and diverse population. We provide academically led acute and specialist services, to people from the local area, from throughout the United Kingdom and overseas. Our vision is to deliver top-quality patient care, excellent education, and world-class research.

We provide first-class acute and specialist services across eight sites:o University College Hospital (incorporating the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing)o National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgeryo Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitalso University College Hospital Grafton Way Buildingo Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicineo University College Hospital Macmillan Cancer Centreo The Hospital for Tropical Diseaseso University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street

We are dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of many complex illnesses. UCLH specialises in women's health and the treatment of cancer, infection, neurological, gastrointestinal and oral disease. It has world class support services including critical care, imaging, nuclear medicine and pathology.

We are committed to sustainability and have pledged to become a carbon net zero health service, embedding sustainable practice throughout UCLH. We have set an ambitious target of net zero for our direct emissions by 2031 and indirect emissions by 2040.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Garland House Surgery is looking for an enthusiastic and motivated Salaried GP to join our friendly, supportive and well-established team.

We are looking for someone who combines sound clinical judgement with a compassionate, patient-centred approach and a genuine enthusiasm for delivering high-quality general practice care.

Whether you are embarking on your GP career as a newly qualified GP or bring many years of experience, we would be delighted to hear from you.

We are a long-established and highly regarded GP training practice with premises in Darfield and Wath-upon-Dearne, serving a patient population of over 10,000. We operate a total triage system and offer 15-minute GP appointments, supporting thoughtful clinical decision-making and quality patient care.

The position is for 6 sessions per week, working Monday, Tuesday and Friday.

We pride ourselves on being a supportive and forward-thinking practice and would welcome the opportunity to introduce you to our team.

Main duties of the job

  • Deliver safe, effective, and evidence-based care to our diverse patient community.

  • Provide consultations through a mix of telephone, online, and face-to-face appointments.

  • Contribute to achieving practice priorities such as QOF, Enhanced Services, and local health initiatives.

  • Take part in clinical meetings, audits, and ongoing learning sessions.

  • Maintain clear, accurate, and up-to-date clinical records.

  • Work collaboratively with our multidisciplinary team, including ACPs, Practice Nurses, HCAs, and PCN staff.

  • As a teaching practice, support the learning and development of medical students and GP registrars by participating in supervision and teaching activities.

    • Are you looking for an opportunity to join a supportive, forward-thinking and highly regarded GP training practice?

    We are an established and well-respected training practice operating across our premises in Darfield and Wath-upon-Dearne. With a patient list of over 10,000, we pride ourselves on delivering high-quality, patient-centred care within a friendly and supportive working environment.

    We offer:

    • 15-minute GP appointments, allowing you to provide considered, high-quality patient care.
    • A total triage model, supporting effective workload management and appropriate patient access.
    • A supportive and experienced clinical team.
    • The opportunity to work within a long-established GP training practice.
    • Convenient locations with excellent transport links, just 10 to15 minutes from both the M1 and A1.

    We are passionate about providing excellent patient care while supporting our clinicians to enjoy a healthy work-life balance and develop professionally.

    If you are an enthusiastic, motivated GP looking to become part of a welcoming and progressive practice, we would love to hear from you.

employer: Practice Plus Group - Health in Justice
title: General Practitioner - Out of Hours
descriptionHtml:
UNLOCK YOUR BEST WORK LIFE

+ MAKE A DIFFERENCE TO EVERY LIFE

We have an exciting opportunity for a General Practitioner to join our Receptions team at HMP Dovegate. HMP Dovegate is a category B remand Prison located in Staffordshire. Within this role you will be working in receptions supporting the intake of new patients into the prison. You will work closely with the multi-disciplinary team including the substance misuse nurses, and early days mental health team to deliver high quality healthcare services. Suitable applicant for this role must have experience and feel confident prescribing controlled substance.

Hours

Monday to Friday: 16:00 - 20:00

Saturday: 12:00 - 16.00

We offer individual 4-hr sessions or a combination of sessions to suit your needs.

Salary

This position is parttime,you'll receive an annual salary up to £125,693 per annum FTE - depending on experience.

How will we support you?

  • Bespoke induction, including our Introducing Health in Justice training course
  • Competency framework
  • Regional and national career development opportunities
  • Our bespoke Learning Management System to address your learning needs
  • Support from the wider team

Candidates are required to have a Legal right to work in the UK and due to the nature of the role, offers of employment will be subject to additional vetting and security checks.

Our General Practitioners are extremely valued and are well respected members of the Prison Healthcare community, as a General Practitioner, your responsibilities will vary. You will

  • Deliver first class healthcare to a diverse group of patients, and therefore as a General Practitioner at Practice Plus Group you get the opportunity to further develop your knowledge in areas you wouldnt usually experience within a practice, or even A&E environment.
  • Provide clinical assessment and diagnosis to patients requirements and make timely decisions regarding future management.
  • Provide a highly specialist resource to other members of the healthcare team at site, as well as the patients you work with having active
  • involvement in clinical governance and effectiveness activities.
If you are interested in career development, we have a wide range of opportunities for you to develop your skills and experience, which include both internal and external options for development and learning.

It doesn't stop there we also offer:

  • Discounts on shopping and leisure activities
  • Support to grow in your role and continue your professional development
  • 24/7 employee assistance helpline and financial assistance when you need it

The Health in Justice team at Practice Plus Group makes a real difference across over 53 prisons, young offenders and immigration removal centres. Were the UKs leading independent provider of NHS services to over 40,000 patients in secure environments, always putting their needs first, regardless of their background.

Practice Plus Groups purpose is to Unlock your best work life and we stand by our core values:

  • We treat patients and each other as they would like to be treated
  • We act with integrity
  • We embrace diversity
  • We strive to do things better together
We are looking for caring, compassionate but also driven professionals who can help us drive our vision for a fair and inclusive healthcare access to all.

Requirements

  • MBChB or MBBS
  • Inclusion on the GMC Register and GP Performers List
  • Evidence of engagement with annual appraisal
  • Experience working as a General Practitioner in community general practice
  • Evidence of continuing professional development
  • Ability to work with patients with a history of substance misuse
  • RCGP Certificate in Substance Misuse 1 and 2, or prepared to undertake these qualifications
Secure environments are one of the most challenging, yet rewarding places for healthcare professionals to work. If you're looking for a role where you can develop your existing healthcare skills and learn something new every day in an environment that never stands still, then this could be the right opportunity for you.

title: Nursing Associate
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a caring, enthusiastic, and motivated Nursing Associateto join our friendly practice team. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a family-friendly General Practice where patient care, teamwork, and staff wellbeing are at the heart of everything we do.

Working alongside our experienced team of Practice Nurses,Healthcare Assistants (HCAs), GPs, and wider multidisciplinary colleagues, you will support the delivery of high-quality, compassionate care to our patients. The role is ideal for someone who enjoys building relationships with people, supporting patients to improve their health and wellbeing, and working as part of a close-knit team.

The hours for this role are 27 hours per week covering Mondays, Thursdays and Fridays.

As a Nursing Associate, you will work closely with our Practice Nurses and HCAs to support the delivery of a wide range of nursing services and health promotion activities. Duties may include:

  • Undertaking clinical observations including blood pressure, pulse, height, weight, and BMI measurements.
  • Supporting the nursing team with chronic disease management and patient reviews.
  • Carrying out ECGs, wound care, simple dressings, and other delegated clinical procedures within your scope of practice.
  • Supporting vaccination and immunisation programmes following appropriate training and competency assessment.
  • Providing health education and lifestyle advice to patients and their families.
  • Maintaining accurate clinical records and contributing to high standards of patient care.
  • Assisting with infection prevention and control procedures and maintaining clinical equipment and supplies.

At Sutton Manor Surgery we are awelcoming and patient-focused GP practice serving the local community. We are proud of our friendly and supportive culture, where every member of the team plays an important role in delivering outstanding care to our patients.

Our nursing team works closely together, creating a positive environment where staff are encouraged to develop their skills, share knowledge, and support one another. We value work-life balance, wellbeing, and continuous professional development, and we are committed to helping our staff thrive in their roles.

We are looking for someone who shares our values of kindness, respect, teamwork, and excellence in patient care, and who wants to make a real difference to the health and wellbeing of our community.

title: Consultant in General Adult Psychiatry - Outpatients
descriptionHtml:
Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to make a substantive whole time appointment to this newly established post with Oldham Mental Health Services. This post will cover the Central sector within the Oldham area. The post has been created due to the current consultant moving to another job in the trust.

The Oldham general adult psychiatry service (generally for people aged 16 to 64) has been run since 2008 according to a model whereby our team of consultants are deployed as follows: Three consultants work exclusively in the community and outpatient focus areas, one working with the Early Intervention Service, and two inpatient area including Home Treatment and two A&E Liaison Team. Also one consultant in Living Well.

Within this arrangement, the consultant appointed to this post will work with other sector consultants (East, West and South sector community outpatients).

Main duties of the job

This is a newly created post. The Consultant will cover thecentral sectorwithin the Oldham area.This is an exciting time to join the Trust and there are many opportunities to contribute to the organisations' innovation and for personal development.

Oldham borough has a new state of the art TMS suite. This is the only NHS provider for this service in the North West.

Oldham has a very strong teaching commitment and candidates will be expected to contribute to the teaching of medical and nursing staff. There are close links to ongoing research projects such as Bright Mind, FreshSTART, Gamechange to name a few.

The Consultants contribute to local service user & carer groups.The Central sector covers the areas of South and East Oldham (Chadderton; Royton and Shaw; Delph, Uppermill, Lees, Ashton Under Lyne).

Patients will be seen in hospital and community clinics, at their own homes or in other clinical settings according to clinical need.

Outpatient clinics are held at the Cherrywood Clinic on the Royal Oldham Hospital site and at the Werneth Primary Care Centre. Werneth Primary Care Centre is 1.5 miles from the hospital.

The consultant in this post will work with the East, South and West Sector CMHTs and also with the Care Management and Review Team, which is a sub-team working across both CMHTs and which supports people with more stable but long term mental illnesses.

We are proud to provide high quality mental health and learning disability services, both inpatient and in the community across five boroughs of Greater Manchester - Bury, Oldham, Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside and Glossop.

Our vision is for a happier and more hopeful life for everyone in our communities and our staff work hard to deliver the very best care for the people who use our services. We're really proud of our#PennineCarePeopleand do everything we can to make sure we're a great place to work.

All individuals regardless of race, age, disability, ethnicity, nationality, gender, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, religion or belief, marriage and civil partnership are encouraged to apply for this post. We would also encourage applications from individuals with a lived experience of mental illness, either individually or as a carer.

If you come and work for us we will offer a range of benefits and opportunities, including:

  • Generous annual leave entitlement for Agenda for Change and Medical and Dental staff.
  • Flexible working opportunities to support your work/life balance
  • Access to Continued Professional Development
  • Involvement in improvement and research activities
  • Health and Wellbeing activities and access to an excellent staff wellbeing service
  • Access to staff discounts across retail, leisure and travel

descriptionHtml:

title: Consultant in Anaesthetics
descriptionHtml:
Benefit from an enhanced starting salary of £140,342, under the Consultant contract for Wales.

West Wales offers an outstanding quality of life, with access to beautiful coastline, national parks and rural countryside. Aberystwyth is a lively university town with a strong community feel, good local amenities and excellent opportunities for outdoor activities.

Hywel Dda University Health Board is looking to appoint a Consultant in Anaesthetics to join the established team at Bronglais General Hospital, Aberystwyth. This post offers the opportunity to develop a sustainable consultant role within a supportive department, while benefitting from an excellent work-life balance in West Wales.

Bronglais General Hospital provides acute services to Ceredigion and surrounding areas and plays a key role in the delivery of planned and unscheduled care. The Anaesthetics department is central to the hospital's surgical and critical care services and is actively involved in service development and future planning.

We welcome applications from motivated consultants who are committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care and who wish to contribute to the ongoing development of anaesthetic services within Hywel Dda University Health Board.

In conjunction with consultant colleagues, the post holder will provide a comprehensive anaesthesia service for general, orthopaedic, gynaecological, obstetric and ophthalmic surgery, covering both elective and urgent activity.

The department operates a fully flexible consultant rota, including elective theatre lists, urgent surgery and trauma lists, and daytime ICU sessions. employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Rehabilitation Medicine
descriptionHtml:
CONSULTANT IN REHABILITATION MEDICINE

Applications are invited for a consultant post in Neurorehabilitation or Rehabilitation Medicine at the Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (OUHFT). The OUHFT comprises four hospitals: John Radcliffe, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre, Churchill Hospital and the Horton General Hospital.

The post is primarily based at the Oxford Centre for Enablement (OCE), which is located at the Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre campus in Headington. OCE is a specialist rehabilitation centre with an international reputation for excellence. It has an active research partnership with both Oxford University and Oxford Brookes University.

There will be opportunities for the successful applicants to develop their own areas of interest which may include management of patients with disorders of consciousness, prosthetics, major trauma, spasticity, Cerebral Palsy or long term neurological conditions.

Applications are welcome from physicians trained in Rehabilitation Medicine, Psychiatry, Neurology, Stroke Medicine / Elderly Care with demonstrated interest and experience in neurological rehabilitation and from those looking to combine clinical work with a research career or educational interest. Those with academic and subspecialty interests are encouraged to contact and discuss the opportunities with Dr Susannah Brain, Clinical Lead for the Oxford Centre for Enablement (OCE) (01865 737320).

PRINCIPAL ACTIVITIES:

Clinical

The post-holder's duties will be primarily at the Oxford Centre for Enablement (OCE).

The Oxford Centre for Enablement (OCE)

OCE is based in a purpose-built building designed to be accessible to people using wheelchairs and suffering from visual and cognitive impairments. There are approximately 240 staff, roughly 190whole time equivalents. The full range of rehabilitation professionals is represented including nursing, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech and language therapy, neuropsychology, counselling, clinical engineering, orthotics and prosthetics. The services provided include 18 Level 1 inpatient beds commissioned by NHS England, 10 level 2 beds commissioned by the ICB, out-patient rehabilitation for people with long term neurological conditions, specialist spasticity clinics, including joint clinics with plastic surgery and orthopaedics, joint transition clinics with a paediatrician, adult cerebral palsy clinics, specialist seating clinics, consultant input to prosthetics, etc. Patients with disorders of consciousness are managed on the ward as per the Royal College of Physicians Guidance. Prosthetics, orthotics and specialist disability services are co-located in the same set of buildings which provide an integrated centre of excellence for patients allowing them to access a variety of services at the same "onestop-shop".

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest NHS teaching trusts in the country. It provides a wide range of general and specialist clinical services and is a base for medical education, training and research. The Trust comprises four hospitals - the John Radcliffe Hospital, Churchill Hospital and Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre in Headington and the Horton General Hospital in Banbury.

Our values, standards and behaviours define the quality of clinical care we offer and the professional relationships we make with our patients, colleagues and the wider community.

We call this Delivering Compassionate Excellence, and its focus is on our values of compassion, respect, learning, delivery, improvement and excellence.

These values put patients at the heart of what we do and underpin the quality healthcare we would like for ourselves or a member of our family. Watch how we set out to deliver compassionate excellence via the OUH YouTube channel.

In 2023NHS England launched its first sexual safety charter, and our Trust proudly signed it. We pledge zero tolerance for inappropriate sexual behaviour and commit to the ten core principles

Oxford University Hospitals promotes a safe, respectful hiring environment.

If you want to make a difference with us, come and join our team. Together, we will uphold the highest standards of care and professionalism.

employer: Rotherham Doncaster and South Humber NHSFT
title: Consultant in Adult MH – Acute Inpatient
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking to appoint to an Inpatient Consultant Psychiatrist post within Adult Mental Health Services, based in Doncaster. This post would complete our substantive recruitment in our Acute Directorate and join a strong group of substantive Consultants across the Mental Health and Learning Disability Care Group. employer: East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Critical Care (Trustwide)
descriptionHtml:
Critical Care in East Kent Hospitals is at an exciting period of redevelopment, having attracted national investment. A new 24-bed Critical Care facility has opened at the William Harvey Hospital, which includes bespoke training facilities, dedicated space for high fidelity simulation training, state of the art echocardiography equipment and critical care ultrasonography simulation training facilities.

We work closely with other specialties and offer opportunities to combine specialties. Whether you are looking for a single specialty role; dual with anaesthesia, acute or emergency medicine, respiratory medicine or renal medicine; or the opportunity for PAs in education at the new Kent and Medway Medical School, we can offer you a forward-thinking approach to flexible working and portfolio careers.

The new Critical Care facility opened in Spring 2022. The facility has spacious, light-filled patient accommodation, 8 negative pressure isolation rooms with positive pressure lobbies, a state-of-the art simulation suite and large multidisciplinary seminar and handover room with high-definition screens for teaching and video conferencing. It houses a large staff common room and rest facilities, on-call rooms and extensive office space.

East Kent Critical Care is a vibrant department, admitting around 1,000 patients each year. Many come to us after suffering an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and in cardiogenic shock, allowing our clinicians to use their strong clinical expertise in echocardiography and point of care ultrasonography.

The unit is equipped with the latest technology, including echocardiography equipment and Intellivent Adaptive Support Ventilation. The department has a strong reputation for ultrasound and echocardiography training, and a burgeoning research portfolio.

We are one of the largest hospital trusts in England, with five hospitals and community clinics serving a local population of around 800,000 people. Our vision is 'great healthcare from great people'. Everything we do is guided by our values: 'People feel cared for, safe, respected and confident that we are making a difference'. We have a new way of working at East Kent Hospitals, called 'We care'. It's about empowering frontline staff to lead improvements day-to-day. We're looking for compassionate people to be part of our improvement journey for the patients, families and carers we care for every day.

title: Clinical Director (Clinical Networks) - Cardiac
descriptionHtml:
Are you a senior clinician with the strategic vision, credibility and experience to lead improvement across London?

NHS England are recruiting a Clinical Director working in London's health and care system to provide visible strategic leadership across the cardiac pathway.

Working with clinical leaders, Integrated Care Boards, providers, patient representative groups, Health Innovation Networks and other strategic partners, you will lead and design a London-wide programme focused on improving clinical outcomes, reducing unwarranted variation and supporting the spread and adoption of evidence-based practice and innovation. You will provide expert clinical advice, strategic leadership and act as an ambassador for clinical improvement across London.

Please be aware that should you be successful in this position, you will be hired to the job title of Clinical Director and this job title is advertised to attract the right skills needed for the role.

You will be a clinically qualified senior leader with GMC or other appropriate professional registration and a licence to practise, with significant NHS leadership experience and recognised expertise in cardiac care. You will bring the influence, judgement and collaborative leadership needed to deliver change across London's complex health and care system. This is why strategic and operational leadership experience in London is important.

This is an exciting opportunity to lead the improvement of outcomes and experience of care for the London population and to coordinate action to reduce health inequalities.

Working with other Clinical Network Directors and strategic partners, the post-holder will contribute to the regional delivery of the 10-Year Health Plan and implementation of the Cardiovascular Modern Service Framework.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

We cannot offer visa sponsorship for external candidates.

employer: The Queen Elizabeth Hospital King's Lynn NHSFT
title: Consultant in Critical Care
descriptionHtml:
As a Consultant in Critical Care, you will join a collaborative team providing specialist care to critically ill patients across our organisation. You will work alongside Consultant colleagues to deliver a high-quality Critical Care service, participate in the on-call rota, and ensure patient care is delivered safely and effectively in line with GMC standards and best practice.

Working closely with Anaesthetic, Critical Care, Medical and Transfer Service colleagues, you will contribute to the delivery and continual development of services, supporting efficient use of resources and helping services operate within agreed budgets. The role requires flexibility to work within a nominally fixed timetable to meet the changing needs of patients and the service.

As a senior leader within the Directorate, you will promote effective multidisciplinary team working, undertake managerial responsibilities as required, supervise junior staff and contribute to appraisal and performance management processes. You will also ensure compliance with Trust and departmental policies and procedures.

Teaching and training are central to this role. You will support the education, supervision and career development of junior doctors and contribute to the training of medical students, nursing staff, paramedics and trainees from other specialties through partnerships with the University of Cambridge and the University of East Anglia.

Provide expert clinical leadership in the assessment, diagnosis and management of patients, ensuring timely decision-making, appropriate intervention and continuous review of care plans to deliver safe, effective and high-quality patient outcomes.

There's never been a more exciting time to join TeamQEH. We're working on a once in a generation opportunity to build a new state-of-the-art hospital and we are also carrying out on one of the biggest pieces of digital transformation work we've ever undertaken.

Our new electronic patient record (EPR) will replace paper-based patient records and will lead to better, safer, joined-up care at The Queen Elizabeth Hospital and beyond.

At The QEH we provide a comprehensive range of specialist, acute, obstetrics and community-based services to around 331,000 people across west and north Norfolk, North Cambs and South Lincs.

We recognise and reward our 4,000 staff and volunteers, priding ourselves on a community atmosphere and positive team spirit. We have approx. 530 beds across 33 wards and have newly built education and training facilities, a range of modern award-winning centres alongside a talented team of people ready to give you a warm welcome.

employer: Wrightington Wigan & Leigh Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Obstetrician & Gynaecologist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Consultant Obstetrician and Gynaecologist with a special interest in Early Pregnancy and Acute Gynaecology to join our team at WWL.

The post holder should have good background knowledge and skills in obstetrics and gynaecology in order to contribute to the provision of both Obstetric and Gynaecological services.

Clinical duties

Day time labour ward cover.

All consultants will take part in a 1 in 12 rota of hot week cover, in which one week (Monday to Friday 09:00 to 19:00) is devoted solely to labour ward and emergency gynaecology cover with all other duties cancelled in that week. These sessions involve prospective cover and must be swapped if they fall during a week in which holiday is taken.

Antenatal clinics

Each of the general antenatal clinics is shared between 2 or 3 Consultants and the special interest antenatal clinics are shared between 2 consultants in order to provide continuity of care during periods of absence for on call duties or leave.

General gynaecology and special interest clinics

The post holder is required to cover General gynaecology clinics. In addition, the post holder will be required to cover EPAU sessions and Menstrual disorder clinics (one stop hysteroscopy clinics). Colposcopy clinics are available to the post holder should they be able to demonstrate appropriate skills.

Theatre

The theatre allocations are currently being reviewed for all consultants depending on demand and requirements for access.

SPA Time

In addition to personal CPD, it is anticipated that the appointee will use SPA time to support the clinical governance framework within the department as well as to develop skills complementary to the needs of the department with mentoring/support as necessary from an existing consultant.

Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust are the proud providers of acute hospital and community services to the people of the Wigan Borough and surrounding areas. At WWL, we value our staff believing that 'happy staff, makes for happy patients'. We have a recognised track record in staff engagement, and living our values 'the WWL Way'. WWL are committed to placing the patient at the heart of everything we do, and in the provision of safe, effective care that acknowledges and ensures dignity. With this in mind we are seeking to recruit people who share our values and beliefs.

title: Junior Oncology Fellow
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity to manage inpatients with cancer. The role involves the acute and day-to-day management of patients with cancer who are admitted to The Christie either due to acute illness, acute complications of their cancer or its treatment.There is exposure to cutting-edge oncological therapies that are being delivered to patients. There is also the opportunity to work closely with specialist oncologists in both the inpatient and outpatient management of patients with cancer. There is access to an elective chemotherapy unit, a supportive oncology multidisciplinary team (including palliative care, specialist therapy, specialist nutrition and associated oncological specialities) an interventional procedures unit, acute assessment unit and specialist treatment services.This job will lead to the development of an individual's ability to manage patients with cancer, including oncological emergencies. We are also a very quality improvement, education and research active site and a prospective employee will have the opportunity to partake in these activities

**The closing date for this post may be extended if there are insufficient applicants or brought forward if there is a high volume of applicants.**

Acute and day-to-day management of patients with cancer who are admitted to hospital (both elective and emergency).Support specialist oncology teams to deliver high-quality care to patients with cancer and to facilitate safe discharge from hospital.Deliver empathic and excellent palliative care to patients in whom that is a key management priority.Support the acute assessment unit.Partake in educational activities for self-development on site.

The Christie is one of Europe's leading cancer centres, treating over 60,000 patients a year. We are based in Manchester and serve a population of 3.2 million across Greater Manchester & Cheshire, but as a national specialist around 15% patients are referred to us from other parts of the country. We provide radiotherapy through one of the largest radiotherapy departments in the world; chemotherapy on site and through 14 other hospitals; highly specialist surgery for complex and rare cancer; and a wide range of support and diagnostic services. We are also an international leader in research, with world first breakthroughs for over 100 years.

We run one of the largest early clinical trial units in Europe with over 300 trials every year. Cancer research in Manchester, most of which is undertaken on the Christie site, has been officially ranked the best in the UK.

The postholder will contribute to the delivery of high quality consultant led care across 7 days. This includes participation in planned weekend and weekday clinical activity to support safe, timely decision making and continuity of care for patients

title: General Practitioner (GP)
descriptionHtml:
Salaried GP.

To work with the GP partners, salaried GPs, the Practice Manager, the nursing and administration team to deliver a wide range of health needs in a primary care setting.

Prescribing in accordance with locally agreed or national guidelines;

We are an approachable and supportive team with an open-door policy. We are proud to have a fabulous multidisciplinary team to support us and look after a list of 11,100 patients around Ringwood.

We are seeking those who want to work in a beautiful part of the country, close to the south coast beaches and on the edge of the New Forest national park. Ringwood Medical Practice

title: Healthcare Assistant
descriptionHtml:
We are a busy and friendly GP surgery in south east London, with good transport links and parking nearby. We are looking for an experienced, reliable and highly motivated Healthcare Assistant who can contribute confidently from an early stage and provide high-quality, person-centred care to our patients.

The successful candidate must have previous Healthcare Assistant experience, preferably within general practice or primary care. They should have experience of NHS Health Checks, routine clinical observations, ECGs and urinalysis, and supporting health promotion and long-term condition reviews. Experience of phlebotomy and EMIS Web is desirable.

The post-holder will undertake a varied clinical and administrative role, working independently within agreed protocols, training and assessed competencies, while recognising the limits of their role and escalating clinical concerns appropriately.

  • Provide NHS Health Checks, record and code findings, and offer appropriate lifestyle and health-promotion advice.
  • Undertake routine observations, ECGs, urinalysis, diabetic foot and new-patient checks within competency.
  • Undertake phlebotomy and administer agreed injections only when trained, competent and appropriately authorised.
  • Support long-term condition reviews and agreed health-promotion referrals.
  • Prepare clinical rooms, maintain stock and support clinicians with minor procedures within competency.
  • Act as a chaperone when required in accordance with practice policy.
  • Check emergency medicines, equipment, oxygen and clinical-fridge temperatures and escalate concerns promptly.
  • Complete stock audits and replenish clinical supplies.
