title: Senior Clinical Trial Unit Fellow in Haematology
descriptionHtml:
The successful applicant will have up to 1 year of full-time clinical trial units post and doing on calls at Hammersmith Hospital on a 1B Banding.

This is an opportunity for an individual to gain sub-specialist expertise and research experience in Immune haematology conditions and clinical trials. The position is suitable for individuals who would like more clinically based experience in the management of patients, clinical trial exposure and the opportunity to undertake prospective and retrospective patient outcome studies with a view to presentation and publication. Collaborations across Imperial College and with other institutions will be encouraged. This post is suitable for candidates towards of the end of their haematology training, who already have MRCP, and are GMC accredited.

Applicants interested in the post will work with Profs Cooper and Milojkovic within the non-malignant and Haemato-Oncology clinical trials units.

We have dedicated haematology clinical trials unit which is experienced in delivering commercial and academic clinical studies. Both trial units have developed and delivered a number of investigator lead studies, involving all aspects of trial planning and delivery from research design to protocol development, ethical approval study implementation and data analysis, and candidates with an interest in developing and implementing clinical studies would be welcomed.

The post is split equally between the two CTUs. Mon- Wed (5 PAs), the candidate will gain experience within the non-malignant CTU and specialist clinics for trial patients and clinical research duties. Wed- Fri (5PAs) the candidate will gain equivalent experience in the Haem-Onc CTU and relevant clinics. The post holder will gain experience in all haematological research areas including; novel therapies for immune haematology disorders, red cell and haemostasis disorders, and across the spectrum of haematology malignancies, including CART, stem cell transplant clinical trials, gene therapy, as well as novel agents in infectious diseases in immunocompromised patients. There will an opportunity to attend Investigator meetings nationally and internationally.

At Imperial College Healthcare you can achieve extraordinary things with extraordinary people, working with leading clinicians pushing boundaries in patient care. Become part of a vibrant team living our values - expert, kind, collaborative and aspirational. You'll get an experience like no other and will fast forward your career. Benefits include career development, flexible working and wellbeing, staff recognition scheme. Make use of optional benefits including Cycle to work, car lease schemes, season ticket loan or membership options for onsite leisure facilities.

The statutory requirement to be fully Covid-19 vaccinated as a condition of employment from April 2022 is subject to legislative review. At Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, we strongly encourage and support vaccination uptake as this remains the best line of defence against COVID19.The successful applicant may have contact with patients and service users and as part of our pre-employment checks and risk assessments, we will ask all candidates to confirm whether or not they have been fully vaccinated or have a medical exemption.

As part of our continued response to Covid19 we are still conducting the majority of our interviews virtually.

We are committed to equal opportunities and improving the working lives of our staff and will consider applications to work flexibly, part-time or job share. Please talk to us at interview.

title: ADVANCED CLINICAL PRACTITIONER
descriptionHtml:
25 - 30 WEEKLY HOURS

The post holder is an Advanced Clinical Practitioner, acting within their professional boundaries. They will provide care for the presenting patient from initial history taking, clinical assessment, diagnosis, treatment and evaluation of their care. They will demonstrate safe, clinical decision-making and expert care for patients within the general practice.

Health Education England describes advanced clinical practice as delivered by experienced, registered health and care practitioners. It is a level of practice characterised by a high degree of autonomy and complex decision making. This is underpinned by a masters level award or equivalent that encompasses the four pillars of clinical practice, leadership and management, education and research, with demonstration of core capabilities and area specific clinical competence. Advanced clinical practice embodies the ability to manage clinical care in partnership with individuals, families and carers. It includes the analysis and synthesis of complex problems across a range of settings, enabling innovative solutions to enhance peoples experience and improve outcomes.

This job description covers many elements of the role but is not exhaustive. There is an opportunity in this role to develop skills and services within Beccles Medical Centre (BMC), including managing key clinical areas, training, and research.

Beccles Medical Centre is an established GP surgery, in the Suffolk market-town of Beccles. The Practice has a list size of approximately 20,000 patients. We have 6 Partners, and just over 100 additional staff. We are a GP Training practice and also host other students studying at the nearby University of East Anglia. We work very closely with our PCN. Our mission is to provide high quality healthcare with respect and compassion, ensuring that the patients are at the heart of everything we do

title: LED IMT3 equivalent in Geriatric Medicine
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic and motivated doctor to join the Department of Geriatric Medicine at University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UCLH) as a Clinical Fellow at IMT3/ST3-equivalent level for six months, commencing in February 2027.

This post offers excellent clinical experience in geriatric and general internal medicine within a leading teaching hospital in central London.

The successful candidate will work within a supportive multidisciplinary team, providing high-quality care to older patients with complex medical conditions, frailty and multiple comorbidities.

The position is particularly suitable for doctors who have completed Internal Medicine Training or equivalent and wish to consolidate their medical registrar-level skills while gaining further experience in geriatric medicine.

There will also be opportunities to participate in teaching, clinical governance, quality improvement and professional development.

The successful applicant will:o Provide comprehensive inpatient care for older patients with acute and complex medical conditions.o Participate in consultant-led ward rounds, multidisciplinary team meetings and discharge planning.o Assess and manage acutely unwell patients, including participation in the general medical on-call rota.o Work collaboratively with nursing staff, therapists, specialist nurses and other clinical teams to deliver safe, effective and patient-centred care.o Develop experience in the management of frailty, delirium, dementia, falls, multimorbidity and other geriatric syndromes.o Maintain accurate clinical documentation and communicate effectively with patients, relatives and healthcare professionals.o Contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate medical teaching.o Participate in departmental educational meetings, clinical governance, audit and quality improvement activities.o Engage in regular educational supervision and develop an individual professional development plan.

University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UCLH) is one of the most complex NHS trusts in the UK, serving a large and diverse population. We provide academically led acute and specialist services, to people from the local area, from throughout the United Kingdom and overseas. Our vision is to deliver top-quality patient care, excellent education, and world-class research.

We provide first-class acute and specialist services across eight sites:o University College Hospital (incorporating the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing)o National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgeryo Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitalso University College Hospital Grafton Way Buildingo Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicineo University College Hospital Macmillan Cancer Centreo The Hospital for Tropical Diseaseso University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street

We are dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of many complex illnesses. UCLH specialises in women's health and the treatment of cancer, infection, neurological, gastrointestinal and oral disease. It has world class support services including critical care, imaging, nuclear medicine and pathology.

We are committed to sustainability and have pledged to become a carbon net zero health service, embedding sustainable practice throughout UCLH. We have set an ambitious target of net zero for our direct emissions by 2031 and indirect emissions by 2040.

employer: Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (Forest)
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Consultant in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry.

CAMHS is part of the Specialist Services Strategic Business Unit in HPFT, managed by the Clinical Director (Dr Shaheen Shora - Fiona McMillian-Shields -non-medical).

CAMHS is managed by a Senior Service Line Leader, Gill Bienveniste supported by Professional Leads and CAMHS Community Managers.

The clinics accept referrals from a number of sources including General Practitioners, SocialWorkers, Health Visitors and Consultant Paediatricians.

Referrals are processed through SPA (the Single Point of Access). The teams are multi-disciplinary including Child and Adolescent Psychiatrists, Psychologists, Mental Health Nurses, Child Psychotherapists, Systemic Therapists and Social Workers.

These teams work on an outpatient model and currently receive approximately 250 referrals per month across Hertfordshire.

Forest House is a specialist psychiatric inpatient unit providing care to children and young people 13 to 18.

The unit admits children through a planned process of assessment, family consultation and liaison with the local CAMHS Tier 3 team.

The Unit has recently been refurbished and extended to 16 beds to include acute admissions and it is an in-patient adolescent unit for East of England NHS.

There is also a provision for eating disorder admissions under the supervision of a dedicated Eating Disorder Service.

"This JD and PS is currently with the Royal College for approval".

An exciting opportunity has become available for a Consultant Psychiatrist to join our current consultant workforce in our Adolescent In-Patient Unit, Forest House Adolescent Unit within Radlett in Hertfordshire.

The successful applicant will work alongside 1 substantive consultant and a medical team composed by Specialty Doctors, GP trainees, Psychiatry Specialty and Core Trainees.

The post holder will complement and support the Senior Leadership Team composed by the other consultant, Therapy Lead, Modern Matron, Team Leaders, Consultant Social worker, Home Treatment Team Lead to achieve the delivery of highest standards of care and contribute to operational management and clinical governance.

In 12 years, the Trust has been successful in acquiring the tender for the provision of specialist Learning disability services in Norfolk, North Essex and Buckinghamshire.

The Trust covers a mix of rural and urban areas, including the City of St Albans, the large towns of Watford, Welwyn Garden City and Stevenage, and the smaller towns of Hemel Hempstead, Radlett, Berkhamsted, Harpenden, Hertford, Ware, Bishops Stortford, Hitchin and Letchworth.

Hertfordshire Social Services have divided the county into four areas. The county has three Clinical Commissioning Groups (CCGs). West Hertfordshire is served by Herts Valleys CCG and Dacorum and East and North Hertfordshire is served by East and North Herts CCG.

The Trust collaborates closely with Hertfordshire County Council and other NHS organisations to promote and support mental health in the community. The Trust clinical services moved from Strategic Business Units (SBUs) into four divisions on the 1st of April 2024, providing clinical services to;

Adult Community Services, including local teams for mental health

Adult Acute and Urgent Services, including rehabilitation, inpatient services and crisis team

Specialist Services such as mental health services for older people, eating disorders, and our mother and baby unit,

Learning Disability and Forensic Services

employer: East of England Community Health and Care NHS Trust (Cambridge)
title: Consultant in Sexual and Reproductive Health
descriptionHtml:
At the East of England Community Health & Care NHS Trust, we are proud to deliver high-quality, compassionate care to our communities. We are looking for a dedicated Consultant in Sexual & Reproductive Health to join our Integrated Contraception & Sexual Health (iCaSH) team in Cambridgeshire.

Working across our clinics in Cambridge, Huntingdon & Wisbech you will play a key role in providing expert clinical care across reproductive & sexual health services. You will work closely with a skilled multidisciplinary team, helping to shape and develop services that meet the needs of a diverse population.

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a forward-thinking organisation that values collaboration, innovation & continuous improvement. Alongside clinical duties, you will support education, supervision, service development and quality improvement, while promoting best practice and patient centred care.

We are seeking a motivated and compassionate clinician with strong leadership and communication skills, GMC Specialist Register entry (or within 6 months of interview) and robust experience in reproductive and sexual health medicine.

In return, we offer a supportive working environment and a strong commitment to professional development and work-life balance.

Join us and make a meaningful difference to the health and wellbeing of our communities.

The post holder will undertake a full range of medical duties in Contraception and Reproductive Health Clinics and will be expected to work with clinical colleagues supported by local managers in providing a safe, efficient, and effective service.

The post holder will share clinical responsibilities with professional colleagues and will actively contribute to the governance arrangements of the department.

The post holder will provide active support to the leadership team to support the continued development of the iCaSH Cambridgeshire service, in order to enhance patient access ensuring that patient safety, confidentiality, and effective clinical governance are maintained and to help develop appropriate clinical pathways.

Rated 'Outstanding' by the Care Quality Commission, we are proud to provide high quality innovative services across most of the east of England that enable people to receive care closer to home and live healthier lives.

There's one reason why our services are outstanding - and that's our amazing staff who, for the seventh year running, rated us incredibly highly in the national staff survey.

If you share our passion for innovative and high-quality care delivery, then please submit your application and join us on our exciting journey as a leading-edge specialist community provider. All are welcome to apply and our promise to you is a culture which prioritises staff engagement and development.

Please be aware that East of England Community Health and Care NHS Trust will never ask applicants to pay fees at any stage of the recruitment process, including job applications, sponsorship arrangements, or employment offers. All recruitment communications and job applications should only be made through our official careers website and published contact details.

If you receive a suspicious job offer or recruitment-related communication, do not make any payments, share personal information, or provide identity documents. We encourage you to report the matter to your local police or relevant law enforcement agency. Any concerns relating to potential recruitment fraud should also be reported to our Local Counter Fraud Specialist (LCFS) as soon as possible.

title: General Practitioner (GP)
descriptionHtml:
We are expanding our GP team and are now looking for a Salaried GP to join our friendly, well-established and high-performing Partnership. We have some flexibility but around 6 sessions per week would be ideal.

You will have clinical autonomy while being supported by an experienced and approachable multidisciplinary team, enabling you to concentrate on providing excellent care for your patients.

We are committed to continually improving our services and developing our team. For the right candidate, there may also be an opportunity to progress towards Partnership in the future.

We offer a competitive salary range starting around £11,250 per session, but dependant on experience.

If you would like an informal conversation about the role or the Partnership before applying, we would be very happy to hear from you.

As part of our GP team, you will provide high-quality, patient-centred care to our registered patients.

Working with a high degree of clinical autonomy, you will assess, investigate, diagnose, treat and refer patients, making appropriate clinical decisions and ensuring that care is safe, effective and responsive to individual needs.

You will work collaboratively with our GPs, Nursing, Pharmacy, Physiotherapy and wider multidisciplinary teams to coordinate care and support positive outcomes for patients.

You will also contribute to clinical meetings, shared learning, quality improvement and the continued development of our services.

Weeping Cross Health Partnership is a stable and forward-thinking Partnership with a well-established place in the local community.

Our team includes eight Partners, seven Associate GPs and highly experienced Nursing, Pharmacy, Physiotherapy and wider multidisciplinary teams. Together, we provide a broad range of services across three practices in Stafford and play an active role within a successful Primary Care Network.

We are proud to have been rated Good by the CQC, with examples of excellent practice highlighted. We also achieve strong QOF results and consistently high levels of patient satisfaction.

We have ambitious plans for the future and offer excellent opportunities for professional development, service improvement and career progression.

Our three practices are located in the suburbs of Stafford, a well-connected county town offering excellent schools, amenities and transport links. Cannock Chase National Landscape is also close by, providing easy access to outstanding countryside and outdoor activities.

employer: Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with Interest in Medical Glaucoma
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of a full time Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist (fixed term contract for a period of 12 months) with interest Medical Glaucoma at Epsom & St Helier NHS Trust.

The Ophthalmology Department at Epsom and St Helier has a well established and highly performing team treating a broad range of Ophthalmology conditions. The successful applicant will join a team of Consultants, Specialist and Specialty Doctors, Fellows, Trainees, specialist nurses, optometrists, orthoptists, HCAs, technicians and a dedicated admin team including a diabetic failsafe officer and an injection service failsafe officer. The post holder will be required to work across both sites and the role may change depending on service needs.

This post is for a part time Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with special interest in medical Glaucoma. The post holder will work alongside the Glaucoma clinical lead Mr Chris Panos and the wider glaucoma team.

The Glaucoma team is a multidisciplinary award winning team (including the Bayer Award in 2017). The clinical team is supported by specialist nurses, orthoptists, HCAs, technicians and a dedicated administrative team including a failsafe officer.

The post holder will be responsible for the assessment, diagnosis and laser management of patients attending glaucoma clinics and the Acute Eye Service. They will support the existing glaucoma consultants in the running of paperless virtual clinics.

St George's, Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals and Health Group cares for a population of four million people in South West London and North East Surrey.Our sites include St George's Hospital, one of 11 major trauma centres in the UK and the largest healthcare provider and major teaching hospital in the area; St Helier Hospital, home to the South West Thames Renal and Transplantation Unit and Queen Mary's Hospital for Children; and Epsom Hospital, home to the South West London Elective Orthopaedic Centre (SWLEOC).

After years of collaboration, our two Trusts became a hospitals group in 2021. While remaining as two separate Trusts, being a hospitals group will help us to collaborate more closely on research, and the development, education, and training of our 17,000-strong workforce.

title: Locum Consultant in Thoracic Surgery
descriptionHtml:
The department of Thoracic Surgery at Wythenshawe Hospital is recruiting a Locum Consultant Thoracic Surgeon, to work alongside our specialised and experienced Thoracic Surgical, Respiratory and Oncology team in the Lung Cancer Directorate.

The post is a whole-time equivalent position at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust and based at the Wythenshawe Hospital Site. Applicants should have substantial experience in general thoracic surgery, including trauma/ minimally invasive techniques and managing patients with thoracic malignancies and pleural disease.

The post is to join 8 substantive appointments within the multi-specialty Directorate of Lung Cancer & Thoracic Surgery. There is a major focus on early detection, accelerating access to thoracic surgery, thoracic trauma, and delivering expansion of the GM Lung Cancer Screening Programme.

The Department of Thoracic Surgery is one of the largest in the UK with access to a high-volume complex practice supported by a nationally leading multidisciplinary team. Extensive opportunities exist for service development, education and research and applicants should expect to have substantial experience and track record for delivery. Applicants should also possess a clear philosophy on their potential contribution to augment and advance the current departmental standards and activity.

The team operates a 'Consultant of the Week' model, with responsibility for the daily triage of referrals, listing schedule review, and daily Board & Ward Rounds.

All Consultants will have access to outpatient clinics, a broad MDT portfolio (including lung cancer, mesothelioma, airway management, sarcoma, emphysema) and 1.5 flexible operating days per week over 8 weeks.

Participation in the thoracic surgery on-call rota, ward cover, and management of admissions from A&E, general wards, the major trauma centre and inter-hospital transfers is expected.

The post holders will be actively involved in the organisation, preparation and delivery of the MDTs and have collective responsibility for delivery of accelerated pathways.

As part of this post along with other colleagues, the post holders will provide support and guidance to the team consisting of specialist registrars, senior clinical fellows, specialist nurses, physiotherapists, OT, Dietician, lung physiologists, and other junior medical staff.

The appointees will take an active role in medical education and will be expected to take on the role of educational/ clinical supervisor for trainees, as well as being encouraged toparticipate in teaching undergraduates and postgraduates, and to participate in departmental audit, research, governance, and service development.

The post-holder will have 1.5 SPAs per week to facilitate these activities.

Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) is a leading centre of clinical excellence, renowned for pioneering patient care, advanced medical research, and a collaborative multi-speciality environment. We are the largest provider of specialist services, and our Oxford Road Campus in Manchester is the largest health academic campus in Europe - a great place to progress your career.

With over 30,000 employees, a turnover exceeding £3 billion, and 10 hospital and community services, join our team to help us deliver outstanding healthcare to our diverse communities.We offer an engaging and supportive environment, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technology. Research and Innovation are at the heart of our work, offering opportunities to lead research that shapes the future of medicine, working alongside experts, advancing clinical practice, and improving patient outcomes.At MFT, we foster a culture where every colleague is valued and empowered to thrive. Your expertise is recognised, your ambitions are supported, and your impact is felt at every level. Whether you want to develop your clinical skills, pursue research interests, or seek leadership opportunities, MFT provides the ideal environment to achieve your medical or professional aspirations.If you are dedicated to driving clinical innovation and delivering compassionate patient care, join us to shape tomorrow's healthcare; where clinical excellence, innovation, and your career will thrive.

employer: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialty Doctor or GPWER Adult Eating Disorders
descriptionHtml:
The post holder will be part of the Hampshire Eating Disorders Service. The post holder will work collaboratively with multidisciplinary colleagues and will be based within the expanding Physical Health (PH) Monitoring Team providing medical assessment, monitoring, treatment recommendations, and consultation for patients aged 18+ and under the care of the Eating Disorders Service. The role includes direct clinical work, liaison with primary care/acute trusts, participation in MDT meetings, contribution to service development and education and support to develop expertise around eating disorders. The PH team is currently expanding and following full expansion is expected to be 1 Clinical Team Lead Nurse, 2 Band 6 Nurses, 4 Band 4 HCAs and 1 Band 3 Admin in addition to this role holder and the Consultant Psychiatrist oversight.

MEDICAL ASSESSMENT AND MONITORING

*Conduct physical health assessments as part of the EDS multi-disciplinary team.

*Arrange and interpret investigations (e.g., blood tests, ECGs).

*Provide feedback and health education to patients and professionals around the physical health complications of eating disorders.

*Monitor physical health symptoms throughout treatment and liaise with GPs as needed.

*Review results from primary care monitoring and take appropriate clinical actions.

*Provide end-of-treatment assessment reports when appropriate.

MEDICAL TREATMENT

*Recommend medical treatment plans for patients accepted on to the Adult EDS caseload.

*Refer patients to appropriate agencies or acute services for further medical care when necessary.

*Support clinical decision-making in physical health clinics and MDT risk meetings.

*As required, and within capacity, provide advice and support to HIOWH Clinicians with the physical health monitoring and management of patients not on the EDS caseload.

CLINICAL GOVERNANCE AND PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS

*Adhere to national and local protocols, including NICE and MEED guidelines.

*Participate in clinical governance activities, incident reporting, and service audits.

*Maintain up-to-date clinical knowledge through CPD and supervision.

*Undergo appraisal and revalidation in line with GMC requirements.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is a newly established organisation, bringing together expertise from across mental health, learning disabilities, community, and physical health services. We are dedicated to delivering compassionate, high-quality, and accessible care to the diverse communities of Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.

With over 13,000 dedicated staff working across more than 300 sites, we place patients and staff at the centre of everything we do. Our goal is to create an integrated healthcare system that improves accessibility and ensures more consistent care for patients. By working together, we aim to improve patient outcomes, drive innovation, and meet the unique needs of the populations we serve.

Our Trust unites services from Southern Health, Solent NHS Trust, Isle of Wight NHS Trusts community and mental health teams, as well as Hampshire CAMHS, originally part of Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust. This transformation enables us to deliver more seamless care across the region, ensuring that patients receive the right support, in the right place, at the right time.

Join us as we embark on this exciting journey to shape the future of healthcare across Hampshire and the Isle of Wight. We are deeply committed to our CARE values of compassion, accountability, respect, and excellence, and offer outstanding opportunities for career development, training, and collaborative working.

descriptionHtml:
This role is joining a team of Consultants responsible for the provision of Obstetric & Gynaecological services to the Health Board. title: Post CCT Clinical Fellow in Knee Specialty
descriptionHtml:
Bristol NHS Foundation Trust

Post CCT Senior Clinical Fellow (SpR level) in Knee Surgery

We are looking to appoint 1 Senior Knee Fellows for start dates August 2027. The posts usually run for 12 months but occasionally 6-month slots can be accommodated. The one post works predominantly with Mr James Murray, while the other post works predominantly with Mr Andrew Porteous. The job will include working with other members of the Bristol Knee Group. The posts will provide exposure to a wide range of knee surgery including partial and total knee replacement, revision arthroplasty and infection work, ligament and meniscal surgery, patello-femoral surgery.

employer: Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialty Doctor in Psychosis Service (16-35 years)
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking to recruit a Specialty Doctor to join our East Early Intervention in Psychosis Service. This service forms part of the overall Community Mental Health provision in the City of Birmingham and works closely with other specialty teams, providers and services to deliver a high quality service.

The clinical base is The Washwood Heath Wellbeing Centre, 4 Clodeshall Road, Birmingham B8 3SN.

The service comprises specialist and dedicated mental health professionals including psychiatrists, senior mental health practitioners, clinical psychologist, occupational therapist and psychotherapists. The post older will work under the supervision of the Consultant Psychiatrist and will have a close working relationship with members of the MDT and liaison with other doctors in primary and secondary care.

The successful postholder should hold full registration with the GMC and have completed at least two years experience or training in psychiatry.

The Specialty Doctor will be a member of the EIP MDT at The Washwood Heath Centre and support the East EIP MDT Team. They will be involved in the assessment and management of young people (16-35 years) with mental ill health and neurodevelopmental conditions. The post holder will also contribute to providing psychiatric and medical risk management and co-work with multi-agency professionals such as social services.

Welcome to Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust. We provide a comprehensive health care service to those people living in Birmingham and Solihull who are experiencing mental health problems. We serve a culturally and socially diverse population of over a million, spread over 172 square miles, have an annual budget of £760 million and a dedicated workforce of more than 6,000 staff - making us one of the largest and most complex mental health foundation trusts in the country.

Our catchment population is ethnically diverse and characterised in places by high levels of deprivation, low earnings and unemployment. These factors create a higher requirement for access to health services and a greater need for innovative ways of engaging people from the most affected areas. We are a team of compassionate, inclusive and committed people working together to provide excellent care to support our community. If you are looking for a place to belong, where you can make a real difference to people's lives, join our team where our warm welcome is waiting for you.

employer: NELFT North East London Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Community Crisis & Therapeutic HTT
descriptionHtml:
JOB TITLE: Consultant Community CAMHS Psychiatrist Crisis & Therapeutic Home Treatment Team

CONTRACT: 10 Programmed Activities (10 PAs) Substantive Flexible working available including job share, part-time, remote sessions considered

BASE: Stapleford House, Stapleford Close, Chelmsford, CM2 OQX Salary £113,565 -£150,569 per annum

On-call responsibilities: The postholder will be part of the Senior Psychiatrist out of hours on-call rota. The community CAMHS Consultants participate in an on-call rota with a current frequency of 1:7, with a 2% of basic salary, Category B on-call supplement. This rota mainly provides telephone advice to the crisis teams, which is the first port of call for children in crises out of hours, covering Southend, Essex and Thurrock.

The on-call shifts are from 17:00 - 09:00 Monday to Friday, and all day on weekends and bank holidays. The on call does not include support to psychiatric inpatient units or Section 136 suites, as this is provided by a different organisation in Essex (EPUT).

This is a new post, that has been created following receiving additional resource from commissioners in order to have substantive medical capacity in the SET CAMHS Crisis and Therapeutic Home Treatment (THT) Team, to provide high quality preventative care, and to reduce the time CAMHS spend in A&Es. A lot of transformation has taken place already and continues to take place within Essex's Community CAMHS Services. This is a new, substantive, full-time post - 10 Programmed Activities (PAs) post with 7.5 Direct Clinical Contact activities (DCC) and 2.5 Supporting Professional Activities (SPAs). This post is vacant currently and we wish to recruit substantively to this post as soon as possible. It is a substantive post and we would consider requests for flexible working, job share or fixed term if preferred. The expectation of the post holder is to support their teams, the Directorate and the organisation to follow the Trusts Values in their day-to-day work. With an excellent reputation for research and development, our skilled health professionals are at the cutting edge of evidence-based innovation, opening up the possibilities for better ways of working and delivery of care.

title: Senior Clinical Fellow (ST3+ Equivalent)
descriptionHtml:
This is a fixed-term post working in the Department of Neurology as a Senior Clinical Fellow (ST3/IMT3 equivalent). The postholder will work alongside the neurology trainees and junior doctors, with clinical responsibilities including clerking non-elective patients admitted under neurology, providing clinical support in the day-to-day care and management of neurology inpatients under the supervision of the neurology consultants, and completing discharge summaries. The ability to perform lumbar punctures is highly desirable.

The postholder will be expected to participate in the neurology on-call rota which consists of day shifts on Saturday and Sunday one weekend in 6, under the supervision of the on-call consultant and 1in 12 Twilight shift (17:00 hrs to midnight) covering neurology and stroke on call.

Provisions will be made to allow participation in some outpatient neurology clinics. There is a weekly educational departmental meeting which the postholder is encouraged to attend and an excellent neuroradiology meeting each Thursday morning in which inpatient neuroradiology is discussed.

In addition, some GIM work will be undertaken. Currently, this consists of 2-week blocks in acute medicine. It is expected that the post holder would undertake two such blocks within the 6-month locum period.

All employees, including the appointee, will be expected to be involved in implementing the Trust's Clinical Governance programme. This includes active participation in clinical audit, quality, clinical guidelines/pathways, professional development, appraisal and risk management.

As outlined above, the postholder will work alongside the neurology trainees and junior doctors, and will be expected to provide a range of clinical duties:

1. Clerking non-elective patients admitted under neurology.

2. Providing clinical support in the day-to-day care and management of neurology inpatients under the supervision of the neurology consultants.

3. Completing electronic discharge summaries.

4. Participating in the neurology ST on-call rota, which consists of day shifts on Saturday and Sunday one weekend in 6, under the supervision of the on-call consultant.

5. Clinical procedures - acute lumbar punctures may be required in some clinical scenarios. The ability to perform LPs is therefore highly desirable. There is also an elective LP list which is currently undertaken by one of our clinical fellows. This service needs additional support.

6. Provision will be made to allow participation in some outpatient neurology clinics.

Join us at the Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital and be part of a workforce of over 10,000 staff!

The NNUH is one of the largest NHS trusts in the UK, providing first-class acute care for around one million people, living in Norfolk and surrounding areas. We are a teaching and research hospital, at the forefront of innovation, home to state-of-the-art facilities, such as the Quadram Institute. We are pleased to work closely with the University of East Anglia, providing teaching opportunities for our staff and placement opportunities for their students. We attract some of the best and leading professionals from across the country and are proud that our workforce represents 94 countries from across the world.

We are a friendly, collaborative hospital, working with local services and home to N&N Hospitals Charity.

We can offer you the full range of NHS benefits/discounts and in addition:

title: MRI Radiographer

title: Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with interest in Oculoplastic Surgery
descriptionHtml:
Manchester Royal Eye Hospital is seeking to appoint a Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with a special interest in Oculoplastic Surgery.

The successful applicant will join the established consultant team and contribute to the delivery of specialist oculoplastic and orbital services. This is a 10 programmed activity post.

Applications are welcomed from candidates who wish to work less than full time.

The successful applicant will be responsible for the diagnosis, treatment, and aftercare of ophthalmic patients. The consultant will provide a sub-specialty interest in Oculoplastic Surgery and will ideally have expertise in Orbital Surgery and Paediatric Oculoplastics.

The post holder will contribute to:

  • Oculoplastic outpatient clinics
  • Oculoplastic theatre lists
  • Emergency Eye Department activity Clinical governance, audit, and service development
  • Undergraduate and postgraduate education

The indicative job plan includes 5.0 programmed activities for oculoplastic clinics (including associated administration) or theatre activity, providing flexibility across these DCC sessions, 2.5 programmed activities for theatre activity, 1 programmed activity within the Emergency Eye Department, and 1.5 supporting professional activities (SPA).

Flexibility will be required to meet service needs, including the ability to vary the balance between oculoplastic clinic and theatre activity where required. Applicants must hold Fellowship of the Royal College of Ophthalmologists, or an equivalent qualification, and have completed appropriate specialist fellowship training in oculoplastic and orbital surgery. A higher degree would be desirable.

Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) is a leading centre of clinical excellence, renowned for pioneering patient care, advanced medical research, and a collaborative multi-speciality environment. We are the largest provider of specialist services, and our Oxford Road Campus in Manchester is the largest health academic campus in Europe - a great place to progress your career.

With over 30,000 employees, a turnover exceeding £3 billion, and 10 hospital and community services, join our team to help us deliver outstanding healthcare to our diverse communities.We offer an engaging and supportive environment, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technology. Research and Innovation are at the heart of our work, offering opportunities to lead research that shapes the future of medicine, working alongside experts, advancing clinical practice, and improving patient outcomes.At MFT, we foster a culture where every colleague is valued and empowered to thrive. Your expertise is recognised, your ambitions are supported, and your impact is felt at every level. Whether you want to develop your clinical skills, pursue research interests, or seek leadership opportunities, MFT provides the ideal environment to achieve your medical or professional aspirations.If you are dedicated to driving clinical innovation and delivering compassionate patient care, join us to shape tomorrow's healthcare; where clinical excellence, innovation, and your career will thrive.

employer: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Geriatrician
descriptionHtml:
The Southampton and Southwest Division is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Geriatrician to join our expanding team. This exciting role will be based within a dynamic and innovative multidisciplinary team, delivering both proactive and reactive care to older adults across our geography.

The successful applicant will provide comprehensive care for acute medical admissions, inpatient medical care, and rehabilitation patients within the hospital setting. In addition, they will lead outpatient clinic activity and support community multidisciplinary team (MDT) services, ensuring seamless, patient-centred care across hospital and community pathways.

We are looking for a clinician with excellent communication, analytical, and clinical decision-making skills who can work collaboratively across professional boundaries. The successful candidate will contribute to the ongoing development of our services, support quality improvement initiatives, and have the opportunity to develop and pursue specialist clinical interests within geriatric medicine.

Provide care for acute medical admissions, medical inpatients, and rehabilitation patients.

Deliver outpatient clinics and support community MDT services.

Contribute to the care of patients with geriatric conditions, including movement disorders and Parkinson's disease.

Participate in the on-call rota (1:10 weekends and five weekdays every 10 weeks).

Support clinical audit, governance, and quality improvement activities.

Teach and supervise medical students, resident doctors, and other healthcare professionals.

Contribute to service management, planning, and governance, including attendance at consultant and senior staff meetings.

Undertake administrative duties associated with patient care and clinical services.

Work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams and contribute to service development.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is a newly established organisation, bringing together expertise from across mental health, learning disabilities, community, and physical health services. We are dedicated to delivering compassionate, high-quality, and accessible care to the diverse communities of Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.

With over 13,000 dedicated staff working across more than 300 sites, we place patients and staff at the centre of everything we do. Our goal is to create an integrated healthcare system that improves accessibility and ensures more consistent care for patients. By working together, we aim to improve patient outcomes, drive innovation, and meet the unique needs of the populations we serve.

Our Trust unites services from Southern Health, Solent NHS Trust, Isle of Wight NHS Trusts community and mental health teams, as well as Hampshire CAMHS, originally part of Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust. This transformation enables us to deliver more seamless care across the region, ensuring that patients receive the right support, in the right place, at the right time.

Join us as we embark on this exciting journey to shape the future of healthcare across Hampshire and the Isle of Wight. We are deeply committed to our CARE values of compassion, accountability, respect, and excellence, and offer outstanding opportunities for career development, training, and collaborative working.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We have a vacancy for a 6 session GP.

Situated in the beautiful Forest of Dean, we work in a purpose-built medical centre occupied in August 2020. We offer 15 minute appointments with a growing list of just over 5500 patients.

A Salaried GP works as an autonomous practitioner, responsible for the provision of medical services to the practice population, delivering an excellent standard of clinical care while complying with the contract.

Furthermore, the post-holder will adhere to the GMC standards for good medical practice, contributing to the effective management of the practice, leading by example, maintaining a positive, collaborative working relationship with the multidisciplinary team.

The role is to support, mentor, and supervise other healthcare professionals within Dockham Surgery and be an integral part of the general practice team.

  • The delivery of highly effective medical care to the entitled population
  • To clinically examine and assess patient needs from a physiological and psychological perspective and plan clinical care accordingly referring patients to other services/agencies in a timely manner, utilising Practice and any other local guidelines
  • Generic prescribing adhering to local and national guidance
  • Prioritise health problems and intervene appropriately to assist the patient in complex, urgent or emergency situations, including initiation of effective emergency care
  • Effective management of long-term conditions
  • Review medications following the appropriate policies, NICE/local clinical guidelines and local care pathways
  • Maintain accurate clinical records in conjunction with good practice, policy and guidance
  • Adhere to best practice recommended through clinical guidelines and the audit process
  • Accept delegated responsibility for a specific area (or areas) or the QOF
  • Be aware of your duties and responsibilities regarding current legislation and adhere to practice policies and procedures on Safeguarding Adults and Safeguarding Children
  • Prepare and complete the revalidation process to remain fit to practice
  • Encourage collaborative working, liaising with all staff regularly, always promoting a culture of continuous improvement
  • To be an integral part of the general practice team as well as supporting the wider network and multi-disciplinary team

We have a wonderful team of 2 partners and 2 salaried GP`s with a fantastic nursing team who will support you. We have a Clinical pharmacist, a pharmacy technician, a GP assistant, an ANP and other ARRS support staff.

employer: South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant in Cardiothoracic Anaesthesia and Critical Care
descriptionHtml:
South Tees NHS Foundation Trust is recruiting Locum Consultants in Cardiothoracic Anaesthesia to join our existing team of 13 Consultants. The term is fixed at 12 months and is in preparation for planned substantive posts which will be advertised for appointment in the near future.

We are looking for dynamic forward thinking cardiothoracic anaesthetists to join us and continue the development of the service. You will join a friendly, committed team to provide anaesthesia and critical care for approximately 1000 cardiac and 700 thoracic cases per year.

Our varied caseload includes minimally invasive aortic and mitral surgery, major aortic work, an established TAVI programme, VAT lobectomies, thymectomies and robotic thoracic surgery. A robotic mitral surgery programme is in the planning stages.

The Tees Valley is home to vibrant towns, picturesque villages, breath taking countryside and stunning coastlines and has the North York Moors National Park on its doorstep. Excellent travel links mean London and Edinburgh are both just a couple of hours away by train.

Recently rated as one of the best trusts in the country for patient safety and one of the best places to work, South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest Foundation Trusts in England.

title: Clinical Teaching Fellow - Medicine & Acute Respiratory Care Unit
descriptionHtml:
This post is a one-year fixed term post to cover maternity leave, starting January 2027.

This post is ideal for a doctor with MRCP seeking to establish a career in any of the medical specialties who is either between core medical and higher training and wants a career break, or a higher specialist trainee as an Out of Programme for Experience who has an interest in Medical Education. The post is also of interest for trainees pursuing a career path in Respiratory Medicine, Critical Care or Acute Medicine where there is the opportunity to build up experience in respiratory conditions and the use of Non-Invasive Ventilation (NIV).

ACUTE RESPIRATORY CARE UNIT (ARCU) - 2.5 days

The unit takes level 1 and 2 patients with a range of respiratory and other medical conditions, including supporting those with respiratory failure who require non-invasive ventilation. Please note the unit cares for patients who have Covid infection (including the use of NIV and high flow oxygen) and you will be expected to manage these patients although full PPE is provided.

You will also review and discuss possible admissions to the unit from ED, the wards and step-downs from Intensive Care. ARCU hosts a consultant of the week who often has a background in Respiratory Medicine or Critical Care, so this is a perfect opportunity for any medical trainee to gain more experience in these areas prior to commencement of ST3 training.

TEACHING - UNDERGRADUTE MEDICAL EDUCATION DEPARTMENT (UMED) - 2.5 DAYS

The post not only involves teaching opportunities but the chance to build your CV when applying for a training number or for any future post. It offers the chance to undertake a higher degree such as the Certificate in Medical Education, present at local, regional, national conferences and research innovative ideas in medical education.

With more than 18,000 colleagues, we are the largest employer in Nottinghamshire and one of the biggest and busiest NHS Trusts in the country, serving more than 2.5m residents of Nottingham and Nottinghamshire and a further four million people across the East Midlands and beyond.

We provide a range of national and internationally renowned specialist services and we are at the forefront of new surgical procedures and research programmes. We are home to the East Midlands Major Trauma Centre, the Nottingham Children's Hospital and in partnership with the University of Nottingham, we host a Biomedical Research Centre carrying out vital research into hearing, digestive diseases, respiratory, musculoskeletal disease, mental health and imaging.

As a teaching hospital, we are instrumental in the education and training of doctors, nurses and other healthcare professionals. We are proud of our strong relationships with universities across the East Midlands, including the University of Nottingham, Nottingham Trent University and Loughborough University.

title: Consultant Breast Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
The post is for One full-time Consultant Breast Surgeons. The post will be based in Singleton Hospital but with clinical commitments at Neath Port Talbot Hospital, and occasionally Morriston Hospital in other parts of the Health Board. It is offered on the amended terms of the Consultant Contract.

The post is offered initially on a 10 session contract, but those wanting to work less than full time would be considered and should also apply. There are no general surgery on-call commitment. Swansea is Wales' second-largest city, and sits on the five-mile sweep of Swansea Bay. An ideal base for exploring South-West Wales, there is also much on offer for visitors in Swansea itself. title: Consultant Chemical Pathologist
descriptionHtml:
This is a full-time replacement post for a Consultant Chemical Pathologist based at Wrexham Maelor Hospital. The Clinical Biochemistry department has strong links with all clinical specialties throughout the hospital and GPs within its catchment area.

We wish to identify someone with broad experience in Clinical Biochemistry, who has a strong clinical background to provide direct clinical care in the specialist Lipid Clinic, Metabolic Stone service and involved with the multidisciplinary Parenteral Nutrition Service, which provides parenteral nutrition to inpatients and a small number of patients on long-term home parenteral nutrition. The department has close links with all clinical services, so there is scope for development of relevant collaborative clinical service or research interests.

As part of the recruitment process, candidates shortlisted for the role will be invited to attend both a Stakeholder Interview and an Advisory Appointments Committee (AAC) Interview. AAC is scheduled for 29 January 2027. The Stakeholder Interview date will be confirmed once shortlisting is complete. This is expected to be held week commencing 25 January 2027.

Clinical Workload

Clinical duties will be based at Wrexham Maelor Hospital, where the consultant will be expected to cover the weekly Lipid and Metabolic Stone Clinics on-site.

The Lipid Clinic service operates in conjunction with the Familial Hypercholesterolaemia (FH) Genetic Screening Programme for patients across Wrexham and Flintshire. The appointee will work closely with the North Wales FH Nurse Specialist to actively identify candidates for FH genotyping and manage complex, difficult-to-treat FH cases throughout the region. The clinic also oversees the review and management of patients requiring injectable therapies. Additionally, a significant volume of primary care lipid referrals are managed via clinical advice and office-based decision letters, bypassing the need for in-person clinic visits. Direct electronic access across primary and secondary care systems streamlines this process, handling a steady influx of weekly advisory requests.

The Metabolic Stone Clinic receives referrals from across all three BCUHB hospitals, managing a broad case mix of cystinuria, calcium phosphate, calcium oxalate, and uric acid stone formers. Clear referral guidelines has been established with the urological team to maintain an efficient caseload across the region.

Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) is Wales's largest health organisation, with a budget of over £2.4 billion and a workforce of over 20,000 staff.

BCUHB provides a full range of primary, community, mental health, acute and specialist hospital services for the population of North Wales, across 3 acute hospitals and a network of community hospitals, health centres, clinics, and mental health units. It also co-ordinates or provides the work of GP practices and NHS services provided by dentists, opticians, and pharmacists across the region.

The Health Board is an integrated health system that strives for excellent, compassionate care delivered in partnership with the public sector and other statutory and third sector organisations.

title: Senior Fellow - Cardiology
descriptionHtml:
University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is delighted to offer a fantastic opportunity to work with us.

Job Title: Senior Fellow in Cardiology

Start Date: ASAP

Contract Type: Permanent

Further details about the role can be found in the job description below.

As part of our team, you will work collaboratively with colleagues, helping to deliver excellent services and ensuring the highest standards of patient care.We are looking for an enthusiastic and motivated Senior Training Fellow in Cardiology to join the Cardiovascular & Thoracic Care Group at University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust.

This is an excellent opportunity for a doctor committed to pursuing a career in cardiology, offering a structured training programme resulting in achievement of all core cardiology skills recognised through the portfolio training pathway, equivalent to those with a NTN. We are looking for someone who has a strong interest in developing a career in cardiology, is committed to delivering excellent patient-centred care, demonstrates excellent communication and teamwork skills, is enthusiastic about learning, teaching and continuous professional development, has the drive to contribute to quality improvement, research and service development.

As one of the largest acute teaching Trusts in England, we offer learning and development opportunities to help you achieve the career you aspire to. UHS is rated 'Good' by the CQC and in the latest national NHS Staff Survey, we were in the top 10 acute trusts for staff engagement and for staff recommending the hospital as a place to work or receive care.

We support flexible working and will consider requests taking into account the needs of the service. UHS employees are able to access a range of NHS discounts, are entitled to a minimum of 35 days paid holiday (pro rata), and we offer a generous pension scheme.

Southampton is an attractive place to live and work situated on the south coast, with an international airport and direct trains to London. The New Forest National Park and beaches of the Jurassic coast are also right on our doorstep. The city offers living costs 30% lower than London and 17 schools rated outstanding by Ofsted.

We believe that using technology wisely shows strong time management and commitment to innovation. However, personalising your recruitment application to highlight your unique skills and experiences is crucial. Relying too heavily on generic, AI-generated content instead of drawing from your own strengths and accomplishments may lead to your application being rejected if multiple candidates present identical or similar information.

title: Consultant Vascular Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
We are currently a team of six full time surgeons working in a tertiary vascular centre performing all types of major vascular and endovascular operations and procedures. One of these surgeons also performs renal transplant surgery and several provide surgery for vascular access. The Vascular service is provided by Mr Dev Mittapalli (full time Vascular & Endovascular Surgeon and Service Lead for Vascular Surgery), Miss Catherine Western (Vascular and Endovascular surgeon and Educational Lead for Vascular Surgery), Mr Jamie Barwell (full time Vascular Surgeon), Lt Col Rob Faulconer (Military Vascular and Trauma surgeon) and Mr Aled Jones (Vascular and Trauma surgeon & Governance lead) and Mr Cris Parry (fulltime NHS Vascular and Trauma surgeon consultant - now retired).

There is a separate on call rota for vascular surgery and which has no commitment to general surgery. The six vascular surgeons currently do fixed days of 24hr on call (which usually coincides with their operating list) during the working week (Monday-Thursday 0800-0800) with a second surgeon available covering the day time on-call and a weekend on call all on a 1:6 rota. There is a surgeon free of elective commitments covering oncalls during day time theare session.

We are expected to provide prospective cover for any periods of annual or study leave and the successful applicant will need to be flexible in providing this cover as are the current Vascular Surgeons. All the on call is shared out equally in terms of numbers of days worked over the year but inevitably in a small team there are periods of intense activity and other quieter periods.

All emergencies are admitted to a dedicated surgical admissions unit at Derriford Hospital.

title: Senior Oncology Teaching Fellow
descriptionHtml:
SENIOR CLINICAL ONCOLOGY TEACHING FELLOW

Applications are invited for the post of Senior Clinical Fellow In Oncology at Whittington Health NHS Trust. This is a fixed term post initially for 12 months, with the option to extend.

All candidates should be eligible for full registration with the GMC.

Please note this post may close earlier if sufficient applications are received.

The Oncology Service is a core part of the Surgery & Cancer Integrated Care Service Unit (ICSU), delivering care to over 3,200 oncology patients and 6,000 breast outpatients annually. The department provides specialist treatment across a range of malignancies, including breast, lung, gastrointestinal, prostate, and haematological cancers. Facilities include a dedicated chemotherapy unit with 15 chairs and an on-site chemotherapy pharmacy. Breast and lung multidisciplinary team (MDT) meetings are held jointly with University College Hospital (UCH), while the GI MDT is based at Whittington. All breast cancer surgery, including implant-based reconstruction, is carried out on site, while gastrointestinal and lung cancer surgeries are performed at UCH. Radiotherapy services are also delivered at UCH

We can offer you:

Patient and user involvement

Risk and complaints management

Clinical effectiveness and audit programmes

Continuous Professional Development

Clinical research in accordance with DOH Governance requirements

You will need:o To be highly motivated and flexible to provide patient focused careo Full registration with the General Medical Councilo Experience of working in the NHS

Whittington Health serves a richly diverse population and works hard to ensure that all our services are fair and equally accessible to everyone. Nowhere is this more obvious than in the way we look after our staff. We aim to employ a workforce which is as representative as possible of this population, so we are open to the value of differences in age, disability, gender, marital status, pregnancy and maternity, race, sexual orientation, and religion or belief. The Trustbelieves that as a public sector organisation we have an obligation to have recruitment, training, promotion and other formal employment policies and procedures that are sensitive to these differences. We think that by doing so, we are better able to treat our patients as well as being a better place to work.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Are you looking for a 4 or 5 session salaried GP role? We have an exciting opportunity to welcome another GP to our experienced and supportive team.

descriptionHtml:

As a Foundation Trust we involve service users, carers, the public, staff and partner organisations in the way that we are run and our future development. If you are interested in becoming a member of our Foundation Trust please visit our website.

This post is based primarily in the Mortimer Market Centre in central London which has one of the largest HIV cohorts in the UK, with over 4,800 people and 500 people with Viral Hepatitis attending for care attending for care. Those requiring in-patient care are admitted to the adjacent University College London Hospital (UCLH) site under the care of the Infectious Diseases Team with liaison support from CNWL staff. Mortimer Market Centre is also one of the largest Sexual Health services in the country with more than 40,000 attendances per year. Most people attending the service self-refer, whilst others are referred by primary care, The UCLH Emergency Department and other medical specialties.

descriptionHtml:

title: Salaried GP (Upper Gordon Road Surgery)
descriptionHtml:
We have an exciting opportunity for a Salaried GP to join our friendly and supportive clinical team at our long established practice in Camberley that is part of the Surrey Heath PCN and Federation

The Salaried GP will provide high-quality primary care services to patients registered with the practice, including temporary patients. The role involves delivering clinical care, participating in practice meetings, and contributing to the overall functioning and development of the practice.The Salaried GP will work collaboratively with the practice team to manage a caseload and deal with a wide range of health needs in a primary care setting ensuring the highest standards of safe, effective, patient-centred care for all registered and temporary patients.

We are a proud training practice owned by a successful GP Federation and Linked PCN, with lots of opportunity for professional growth

We are offering up to 14 sessions per week

Some of the benefits of working with us include:

  • Indemnity cover funded
  • Opportunity to develop areas of special interest
  • Opportunity for portfolio working - provider of community clinics for Dermatology and join injections, plus locally commissioned services
  • Total Triage appointments system
  • Managed DocMan service to minimum the document burden on GPs
  • BMA compliant contracts

To apply please send a copy of your CV to HR via:shcp.hrenquiries@nhs.net

  • In accordance with the practice timetable, as agreed, the post-holder will make themselves available to undertake a variety of duties, including surgery consultations, telephone consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork and correspondence in a timely fashion Including reviewing and actioning lad reports, managing Docman and other clinical correspondence.
  • Providing high-quality clinical care to patients, including consultations, history taking, examination, diagnosis, treatment and follow up. Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems
  • Managing a range of acute and chronic medical conditions providing appropriate care and advice. Assessing the healthcare needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems
  • Recording clear and contemporaneous consultation notes to agreed standard and using agreed clinical systems
  • Collecting data for audit purposes

  • Working sessions covering 8:00 to 20:00 Monday to Friday, Saturdays 9:00 to 17:00, as part of a rota, including working as 'Duty Doctor'

About us:

We are Surrey Heath Community Providers Limited, which is a federation of 7 GP practices across 10 sites, covering a population of over 104,000 patients across Surrey Heath. We began in 2016 and now employ around 200 members of staff across our head office sites, and our primary care and unplanned care services. Our services include Surrey Heath Primary Care Network, PRIMACY workflow management and Upper Gordon Road Surgery.

As a GP Federation, we are proud to represent our member practices and to champion primary care by working with local general practice and system partners in the provision of community-based healthcare services. We are dedicated to providing safe and compassionate care to our patients across our range of primary care and unplanned healthcare services in Surrey Heath, and believe in continuous commitment to quality service delivery and positive patient outcomes.

Patients are at the heart of everything we do, and we pride ourselves in ensuring our patients feel safe, supported, communicated with and respected, at a time when they may be feeling vulnerable. Our vision is to provide high quality, seamless health care that enables people to lead healthier lives, whilst feeling supported and cared for.

Please note that due to the high number of applications we receive we are only able to contract candidates for shortlisting. If you do not receive a response within two weeks of the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful.

title: GP Training Programme Director (London - Lewisham)
descriptionHtml:
GP Programme Directors are responsible for providing education in a safe environment for doctors wanting to become GPs. This involves planning, facilitating and evaluating the process of learning. There will be support from the other Programme Directors.

1 FTC opportunity for an London (Lewisham) GP Training Programme Director has become available with a view to starting ASAP , currently lasting until 31st March 2027.

VTS half day release is Tuesday afternoon from 1pm.

If you have questions about the role, please contact the following:

AD for Lewisham: selvaseelan.selvarajah@nhs.net

The posts will be for 2 sessions a week (8 hours per week)

Proposed interview date (subject to change): 8th December 2026

The role of the GP Training Programme Director is to work with and support the Head of School in leading the delivery of a wide range of functions, aligned to the NHS England mandate.

The role will include, amongst other responsibilities, overseeing the GP School programme management and advise the Head of School on the following matters:

  • Specialty-specific matters and trainee/trainer concerns.
  • Recruitment to training posts and programmes.

To use our educational resources to support learners within programmes to fulfil their full potential.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

Applications are invited from Specialist Registered Consultants or those that are in the process of obtaining your CCT/ CESR within six months of interview.

employer: Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Bolton CMHT
descriptionHtml:
Recruitment Premia is made available for consultant psychiatry posts in community mental health teams. The recruitment premia for this post is up to £40,000 over 3 years. Premia is intended to attract new candidates to the Trust and therefore will not normally be available to applicants who are currently substantively employed by the Trusts in Greater Manchester and is subject to eligibility criteria and organisational approval. Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust is seeking a Consultant Psychiatrist to join our multidisciplinary Community Mental Health Team at Bolton. Bolton Community mental health teams (CMHTs) provide multi-disciplinary assessment, treatment, and care of individuals with severe and enduring mental health problems. They service is available to residents of Bolton, aged 16 to 70 years, with a diagnosed functional mental health problem.

The postholder will carry out comprehensive psychiatric assessment, provide treatment for inpatients on the ward and support ward-based staff to manage psychiatric emergencies. The postholder will lead clinical decision making in the multidisciplinary team to ensure the delivery of high quality care and engage with service transformation programmes including attendance at consultant meetings/peer review for their service and directorate.

o Provide Medical leadership for MDT meetings.o Carry out comprehensive psychiatric Assessment and provide treatment for inpatients on the ward.o Support ward-based staff to manage psychiatric emergencieso Conduct patient reviews and lead Multidisciplinary ward reviews, CPA reviews and multi-professional meetings.o Be the responsible clinician for the purposes of the Mental Health Act 1983(amended 2007) and carry out duties in accordance to the code of practice.o Renew and maintain Responsible Clinician status according to agreed procedures.o Carry out comprehensive Risk Assessments and participate in Trust's risk management processes.o Provide medical leadership to the inpatient ward team.o Maintain a high level of effective communication and work flexibly and cooperatively with other parts of the service including other wards and inpatient units, community mental health teams, services and primary careo Liaison with Families and Carerso Complete reports for Mental Health Tribunals with the support of the Staff Grade doctoro Attend Mental Health Tribunals or supervise other members of the medical teams in Tribunal work Assess for use of the Mental Health Act, complete consent to treatment and authorise Section 17 leave.

employer: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust
title: Clinical Fellow General Surgery
descriptionHtml:
Ready to take the next step in your surgical career? Join University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust (UHL) as a Junior Clinical Fellow in General Surgery at Trust Grade F2/CT1 level, depending on your experience.

Build your confidence, broaden your clinical experience and develop your surgical skills in a teaching hospital environment. Working alongside experienced clinicians and multidisciplinary teams, you will make a meaningful contribution to the care of elective and emergency surgical patients, with appropriate senior supervision.

Gain hands-on experience through ward-based care and the emergency surgical on-call rota, with participation in theatre activities and outpatient clinics suited to your experience and competence. Cross-site working across Leicester Royal Infirmary, Leicester General Hospital and Glenfield Hospital will broaden your experience of surgical care.

We are looking for an enthusiastic, motivated doctor who communicates well, enjoys working as part of a team and brings a flexible, compassionate approach to patient care.

Provide safe, effective and compassionate care for General Surgery inpatients, joining consultant-led and registrar-led ward rounds.

Assess, investigate and manage acute surgical conditions under senior supervision, and take part in the emergency surgical on-call rota.

Contribute to preoperative assessment, perioperative care and postoperative management of elective and emergency patients.

Assist in theatre and attend outpatient clinics within your experience and competence.

Recognise deteriorating patients, start appropriate management and promptly escalate concerns to the registrar or consultant.

Work with nursing staff, medical colleagues and the multidisciplinary team to coordinate patient-centred care, communicating clearly with patients and relatives.

Maintain accurate, timely clinical records, discharge summaries and correspondence.

Participate in quality improvement, service development and clinical audit, and show an interest in research and critical appraisal.

Follow Trust policies, clinical guidelines and governance processes, keep statutory and mandatory training up to date, and fulfil safeguarding responsibilities.

Promote dignity, respect and inclusion in patient care and working relationships.

Provide clinical support and guidance to colleagues within the limits of your competence, helping teams deliver coordinated care and develop their skills.

Our new strategy, developed with the support and feedback of colleagues, patients, and partners, is our compass for the next seven years (2023-2030).

We have four primary goals:

  • high-quality care for all,
  • being a great place to work,
  • partnerships for impact, and
  • research and education excellence

And we will embed health equality in all we do - taking active steps to reduce the avoidable differences in healthcare that some people face, working in partnership with communities.

Our strategy is underpinned by new values and we will work to ensure they are an everyday reality for all:

  • we are compassionate,
  • we are proud,
  • we are inclusive, and
  • we are one team

This is an exciting moment as we look to the future with clarity on what we already do well and where we need to focus our energies to make an even bigger difference for the people we serve.

About the University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust:

https://www.uhleicester.nhs.uk

descriptionHtml:

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Complex Trauma & Limb Reconstruction Fellow Post CCT 2028
descriptionHtml:

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team
descriptionHtml:
