employer: North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust
title: Deputy Medical Director - Quality and Governance
descriptionHtml:
The Deputy Medical Director for Clinical Quality & Governance (DMD-QG) provides strategic clinical leadership to ensure that care across all physical, community, and virtual settings is safe, effective, and shaped directly by the voices of patients.

As a key member of the Chief Medical Officer's senior team, the post holder bridges corporate safety assurance and front-line clinical practice, ensuring that the Trust systematically transitions from a culture of compliance to a proactive, continuous culture of learning and improvement.

The DMD-QG will support the Chief Medical Officer with the integration of clinical services and processes across the Trust and a vital role in leading quality governance across health and care boundaries as the Trust expands its neighbourhood models, introduces specialised elective facilities, and integrates systems within the wider Integrated Care Board (ICB).

The DMD-QG will provide medical leadership to the Clinical Risk Manager for serious incidents/matters relating to PSIRF and inquests.

Key Strategic Responsibilities
  • Clinical Governance & Patient Safety Leadership: Champion the Trust-wide integration of the Patient Safety Incident Response Framework (PSIRF), while providing senior clinical oversight for complex professional standards (MHPS) and high-profile incident investigations.
  • Regulatory Excellence & Compliance: Lead institutional readiness programs for Care Quality Commission (CQC) inspections to systematically improve and maintain quality ratings across all registered and virtual Trust domains.
  • Modern Service Frameworks (MSFs): Direct the Trust-wide adoption of national MSFs, utilizing clinical data, mortality metrics, and peer benchmarking to eliminate unwarranted variation in high-volume, high-risk clinical pathways.
  • Data Transparency & Accessibility: Drive corporate transparency by transforming complex safety and mortality data into accessible, front-line dashboards that empower clinical teams and ensure public accountability.
  • Patient-Centric Co-Production: Oversee the structural evolution of the Patient & Public Voice Partnership, structurally shifting patient engagement from reactive feedback into systematic service co-design alongside patients and families.
  • Executive Deputising & Strategic Representation: Actively partner with and deputise for the Chief Medical Officer, maintaining a senior, non-clinical medical presence on-site, chairing pivotal safety and mortality committees, and acting as Medical Co-ordinator during Major Incidents.

North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust is a large, complex organisation serving a diverse population across multiple sites. We are committed to delivering high quality, safe and effective care, with a strong focus on continuous improvement and clinical leadership.

You will be joining a supportive and collaborative senior leadership community, working closely with clinical and corporate colleagues to address key priorities and challenges. This role offers a unique opportunity to make a rapid, visible difference at a critical time,improving care, strengthening standards, and embedding a positive, accountable culture.

title: Haematology Specialty Doctor
descriptionHtml:
This is a full-time substantive post as Specialty Doctor in the Haematology Department at Southmead Hospital.

The post holder will provide care for patients with haematological conditions, mainly General Haematology and haematological malignancies, and will contribute to liaison haematology work. The successful applicant will take part in Haematology clinics, MDT meetings, bone marrow biopsy lists, provide support to the Chemotherapy unit AND and provide laboratory haematology reporting.

This Speciality Doctor will be expected to provide day to day responsibility for patients attending the Medical Day Care unit for chemotherapy, including pre-assessment of patients, prescribing and monitoring of chemotherapy and monitoring for side effects. They will also be expected to attend approximately three outpatient clinics per week, and to attend and present patients at the local and the PAN Bristol haemato-oncology multidisciplinary team meetings. They will be required to perform and supervise/demonstrate a number of diagnostic procedures - such as bone marrow biopsies and venesection. In addition, it is expected that the postholder will have opportunities to develop their skills in an area of their own interest, which will be discussed through appraisal and the job planning review process.

In addition, they will be required to:

  • Carry out teaching duties as required and take an active part in the post graduate medical education programme and to be involved in the teaching between the medical staff and nurses and other clinical professionals.
  • The postholder will be expected to attend regular team meetings and to attend and participate in all aspects of clinical governance and to take part in departmental audit
  • Provides cover for colleagues on leave or in case of sickness including occasional participation in ward and laboratory work

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust brings together more than 28,000 staff to deliver over 160 clinical services across thirteen hospital locations,operatingfrom three main sites at Southmead, Bristol citycentreand Weston.

With an annual turnover of £2.3 billion, we are now one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom. Our hospitals are spread across Bristol and Weston, join us and you can enjoy the very best of both worlds; city living within a stone's throw of the countryside or beside the seaside, both with easy access to all that theSouth Westhas to offer.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust values all people as individuals. As an equal opportunities employer actively working towards a diverse workforce we aim to recruit and retaina workforce whichrepresentsthe rich diversity of the local population at all levels and are committed to designing our services around the needs of individual patients and those around them. Anonymous information will be used from your applicationin order toensurewe'remeeting our pledge.

title: 4-6 session Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
The Village Surgery in Poole seeks an innovative, self-motivated GP for 4-6 sessions per week and flexibility in how these sessions are met, A GP who is keen to incorporate his or her ideas for any progressive development into the practice and be fully involved with the options to put new processes in place. We are a democratic, fair and friendly partnership with a great team ethos and can genuinely offer you a good work/life balance.

We welcome applications from either established or newly qualified GP's.

Benefits

  • £10,500 a session, review following probation period
  • 6 weeks equivalent annual leave, plus Bank Holidays pro rata, 1 weeks pro rata CPD Leave
  • NHS Pension
  • Generous annual leave allowance
  • Modern purpose built premises

The post-holder will manage a caseload and deal with a wide range of health needs in a primary care setting, ensuring the highest standards of care for all registered and temporary patients.

Clinical Responsibilities -

In accordance with the practice timetable, as agreed, the post-holder will make him/her-self available to undertake a variety of duties including surgery/telephone consultations, on-call duties, and queries, occasional visits, generating, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork including completing medical reports as required.

Prescribing in accordance with the practice prescribing formulary (or generically) whenever this is clinically appropriate

Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems, Assessing the health care needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems

Screening patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness in consultation with patients and in line with current practice disease management protocols

Onward referrals to other care providers as appropriate

Recording clear and contemporaneous consultation notes to agreed standards

Contributing to the attainment of all quality indicators (QoF) and any local or national initiative that the practice takes part in

In general the post-holder will be expected to undertake all the normal clinical duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.

We are a friendly and supportive Practice with an excellent Primary Care Team comprising of 5 GPs (2 male and 3 female), an Advanced Nurse Practitioner, 2 Practice Nurses, 1 HCA and 16 admin/reception staff. We are located within the university and support the students of the Arts University.

The team is supported by the Partners, Practice, Deputy Practice and Reception Managers. We are part of the North Bournemouth Primary Care Network (NBPCN), and also supported by the NBPCN team members which include Pharmacists, First Contact Physios, Acute frailty visiting team, Social Prescribers, working with Dorset Mind and a Mental Health Practitioner. Supporting our Severe Mental Health patients we have a network SMI worker. Our PCN Digital Care Co-Ordinators work alongside the practices to offer support in meeting the PCN DES requirements.

Within the NBPCN we have an equal opportunity to choose the best services and outcomes for our practice population and development, when they arise, and under no pressure to consolidate.

We are proud to offer a high standard of care but are firm believers in a good work/life balance.

Established GP Training Practice supporting GP Registrars.

Excellent relations with local Pharmacies and Electronic Prescribing

High QOF and Enhanced Services achievers.

CQC Good Rating October 2025

TPP SystmOne clinical system, with use of Arden's templates.

Modern purpose-built premises

title: Consultant Psychiatrist HMP Channings wood and Exeter
descriptionHtml:
This is a new 6 PA post created in response to clinical demand and service mobilisation.

This post-holder will have his or her base at HMP Channings Wood and HMP Exeter for the allocated PAs, where the mental health service comprises full multidisciplinary teams, including mental health practitioners, Learning disability nurses, an ADHD nurse, Cognitive Change nurse, Speech and Language Therapist, and a psychology team, supported by administration and a service manager.

The post includes an interesting and varied range of clinical responsibilities for prisoners with a wide range of clinical conditions, including acute and chronic mental illness, personality disorder, brain injury, dementia and neurodiversity.

The post holder will be supported by the South West Prisons Consultant team and the Associate Clinical Director for South West Prisons, who will also act as Line Manager.

The post holder will be eligible for inclusion in the Specialist Register in Forensic Psychiatry or General Adult Psychiatry.

The primary duties of the post holder will include consultant leadership for the Mental Health In-reach Team at the prisons.

In terms of breakdown of the post:

2 PA's will be at HMP Exeter

2 PA's will be at HMP Channings Wood

The post holder will have 2 SPA allocated in their job plan for undertaking activities that support the professional role such as teaching, training, clinical management, clinical governance, service development and other relevant activities.

Provision of comprehensive psychiatric care through evaluation, diagnosis and use of appropriate treatment plans/strategies

To ensure treatment of patients in accordance with acceptable and established standards, protocols and guidelines (including NICE, Royal College of Psychiatrists and the General Medical Council

Ensuring the involvement of families and carers, wherever possible, with the patients' consent in treatment planning and care.

Providing psychiatric leadership to the multi-disciplinary teams. This includes taking a lead in clinical governance in both teams and contributing to directorate wide issues especially those related to both teams.

To liaise with other agencies as may be appropriate, especially with regard to continuity of patient care

Availability to act as Section 12(2) approved doctor for the purpose of Mental Health Act Assessments if indicated.

Identifying and advocating for needed resources including staff as necessary

Taking part in administrative/management duties within the teams, directorate and the Trust as a whole

Participating in clinical governance, clinical audit, various medical advisory committees and other committees as may be necessary

At Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust, we offer a wide range of NHS healthcare services to people living in South-East London and to people in prison across England. Our wide array of services includes community health care, such as district nursing and speech and language therapy, care for people with learning disabilities and mental health such as psychiatry, nursing and therapies.

Oxleas is a great place to work. It has been recognised as one of the Top 10 Best Places to Work 2023 by the Sunday Times amongst very big employers. Our staff survey results show that we are in the Top 5 in England and the highest in London for staff experience amongst similar trusts.

"We are always delighted to welcome new colleagues to the Oxleas family. We care about making Oxleas a great place to work - it's a big priority in our strategy. Come and join us - it's a place where our values, teamwork, equity, and wellbeing matter and where you can really help to improve people's lives."

Ify Okocha

Chief Executive

title: Consultant in Cardiology
descriptionHtml:
Consultant In Cardiology with Subspecialist Expertise in Echocardiography (10 PAs Per Week)

Based Between University College London Hospitals (UCLH) and Barts Heart Centre)

Barts Health NHS Trust invites applications to join the Cardiology teams at UCLH and the Bars Heart Centre as a Consultant Cardiologist with specific expertise in echocardiography and potentially also additional cardiac imaging.

This 10 PA appointment is principally based at UCLH (4 days per week) and the appointee will co-lead the development of this already busy clinical service. We are looking to start on-site stress echocardiography (exercise and dobutamine stress) and to expand our on-site TOE offering. This role will also consolidate the on-site Consultant support for our cardiac physiologist team. It will provide departmental leadership in areas such as audit, governance and quality assurance. The appointee will also assist in provision of clinical advice (particularly in relation to imaging) to our Acute Medical, ITU, Oncology and other specialist services at UCLH.

It is hoped that the successful appointee will also contribute to and extend the current research activities of the department.

There will also be involvement in General Cardiology Outpatient Clinics at UCLH (average of 1 clinic per week) and the UCLH Cardiology inpatient/ED/SDEC liaison service (1 week per month, weekdays). Additionally, there is a small on-call commitment (6 weekends per year, providing daytime-only ward rounds and referral reviews).

There is also one weekly clinical session at Barts Heart Centre (the details of which will be guided by the successful appointee's specific interests) plus the opportunity for participation in several specialist cardiac MDT meetings run from Barts e.g. general valve MDT, TAVI MDT, endocarditis MDT etc

Barts Health is one of the largest NHS trusts in the country, and one of Britain's leading healthcare providers.

Our vision is to be a high-performing group of NHS hospitals, renowned for excellence and innovation, and providing safe and compassionate care to our patients in east London and beyond. That means being a provider of excellent patient safety, known for delivering consistently high standards of harm-free care and always caring for patients in the right place at the right time. It also means being an outstanding place to work, in which our WeCare values and behaviours are visible to all and guide us in how we work together.

We strive to live by our WeCare values and are committed to promoting inclusion, where every staff member has a sense of belonging. We value our differences and fully advocate, cultivate and support an inclusive working environment.

It is expected that candidates will be fully trained in general cardiology and show expertise in their subspecialty commensurate with a leadership role at UCLH. Applicants should possess the MRCP or equivalent, be GMC-registered with a license to practice, and be on the specialist register for cardiology or within six months of specialist registration. Candidates with an interest in clinical research relevant to echocardiography and imaging are particularly encouraged to apply

title: Consultant in Luminal Gastroenterology & GIM
descriptionHtml:
Substantive Consultant in Luminal Gastroenterology and General Internal Medicine

Please note: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust is recruiting to two Consultant Gastroenterology vacancies:

1. Consultant Gastroenterologist and Hepatologist post based primarily at Southmead Hospital.

2. Consultant Gastroenterologist post based primarily at the Bristol Royal Infirmary/City site.

While each post has a designated base, there may be opportunities for cross-site working across Bristol NHS Foundation Trust in the future.

A separate advertisement and Job Description are available for the Southmead site Consultant Gastroenterologist post. Applications to either vacancy will be considered through a joint shortlisting and interview process. Candidates wishing to be considered for only one post should clearly state this within their application; otherwise, they will be considered for both vacancies where appropriate.

This is a substantive appointment for a Consultant in Luminal Gastroenterology and General Internal Medicine. The successful applicant will join a team of 7 Luminal Gastroenterologists and 6 Hepatologists and will be based at the Bristol Royal Infirmary.

Accreditation in Gastroenterology and General Internal Medicine is required, although applicants within 12 months of obtaining CCT are also encouraged to apply.

The Bristol Royal Infirmary provides a regional TPN service, and the successful applicant will be expected to deliver care to patients with complex inflammatory bowel disease and intestinal failure. We also provide a regional Bowel Cancer Screening service and work closely with colleagues in Colorectal, Upper GI and HPB Surgery, as well as the regional Oncology Service. We undertake joint transition clinics with our colleagues in Paediatrics, who provide the regional paediatric gastroenterology service. There is a therapeutic endoscopy service with regular propofol-sedated lists, ERCP, EUS and SpyGlass. We have an excellent GI Physiology service and are supported by an experienced team of IBD and Nutrition ACPs and CNSs. Sub-specialty interests in any area of Luminal Gastroenterology are encouraged, and there are active research programmes with strong links to the University of Bristol and the University of the West of England.The post requires independent upper and lower GI endoscopy, luminal outpatient clinics, and inpatient responsibility for the luminal gastroenterology ward on a 1:5 rotational basis. The post includes a commitment to the emergency endoscopy rota (1 in 9), plus approximately 5 weekday GIM on-call shifts per annum. We deliver elective work at South Bristol Community Hospital and Weston General Hospital, and the successful applicant will share these responsibilities as appropriate.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Experienced General Practitioner (4 Sessions)

Salary: £13,000 per session per annum

Contract: Salaried GP

Sessions: 4 sessions per week

Required days: Monday (essential) + flexibility for remaining sessions

On-call: Weekly on-call commitment

Experience: Minimum 5 years post-CCT

We are seeking an experienced GP (minimum 5 years post-CCT) to join our team for 4 sessions per week. This role is ideal for a confident, clinically strong GP who is comfortable managing complexity and contributing to a large, dynamic practice.

  • Monday availability is essential

  • Participation in the weekly on-call rota is required

  • Clinical sessions include a mix of booked appointments and triage

  • Strong clinical and administrative support provided

  • Opportunity to contribute to service development depending on interests

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary of £13,000 per session

  • Stable, supportive partnership and management team

  • Well-organised systems with a focus on workload management

  • Excellent MDT support to reduce GP pressure

  • Opportunities for teaching, portfolio roles or leadership interests if desired

  • Friendly, inclusive team culture with regular clinical meetings

The post-holder will provide high-quality general medical services to the practice population and work collaboratively as part of the wider clinical team.

Key duties include:

  • Undertaking clinical sessions comprising a mix of booked appointments and triage

  • Participation in theweekly on-call rota

  • Providing safe, effective and evidence-based patient care

  • Managing acute and chronic conditions, including patients with complex needs

  • Reviewing clinical correspondence, results and actioning tasks in a timely manner

  • Contributing to practice clinical meetings and learning activities

  • Working closely with the multidisciplinary team to support continuity of care

  • Supporting training and supervision as appropriate to experience

  • Adhering to practice policies, NHS contractual requirements and GMC guidance

Eltham Medical Practice is a large, well-established GP practice serving approximately 26,500 patients. We are rated Good by the CQC and are committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care within a supportive and collaborative working environment.

We are a training practice with a strong multidisciplinary team including GP trainees, medical students, advanced clinical practitioners, pharmacists, first contact physiotherapists, care coordinators and an experienced management and administrative team. We place a strong emphasis on innovation, efficiency and sustainable general practice, while maintaining a friendly and inclusive team culture.

employer: Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Working Part time: 5 Sessions per week

Salaried GP with a number of combinations of sessions offered.

The division has the pleasure in offering an innovative and fresh opportunity for a salaried GP to join the Hospital at Home service supporting people with medical interventions at their own home.

As pressure on emergency departments across the UK grows, new care models will be pivotal in delivering and relieving some of these pressures by diverting work away from the hospital and into the community.

This is an exciting opportunity to work collaboratively with other multi-disciplinary teams within primary and secondary care and to expand your portfolio and leadership skills in evolving primary care roles.

Hospital at Home (Clinical sessions-negotiable)Our Hospital at Home service is designed to provide monitoring and treatment at home, which has traditionally been provided in hospital, such as intravenous (IV) therapy. The service encompasses Virtual Wards, Urgent Community Response (UCR) and IV OPAT service. The post holder will be required to undertake medical management including clinical assessment ensuring safe management of patients within the Community setting. Working closely with primary and secondary care colleagues to ensure safe and effective clinical care is delivered to support admission avoidance and facilitate early discharge where clinically appropriate.

1. Manage the medical requirements and provide medical oversight to patients being cared for by the intermediate care service (Hospital At Home).

2. Respond to medical problems presented by patients, including history taking, examination, investigation, diagnosis, treatment and referral to other agencies where appropriate.

4. Develop, monitor and adjust clinical management plans for health in consultation with patients and other team members and in line with current pathways and protocols

5. Liaise with secondary care consultants in the management of patients within the intermediate care pathways.

6. Undertake and order appropriate clinical diagnostic testing including arterial blood gas analysis, Xrays and blood tests.

7. Be competent in arterial blood gas interpretation and ECG interpretation.

9. Assist in developing appropriate pathways for people in intermediate care settings and for people being cared for by the team to avoid unnecessary hospital admission.

10. Assist in developing appropriate pathways for people in secondary care setting to facilitate safe early discharge into intermediate care service.

11. In accordance with the service rota as agreed, the post-holder will undertake clinical sessions including, telephone advice and visiting patients at home. Required shifts are weekdays and there is an expectation to join the GP on-call rota at the weekend.

The Trust's services are provided from three locations: o The Countess of Chester Hospital: providing 473 general and acute beds. o Ellesmere Port Hospital: providing 60 beds as a rehabilitation, intermediate and outpatient facility. o Tarporley War Memorial Hospital: a base for community services which serve the local rural population. The Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust employs 5,964 staff (headcount) to provide care and treatment to a population of over 400,000 people living in Chester and West Cheshire which includes Ellesmere Port and Neston as well as the Deeside area of Flintshire. The Trust works collaboratively within the wider Cheshire and Merseyside Integrated Care System. Due to its location on the border with North Wales, the Trust also works closely with the Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board. The Trust treats patients from England and some parts of Wales. During 2024/2025, there were approximately 643,000 patient attendances (inpatient, A&E, outpatient and diagnostic) ranging from a simple outpatient appointment to major cancer surgery

employer: Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialty Doctor in General Surgery
descriptionHtml:
10 PA's per week (plus adjustments for on-call)

The General Surgical department at Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust provides a variety of services across the Trust sites including General Surgery, Upper GI surgery, and Colorectal Surgery.

An opportunity exists for an enthusiastic surgeon with at least 12 months uk experience seeking an opportunity to join the General Surgical, Upper GI and Colorectal Surgical team for a fixed term appointment. This post does include an on-call commitment.

The department serves a population of 210,000 for General Surgery, comprising of list cases, endoscopy sessions, emergencies and outpatient clinics.

The department is extremely busy and the person appointed will take part in regular operating and outpatient sessions as well as having ward duties.

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

Together we employ nearly 20,000 staff. Our five main hospital sites are Diana, Princess of Wales Hospital, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole and District Hospital, for NLAG and Hull Royal Infirmary and Castle Hill Hospital for HUTH.

As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

employer: South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
This post is to provide consultant psychiatry input for the Service for Complex Autism and Associated Neurodevelopmental Diagnoses (SCAAND). SCAANDprovidesspecialist assessments and evidence-based treatments for children and young people with autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disabilityand neurodevelopmental conditions, especially those with mental health needs and other co-occurring conditions. Children and young people referred to the service may also have associated genetic conditions, sensory impairments, physical impairments or other additional needs. SCAAND includes a pathway for young people with Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS). The successful applicant will work closely with the existing Consultant Child Psychiatrists and the other disciplines withinSCAAND andmay hold roles in other pathways.

This is an established post. The vacancy has arisen following retirement of the post-holder and is offered as 10 PAs.

The appointed Consultant Psychiatrist will join the existing MDT and is expected to lead in assessment and management plans. Consultants are expected to be providing clinical service leadership within their senior role in the MDT and support areas of clinical governance and management.

Theteamworks in close collaboration with the Autism and Intellectual Disabilities Intensive Intervention Team (AID-IIT) and Orchids (an intensive intervention team for children under 13), based together in National and Specialist (N&S)Outpatient CAMHS within South London and Maudsley (SLAM) NHS Trust. The team benefits from joint working and sharing ofexpertisewith colleagues within wider N&S CAMHS.

The post holder will provide consultation but also (as described above) work directly with children, adolescents and their families using specialist knowledge and expertise; they will prepare timely consultation, assessment and review reports and maintain and ensure high service standards for safeguarding, adherence to relevant legislation (including Mental Health Act, Children's Act & Mental Capacity Act) and progressive clinical practice.

Quality improvement projects and client experience data collection are vital aspects of day-to-day work, which the post holder will be expected to play a major role in undertaking and encouraging other service clinicians to do likewise.

Working for the Trust

There are excellent opportunities for professional development including management, training, research, and audit experience.

Benefits

We are committed to ensuring our staff get the most out of their benefits package and understand the importance of a healthy work life balance. There is an extensive range of excellent benefits for you and your family. It's important to us that you are valued and appreciated and that is why we have a comprehensive benefits package on offer.

Some of our benefits are highlighted here:

Generous pay, pensions and leave.We offer a comprehensive pay, pensions and leave package which is dependent on the role and length of service.

Work life balance.We support a range of flexible working options, such as: part-time working and job sharing.

Career development.There are plenty of opportunities to progress your career and we support your development through a number of programmes such as mentoring, coaching, positive people management, collective leadership and other talent programmes.

Car lease.Our staff benefit from competitive deals to lease cars.

Our staff benefit fromkeyworker housing, which is available on selected sites.

NHS discounts.With discounts of up to 10% from a variety of well-known retail brands through the Health Service Discounts website.

Other benefits include:

Counselling services

Wellbeing events

Long service awards

Cycle to work scheme

Season ticket loan

Childcare vouchers

Staff restaurants

title: Support Worker
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a confident Care & Support Worker with a passion for delivering outstanding healthcare.

You'll be working full time 42 hours a week, 12 hour shifts, including alternate weekends (four shifts week one, three shifts week two, on a two week rolling rota), days only, making a positive difference to the lives of the people in our care at Hawkstone.

Hawkstone is a specialist residential service in Bradford, West Yorkshire, supporting people with learning disabilities, complex needs and behaviours that may challenge.

We encourage and enable the people we support to lead a full and happy life. We work with them to ensure they have more choice and control in their lives. We find out their strengths, abilities and preferences so that the care provided can be as person-centred and meaningful to each individual as possible.

At Cygnet, our perks go way beyond pension schemes and excellent professional development - you'll also enjoy discounts with our free NHS blue light card, perkbox with vouchers for everyday purchases and shopping, private health cash plans, free confidential mental health support and much more, to support your wellbeing in and out of work.

An unpaid carer? We recognise that many of our colleagues have unpaid caring responsibilities and we welcome applications from unpaid carers. We value the skills and experience that caring can bring to the workplace.

Your day-to-day...

  • Offer enhanced care with a flexible learning approach for all the people in our care
  • Provide guidance & encouragement through physical & emotional support
  • Learn about individuals specific needs & provide help in the most appropriate way
  • Assist with and report on medical & welfare needs
  • Safeguard
  • Maintain a safe, clean environment for all
  • Supporting service users to access the community, to attend things like work, college, hobbies & activities, days out & holidays
  • Supporting the service users to grow, develop & learn through engaging them in tasks such as cooking & cleaning

Cygnet has been providing a national network of high-quality specialist mental health services for more than 30 years. In this role you'll have the chance to make a real impact on patients, service users & their families.

employer: University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust
title: ENT Locum Consultant
descriptionHtml:
This is an excellent opportunity to work within a forward-thinking organisation serving the communities of Bournemouth, Poole and Dorset while helping to maintain and develop a high-performing ENT service. We are looking for a 12month fixed term Locum for our thriving ENT department. You will join 7 other consultant colleagues to deliver high quality care for our patients.The Consultant in ENT will provide comprehensive specialist care for patients with disorders of the ear, nose, throat, head and neck. The post holder will undertake outpatient clinics, diagnostic assessment, elective and emergency surgical procedures, and multidisciplinary management of conditions. Responsibilities include contributing to on-call services, supervising and training junior medical staff and allied healthcare professionals, participating in clinical governance, quality improvement, audit and research activities, and supporting the delivery of safe, effective, and patient-centred care. The successful candidate will work collaboratively with colleagues across the wider multidisciplinary team to develop services and achieve excellent clinical outcomes for patient

UHD are investing, developing and transforming Trust services in line with the New Hospital Programme. As part of this, some services may move site this year or next, either temporarily or permanently. Recruiting Managers will be happy to answer any service-specific questions at interview.

This service has a planned move from Poolesite to Bournemouthsite 2027.

If a role or service relocates as part of a planned move, excess mileage will not be reimbursed. Travel from home to the new work base will be classed as a normal commute. Any other changes will be managed under Trust or national terms and conditions.

UHD has active networks including Women's, BAME, Pride, EU, Pro Ability, and Armed Forces. We support Disability Confident and Armed Forces Covenant interview schemes.

AI tools may be used, but applications must honestly reflect your own skills and experience. Integrity is key to our recruitment process.

title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Needham Market Country Practice is seeking a motivated, enthusiastic, and patient-focused GP to join our friendly and supportive team as a Salaried GP for up to 8 sessions per week.

This is an excellent opportunity to become part of a well-established, forward-thinking practice that is committed to providing high-quality care to our local community while supporting a healthy work-life balance for our staff.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Salaried GP for 4-8 sessions per week.

We are a friendly, forward thinking city centre practice (approx. 13,500 patients) with a mixed and varied patient population. We are 'college doctors' to eight of the Oxford colleges.

The successful applicant will be an enthusiastic and committed GP and join our well organised practice, working in a multi-professional team whilst gaining valuable skills in a supportive and professional environment.

We are a teaching and training practice, with excellent feedback from all of our learners. We have medical students from the University of Oxford and we are actively involved in research as an NIHR approved research practice.

We are based in the heart of Oxford in a brand-new, purpose-built premises with our neighbouring practice of KES@Northgate. We have expanded practice services following our merger of 27 and 28 Beaumont Street practices.

We have strong relationships with the other three practices in our PCN (Oxford Central PCN) and work collaboratively alongside each other. We are building our team of health care professionals within the PCN.

We offer a competitive salary / partnership drawings, NHS pension, medical defence fees plus a generous leave allowance.

For further details or to arrange an informal visit please contact Dr Matthew Easdale, GP Partner.

To apply please send your CV and covering letter detailing your interest and suitability for the role to bobicb-ox.nhc.manager@nhs.net

Website

https://www.northgatehealthcentre.co.uk/

We are a supportive team of 4 GP Partners and 7 Salaried GPs with a strong & expanding nursing team, 3 experienced paramedic practitioners and a pharmacist. We are well supported by our friendly and efficient patient advisory, administration and management teams. We are high performers through QoF and other enhanced services. We have excellent patient feedback.

employer: North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locally Employed Doctor - FY2 Acute Medicine *Internal Only*
descriptionHtml:
INTERNAL ONLY TO NORTH CUMBRIA INTEGRATED CARE NHS FOUNDATION TRUST (NCIC) EMPLOYEES ONLY

We are looking to flexibly employ 1WTE Trust Grade Doctor (FY2) to work in the department of Acute Medicine, covering our Acute Medicine Unit and Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) services as part of our Foundation Year roster.

This appointment is for 12 months, with opportunities to extend.

This role is intended to replace an existing member of the team who is leaving and so will join within their roster line on the current 1:10 rota pattern.

The post-holder will work closely with the Consultant, Nurse in Charge and all other staff while on Acute Medical Unit working on the on-call rota.

This is an exciting time to join our Acute Medicine team as we see increased number of admissions through the Acute Medical unit, combined with an increase in the numbers of patients attending the Same Day Emergency Care service. We see a wide variety of acutely unwell patients within our services and this clinical role is essential to supporting safe, effective and high quality care.

The successful applicant will work as part of our medical workforce which is comprised of locally employed Doctors, Doctors in Training via the Lead Employer Trust and rotational/training posts.

Please see job specification for more information.

At NCIC, we have an ambition to deliver outstanding healthcare services to the population of North Cumbria. The Trust is committed to creating a centre of excellence in providing rural and remote healthcare and provides a wide range of community and acute services throughout our county.

Our 5 key principles demonstrate our belief in the delivery of 'safe, high quality care every time':

  • Being a clinically led organisation
  • Quality and safety at the heart of our Trust
  • A positive patient experience every time
  • A great place to work
  • Managing our money well

As an organisation we are serious about supporting a diverse workforce that reflects our local community and are very much focused on being an inclusive and compassionate place to work.

Across the North East and North Cumbria we are working together to deliver our ambition to be the greenest region in England by 2030. All staff are expected to support sustainability.

title: Senior Clinical Fellow - General Internal Medicine
descriptionHtml:
We are currently recruiting into Trust Grade Senior Clinical Fellow posts covering a range of specialties including General Medicine, Gastroenterology, Stroke Medicine and Elderly Care. The posts will cover a variety of General Internal Medicine specialities with a view to doing 4 month rotations between these areas.

For a full breakdown on each ward please see Job Description.

Medical assessment and rehabilitation are the core services provided by the Medicine for the Older Persons team. Rapid multidisciplinary assessment and intervention is performed on our new Acute Frailty Unit (AFU) (Durrington ward - 24 bed short stay elderly care ward with direct streaming from the Medical Assessment Unit), with Spire (30 beds) and Imber (24 beds) wards, acting as acute downstream wards focused on acute care and rehabilitation.Spire ward includes therapeutic areas including a "Memory Caf" as well as an enclosed garden area, as well as providing care for patients with infectious diseases due to its many side rooms.

The orthogeriatric service has been established since 2011 to provide pro-active care to all hip fracture patients and those elective and trauma patients aged 75 and older. The orthogeriatric service has consistently performed well in the National Hip Fracture Audit and Blue Book standards.

Outpatient opportunities exist in the Nunton Unit, where Rapid Access clinics, Parkinson's clinics, TIA and falls clinics and general Elderly clinics are held.

It is our intention to create rotational posts between these clinical areas, with placement opportunities including Respiratory Medicine, Endocrinology and Cardiology, so that all Trust Grade doctors have an opportunity to experience this range of in-patient services. We support educational supervision of all our trainees and would be happy to encourage / support CESR training in post.

Salisbury NHS Foundation Trust (SFT) is an innovative hospital with a proud heritage and over 250 years of experience behind us. Here we're driven to deliver an outstanding experience for everyone and have been well regarded for the quality of care and treatment we continue to provide for our patients and also our staff.

We are an acute Trust, rated "Good" by the CQC, with a track record of high performance providing regional and super regional specialist services such as: Burns, Plastics & Reconstructive Surgery, Wessex Regional Genetics Laboratory, Wessex Rehabilitation, Spires Cleft Centre and the Duke of Cornwall Spinal Treatment Centre. We have about 470 beds and employ over 4000 staff.

We support flexible working and will consider requests taking into account the needs of the service. We think working here is pretty rewarding. You can access a range of NHS discounts, receive a minimum of 35 days paid holiday (pro rata), and we offer a generous pension scheme. On-site benefits include car parking (fee applies), leisure centre, day nursery and holiday play scheme.

Salisbury is an attractive place to live and work and really gives you the best of everything. With easy access to London and local airports, the city of Southampton is only a short train or car journey away or if you prefer the sea, Bournemouth is also accessible. Don't just take our word for it, why not explore what Salisbury has to offer by visitingwww.experiencesalisbury.co.uk

employer: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant Paediatric Urologist Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
The Paediatric Surgical Service is part of the Family Services Care Group and is based at Hull Royal Infirmary, with services largely delivered within the Women's and Children's Hospital. The service provides general and specialist paediatric surgery, including paediatric urology, colorectal, gastrointestinal and neonatal surgery, working closely with paediatrics, neonatology, anaesthetics, radiology and emergency care. Services include outpatient clinics, day-case and inpatient operating lists and emergency surgical care.The locum will work alongside the existing consultant paediatric surgical team to maintain safe and timely surgical provision during a four-month period of locum cover. Theresa Bowen's correspondence of 29 October 2026 identifies Anna Radford and Marcin Kazmierski as the two consultants providing the urology service. Staffing, governance arrangements and operational details should be confirmed by the Clinical Lead before publication.

The postholder will assess and manage children and young people with paediatric urological conditions within their competencies; provide specialist advice to colleagues; contribute to multidisciplinary discussion and coordinated care with relevant paediatric, neonatal, anaesthetic and diagnostic specialties; and support effective communication with children, families and referring clinicians. They will maintain appropriate safeguarding practice, clinical governance, audit and incident reporting, and contribute to supervision and teaching of junior medical and multidisciplinary colleagues where appropriate.The successful applicant must be able to demonstrate relevant paediatric surgical experience and appropriate paediatric urology expertise to support the identified service need. The exact urology case mix, operative commitments and level of emergency/on-call participation will be agreed with the Clinical Lead.

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

Together we employ nearly 20,000 staff. Our five main hospital sites are Diana, Princess of Wales Hospital, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole and District Hospital, for NLAG and Hull Royal Infirmary and Castle Hill Hospital for HUTH.

As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

employer: Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Acute/General Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The Division of Medicine is looking to fill a vacancy within Acute/General Medicine in order to increase the consultant capacity within the acute medical team. It is full time based on a 10 PA contract, although less than full-time would be considered. A 'special' interest (as defined by theAcute Internal Medicine curriculum or dual CCT) will be considered.

The Trust is based on two Acute sites with Acute Medical services on each site. The Acute Stroke unit is based at Calderdale Hospital along with specialist Cardiology and Respiratory wards and the specialist Gastroenterology and Oncology/Haematology wards are based at Huddersfield with specialist Frailty and Care of the Elderly services.

The successful applicant will form part of our Acute Medical Consultant team, providing Acute services across the two Trust sites, Successful candidates will be expected to cover our two Acute Floors, Short Stay/outlying wards, Medical Same Day Emergency Care (MSDEC) unit and EDs (Admission Avoidance).

Applicants must be on the General Medical Council Specialist Register. In accordance with the regulations, all other categories of doctors must be on the GMC Specialist Register to be considered for a consultant appointment by the Advisory Appointments Committee. Applicants must continue to hold a License to Practice.

Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust are proud providers of acute hospital services, where we value our staff and recognise that they are our greatest asset. CHFT is at the forefront of Digital Health utilising a number of electronic solutions to improve patient care. The CQC rated us as Good in June 2018. In their report they confirmed that; "Staff were caring and provided compassionate care. Patients were treated with dignity and respect and their privacy was respected. Patients spoke positively about the care they received".

Our Future Plans

The Department of Health and Social Care has awarded capital funding to invest in local health services at both Calderdale Royal Hospital and Huddersfield Royal Infirmary. This is a significant investment and an opportunity to enhance services for our populations in Calderdale and Huddersfield and West Yorkshire for generations to come. To find out more, please visit Our Future Plans - CHFT (cht.nhs.uk)

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a motivated and compassionate Salaried GP to join our friendly and supportive team for 2 sessions per week, on a 6 month contract (to be reviewed with a potential extension), Friday essential.

This is a fantastic opportunity to be part of a well-established, forward thinking practice that values teamwork, high quality patient care and continuous improvement.

As a Salaried GP you will provide high quality, compassionate care to a diverse patient population, including acute, chronic disease and preventative care.

You'll work as part of a multidisciplinary team to manage patient demand effectively, contribute to clinical decision making and ensure continuity of care.

The role includes a mix of face-face and telephone as well as Duty and home visits.

Friarwood Surgery is a GP Practice based in Pontefract, serving a growing list of over 13200 patients. Led by a team of dedicated GP Partners, we pride ourselves on delivering high quality, patient centred care in a supportive environment.

We use SystmOne and benefit from a strong relationship with our PCN and local healthcare providers. We are also a GP training Practice.

title: Advanced Clinical Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Shore Medical is seeking an experienced Advanced Clinical Practitioner (ACP) to join our primary care team, working across our practice sites as required.

The post holder will provide expert clinical assessment, diagnosis and treatment for both adult and paediatric patients presenting with acute and chronic conditions, working within their scope of practice and the four pillars of Advanced Practice. They will provide appropriate management, prescribing and referral where necessary, ensuring patient safety and adherence to national and local guidance.

We are looking for an experienced ACP with a background in Primary Care who is committed to delivering safe, high-quality patient care and maintaining excellent clinical standards. The successful candidate will work collaboratively with the wider multidisciplinary team, supporting clinical leadership and the delivery of effective patient-centred care across Shore Medical.

  • Provide autonomous clinical assessment, diagnosis and treatment for adult and paediatric patients with acute, chronic and undifferentiated presentations.
  • Work within the Four Pillars of Advanced Practice, NMC Code and professional scope, ensuring safe, evidence-based and high-quality care.
  • Undertake clinical decision-making, prescribing, investigations and referrals where appropriate.
  • Provide clinical leadership, supervision and support to the wider nursing and multidisciplinary team.
  • Contribute to clinical governance, audit, research and continuous professional development.

    • Shore Medical is a GP Super Partnership with 6 practices across Poole and Bournemouth. We aspire to offer exceptional care to our 58,000 patients and are innovative in our approach to developing new teams and pathways to ever improve how general practice is delivered.

    We have a friendly and supportive team of more than 200 staff, with over 40 GPs, Pharmacists, Paramedics, Nurses, Mental Health specialists and our range of administrative staff. We have a great social side to our team with Summer and Christmas parties, running and paddle boarding groups as well as many other events throughout the year.

    The Practices in the Partnership are:

    • Lilliput Surgery
    • Poole Road Medical Centre
    • Wessex Road Surgery
    • Heatherview Medical Centre
    • Fernside Surgery
    • Parkstone Tower Practice

    We offer

    • Competitive salary
    • Friendly and supportive working environment
    • Continuous CPD
    • NHS Pension Scheme with Life Insurance
    • Free parking at most of the sites
    • Cycle to work scheme
    • Refer a Friend scheme
    • Summer & Christmas parties

title: Locum Consultant - Endometriosis
descriptionHtml:
Locum Consultant in the department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology

This is a 10 PA locum appointment for a Consultant in Gynaecology at St James Hospital and Leeds General Infirmary, Leeds. The post will be available immediately for a period of 6 months.

This is a new post and has been developed to address an increase in demand for the endometriosis service. We want to encourage the successful candidate to contribute to the BSGE accredited endometriosis service, supported by the wider Obstetric and Gynaecology team, following discussion with the department.

The successful applicant should be a member of the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (MRCOG) and they should be on the GMC Specialist Register or be within 6 months of being admitted to the register for trainees if currently in a training programme within the UK, or have references which have been authorised by the Deputy Medical Director and Clinical Director.

Candidates not yet on the Specialist Register (including those awaiting CESR outcome) may be considered for appointment to Locum Consultant post, subject to demonstrated competence and appropriate governance arrangements.

Applicants should have established skills in Obstetrics and Gynaecology with ability to work within a busy tertiary unit. Excellent communication and team working skills, a strong commitment to teaching and service development are essential.This is a 10 PA Locum appointment for a Consultant Gynaecologist with a specialist interest in endometriosis. This post will deliver 10 PAs supporting the Gynaecology teams across Leeds General Infirmary and St James University Hospital.

This post has arisen as part of the expansion of Consultant staffing within the Leeds Teaching Hospitals Women's clinical services unit (CSU) and the growing demand for endometriosis provision.The Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is committed to delivering the highest quality and safest treatment and care to every patient, every time.

Our vision is to provide the highest quality specialist and integrated care.

We will do this through delivery of our multi-year goals and strategic priorities, which you can read about on this page.

Central to it all is The Leeds Way  our values and behaviours that are at the heart of everything we do.

title: Support Worker
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a confident Support Worker with a passion for delivering outstanding healthcare.

You'll be working full time 42 hours a week, 12 hour shifts (days and nights), making a positive difference to the lives of the people in our care at Cygnet Cedars.

Cygnet Cedars is a 23-bed high dependency complex care service for men with learning disabilities, associated complex needs and who may have behaviours that challenge. We accept emergency referrals and the team are experienced in managing them quickly and efficiently to ensure the transition for each individual is as smooth as possible.

At Cygnet, we support our people to grow their careers, gain new skills and keep stepping up. Apply now to enjoy excellent career prospects while reaping the rewards of making a difference to others every day.Cygnet Health Care was established in 1988. Since then we have developed a wide range of services for individuals with mental health needs, autism and learning disabilities within the UK. We have built a reputation for delivering pioneering services and outstanding outcomes for the people in our care. Our expert and highly dedicated care team of 10 000 employees empower 2864 individuals across 150 services to consistently make a positive difference to their lives, through service-user focused care and rehabilitation.
